articles.title: COP31: BNDES anuncia pacote com potencial de captar R$ 39 bilhões para projetos climáticos
articles.titleKo: COP31: BNDES anuncia pacote com potencial de captar R$ 39 bilhões para projetos climáticos
articles.originalSummary: O presidente do Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES), Aloizio Mercadante, anunciou nesta quinta-feira, 13, um pacote de R$ 13 bilhões em investimentos internacionais para o enfrentamento das mudanças climáticas. Segundo ele, a instituição fechou a maior parceria global com o Fundo do Clima da ONU (GCF, na sigla em inglês), que almejar captar até R$ 39 bilhões. O anúncio foi feito durante a 31ª Conferência das Nações Unidas sobre Mudanças CLimáticas (COP31), em Antália, na Turquia. “Todos os projetos são para descarbonização, soluções baseadas na natureza, economia sustentável e parceria público-privado”, disse Mercadante, em evento com a sociedade civil, ao lado do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. “O modelo prevê a combinação de recursos do BNDES, de organismos multilaterais e de investidores privados para formar fundos com capital-alvo definido, capazes de financiar projetos de sustentabilidade e alavancar novas operações de crédito”, acrescentou. O GFC acertou aportes em dois fundos selecionados pelo BNDES. Um deles prevê US$ 250 milhões no Catalytic Transition Fund Brazil(CTF), gerido pela Brookfield, e com capital alvo de R$ 7 bilhões. No fundo Flying Rivers Capital, o aporte será de US$ 50 milhões, com alvo a R$ 2,2 bilhões. O BNDES investirá R$ 1,1 bilhão no CTF e R$ 540 milhões na Flying Rivers. “Estamos usando poder catalítico de um banco público e da ONU para trazer investimentos privados à causa ambiental”, afirmou Mercadante. Em paralelo, o BNDES alocou R$ 870 milhões no Just Climate Brasil, gerido pela Generation Investment Management, uma gestora fundada pelo ex-vice-presidente dos Estados Unidos Al Gore. O veículo mira captar R$ 3,8 bilhões. Captação Durante a COP, o BNDES também informou que captou US$ 147 milhões (R$ 808,5 milhões) com o Banco Internacional para Reconstrução e Desenvolvimento (BIRD), ligado ao Banco Mundial, e os Fundos de Investimento no Clima (CIF) para investimentos em restauro florestal no Brasil. Do total, o Bird fica responsável por US$ 100 milhões e o CIF, por US$ 47 milhões. Na ocasião, o BNDES também assinou com representantes do Bird e do Banco Interamericano de Desenvolvimento (BID) uma carta de intenções que abre caminho para captação de US$ 1 bilhão (R$ 5,5 bilhões), voltados a investimentos em descarbonização na indústria brasileira. *Os repórteres viajaram a convite da Confederação Nacional das Seguradoras (Cnseg) e do Instituto Clima e Sociedade Com informação do Estadão de Conteúdo (André Marinho e Paula Ferreira, enviados especiais). Luke’s Lobster is introducing a limited-time Lobster Mac & Cheese at select locations beginning December 9, offering a new seasonal menu item for the holiday season. The dish, developed over two years, features wild-caught lobster mixed with ruffled mafalda pasta and a three-cheese sauce made with American, Monterey Jack, and mascarpone cheeses. It is finished with toasted breadcrumbs and priced at $18. The Lobster Mac & Cheese will be available at Luke’s Lobster locations in Balboa Island, Santa Monica, and San Francisco’s SoMa neighborhood. A traditional Mac & Cheese option without lobster will also be offered at participating restaurants for $9. Customers can also purchase packaged Luke’s Lobster Mac & Cheese at Whole Foods Market for $10.99. The limited-time offering expands Luke’s Lobster’s menu with a seafood-focused version of the classic comfort food during the holiday season. articles.title: Prejuízo da Azul cai 74,5% no terceiro trimestre e fica em R$ 164,5 milhões
articles.titleKo: Prejuízo da Azul cai 74,5% no terceiro trimestre e fica em R$ 164,5 milhões
articles.originalSummary: A Azul teve prejuízo líquido de R$ 164,5 milhões no terceiro trimestre de 2026, perda 74,5% menor em relação ao prejuízo de R$ 644,2 milhões registrado no mesmo período de 2025. A melhora veio principalmente do resultado financeiro, que ficou negativo em R$ 724,5 milhões, perda 62,2% menor que a de um ano antes, depois da reestruturação concluída pela companhia no Chapter 11 nos Estados Unidos. O Ebitda ajustado somou R$ 1,20 bilhão, recuo anual de 39,4%, e a margem Ebitda caiu de 34,6% para 21,4%. A receita líquida total foi de R$ 5,64 bilhões, 1,8% abaixo da do terceiro trimestre do ano passado. A dívida bruta encerrou setembro em R$ 22,64 bilhões, 39,3% menor que um ano antes. Os números excluem R$ 373,6 milhões em despesas que a empresa classificou como não recorrentes, ligadas à reestruturação. Desse total, R$ 204,2 milhões vieram de aeronaves devolvidas no processo, R$ 56,8 milhões de honorários de consultores e R$ 42,1 milhões do plano de remuneração em ações. O custo médio do litro de combustível subiu 47,2% em um ano, para R$ 5,63, e o gasto com querosene de aviação cresceu 34,2%, para R$ 1,84 bilhão. O custo ajustado por assento-quilômetro oferecido (CASK), principal medida de custo unitário do setor, subiu 22,1%, para 42,54 centavos de real. Também pesaram a alta de 27,8% em salários e benefícios, reflexo de contratações, treinamento e do reajuste de 5% da convenção coletiva, e o aumento de 50,6% nas despesas com manutenção. A capacidade total, medida em assentos-quilômetro oferecidos, caiu 6,9%. No mercado internacional, a queda foi de 32,7%, enquanto no doméstico houve alta de 1,6%. A frota operacional passou de 185 para 161 aeronaves, e o número de passageiros transportados recuou 4,7%, para 7,69 milhões. Com menos assentos e passagens mais caras, a receita por assento-quilômetro (RASK) atingiu o recorde de 47,23 centavos, alta anual de 5,5%. A receita por passageiro-quilômetro (RPSK), o rendimento, subiu 8,7%, e a tarifa média avançou 3,1%, para R$676,60. A taxa de ocupação dos aviões, porém, caiu de 84,6% para 82,2%. articles.title: The Big Biscuit Announces Annual Pajama Jam Initiative
articles.titleKo: The Big Biscuit Announces Annual Pajama Jam Initiative
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . The Big Biscuit is once again spreading warmth this holiday season through its annual Pajama Jam initiative, giving guests across its four-state footprint an opportunity to support local children and families in need. Pajama Jam started as a local initiative by Kansas City radio station Q104, to serve children in need at a local nonprofit, Operation Breakthrough. Since joining as the official sponsor and drop-off site for the donation drive five years ago, The Big Biscuit has expanded the initiative across all of its locations. This year, The Big Biscuit is partnering with eight nonprofit organizations to support children and families across Kansas, Missouri, Arkansas, and Oklahoma. “At The Big Biscuit, we believe meaningful relationships start with caring for the people and communities around us,” said Christine McLeod, Vice President of People at The Big Biscuit. “Pajama Jam is a great example of how our teams and guests come together to make a meaningful difference, helping bring comfort and a little extra joy to children during the holiday season. We’re proud to be part of communities that continue to show up for one another.” From November 16 through December 13, guests can drop off new, unused children’s pajamas for children from newborn through age 12 at any Big Biscuit location. Donations will support local children and families through community nonprofit partners in each participating market. “There is something truly special about receiving a new pair of pajamas during the holidays,” said Mary Esselman, Chief Executive Officer of Operation Breakthrough. “They bring a sense of warmth and comfort, but also that wonderful feeling of being cared for and cherished. For families already juggling competing needs—food, gas, rent and other essentials—new pajamas are not in the budget, so the donors to this annual drive are really adding holiday joy for children.” Here’s how each market is making a difference this holiday season: Kansas City: Donations benefit Operation Breakthrough, which supports children and families through education, advocacy and essential resources. Oklahoma City: Donations benefit Citizens Caring for Children, supporting children in foster care with essential resources and care. Tulsa, OK: Donations benefit Emergency Infant Services, providing essential assistance to infants and toddlers and their families. Fayetteville, AR: Donations benefit Children’s Safety Center, which provides care and advocacy for children affected by abuse. Joplin, MO: Donations support Children’s Haven, which provides safe, nurturing care to children in the community. Springfield, MO: Donations support Ozarks Area Community Action Corporation (OACAC), which helps individuals and families overcome barriers to stability and opportunity. Wichita, KS: Donations will go to Wichita Children’s Home, which provides children with safe, supportive care and resources when they need them most. Manhattan, KS: Donations will go to Manhattan Emergency Shelter, Inc., helping individuals and families experiencing homelessness find safe, stable and affordable housing. How to Get Involved Donation dates: Monday, November 16 through Sunday, December 13. What to donate: New, unused pajamas for children from newborn to age 12. Where to donate: Any Big Biscuit location. Online: Guests who cannot make it to a restaurant can shop the Pajama Jam Wish List and have new, unused children’s pajamas shipped directly to The Big Biscuit. Thank You to Our Community Sponsors The Big Biscuit extends a special thank-you to Camm Construction, Hen House and KITCH Meals for supporting this year’s Pajama Jam and helping bring warmth and comfort to children and families in our communities. Black Rock Coffee Bar is giving customers more reasons to visit later in the day. It’s also giving them more time to do it. The chain has made extended hours permanent at roughly 70 percent of its stores after testing the initiative beginning in late June and early July. New locations are opening with the longer schedule, too. Alongside a growing food menu, the move is helping Black Rock build sales beyond its morning business. The benefit hasn’t been limited to the added hour. CEO Mark Davis said sales have also grown in the hours leading up to it, while the later business is attracting a younger customer. “When we made the decision to make them permanent, they are definitely profitable, they are contributing to the same store sales, and they are contributing to the transactions,” Davis said during Black Rock’s third-quarter earnings call. But it’s one piece of a broader traffic improvement as Black Rock works to get more business from existing stores. Same-store sales rose 5.8 percent in Q3, up from 4.2 percent in the prior quarter and marking Black Rock’s 15th consecutive positive period. Transactions increased 2.4 percent, and the two-year same-store sales stack reached 16.6 percent. Revenue climbed 29.7 percent to $66.8 million. Traffic turned positive after declines in the first half, when Black Rock was comparing against activity surrounding its loyalty rollout. Transactions improved from 1.7 percent growth in July to 2.4 percent for the full quarter. Davis expects Q4 to deliver the year’s strongest same-store sales and transaction growth. Food is becoming a larger part of that story. It represented 14.2 percent of Q3 sales mix, while Black Rock’s Fuel energy platform accounted for 26.3 percent. Food attachment has increased across every daypart in each quarter of 2026. Grilled cheese and cake pops are helping build afternoon and evening orders. The latter earned a permanent place on the menu, with rotating seasonal flavors providing additional news. Black Rock has also begun rolling out an enhanced core menu with more sweet, savory, and snackable options. The goal isn’t to keep adding complexity. “We want to have a menu that does not grow substantially,” Davis said. “I think as we bring things on, we take things off.” Limited-time offerings serve as a testing ground for both customer demand and store execution. Cake pops, for instance, offered something new without creating a difficult preparation process for employees. Black Rock’s lobbies provide another way to build food occasions alongside its drive-thru business. Still, Davis said later-day food attachment isn’t where the company wants it yet, leaving room to improve as the menu evolves. The chain is becoming more targeted in how it encourages those visits, too. Loyalty represented approximately 69 percent of transactions in Q3, holding steady as Black Rock opened stores and added customers. Personalized campaigns can follow specific behaviors, such as sending an offer after a food purchase to encourage another visit. About 90 days into testing a customer data platform, Black Rock is also using point-of-sale information to reach previous visitors outside its loyalty program. articles.title: Loxam recebe aval do Cade para aquisição do controle da Mills
articles.titleKo: Loxam recebe aval do Cade para aquisição do controle da Mills
articles.originalSummary: O Conselho Administrativo de Defesa Econômica ( Cade ) aprovou, sem restrições, a aquisição do controle acionário da Mills pelo grupo francês Loxam, um dos principais players internacionais do setor de locação de equipamentos. A operação prevê a compra de 50,3% do capital social da companhia brasileira e foi anunciada pelas empresas em maio. A decisão se tornará definitiva após o prazo de 15 dias contados a partir da publicação no Diário Oficial da União, caso não haja recurso ou avocação pelo Tribunal do Cade. Com a aprovação concorrencial, a operação avança para o cumprimento das demais condições estabelecidas no contrato de compra e venda. A transferência efetiva do controle ocorrerá após a conclusão dessas etapas, que será comunicada ao mercado pelos canais oficiais das companhias. Até o fechamento da transação, Mills e Loxam permanecem operando de forma independente. A aquisição representa uma nova etapa na trajetória de mais de 74 anos da Mills e abre perspectivas para o fortalecimento de sua atuação no mercado brasileiro. A combinação das experiências e competências das duas organizações poderá contribuir para ampliar oportunidades de crescimento, diversificação de serviços e compartilhamento de conhecimentos e boas práticas. A Mills possui uma plataforma multiproduto, com atuação nos segmentos de plataformas elevatórias, equipamentos pesados, intralogística e formas e escoramentos. O Grupo Loxam, por sua vez, conta com ampla experiência internacional no setor de locação de equipamentos e operações no Brasil, incluindo soluções de energia temporária. A complementaridade entre os negócios é um dos principais fundamentos estratégicos da transação. A companhia segue operando normalmente, mantendo seus padrões de atendimento, qualidade e relacionamento com clientes, colaboradores, fornecedores e demais parceiros. Eventuais definições sobre a integração das empresas, estrutura organizacional, governança e marcas serão avaliadas após a conclusão da transação e comunicadas oportunamente. O acordo anunciado estabelece o valor de R$ 16 por ação para a aquisição do bloco de controle, sujeito à atualização prevista contratualmente até o fechamento. Após a transferência do controle, a Loxam deverá realizar uma oferta pública unificada obrigatória de aquisição de ações (OPA) destinada aos acionistas remanescentes da Mills, conforme as condições previstas para a operação e a regulamentação aplicável. A aprovação pelo Cade reforça o avanço de uma transação que reúne duas empresas com experiência consolidada no setor de locação de equipamentos. A expectativa é que, após a conclusão do negócio, a combinação de competências, escala e conhecimento de mercado contribua para o desenvolvimento de novas oportunidades e para o fortalecimento da presença das companhias no Brasil. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Carrot, the beloved fast-casual concept renowned for its extensive health-conscious menu, is continuing its New York City expansion. On November 17th, the Miami-based brand is opening their seventh NYC location in Midtown. Following their evolution from Carrot Express to simply Carrot, the new outpost will bring its signature wholesome dining experience to one of Manhattan’s busiest neighborhoods. This marks another milestone as Carrot currently operates nearly 40 locations throughout South Florida and NYC. Carrot first entered the New York City market in 2022 and has continued to expand its presence across Manhattan, with locations in Flatiron, Bryant Park, Brookfield Place, Nolita, Midtown and the Upper West Side. For more than 30 years, Carrot has been committed to serving fresh, wholesome food made with quality ingredients. The brand’s evolution to simply Carrot reflects a belief that wellness should feel natural, approachable and rooted in real food, not perfection. Their new identity embraces a simpler, more authentic approach to healthy living, encouraging people to enjoy food that feels good and fits seamlessly into everyday life. Spanning 2,340 square feet with 58 seats, the new Midtown location will be designed by Mico Design Studio, the creative team behind the brand’s refreshed aesthetic. Blending earthy elegance with modern comfort, the space will feature the warm, inviting design elements that define Carrot’s evolving identity, creating a welcoming neighborhood destination for all-day breakfast, lunch and dinner. “We are thrilled to continue growing in NYC and bring Carrot to another corner of Midtown,” said Mario Laufer, co-founder of Carrot. “Whether guests are stopping in for their morning coffee, fueling up with a protein-rich lunch or picking up dinner, our goal is to make eating well convenient and delicious without compromising on quality.” Carrot continues to offer one of the most extensive health-conscious menus in the industry, featuring thoughtfully crafted options for vegans, vegetarians, gluten-free options and protein rich lifestyles alike. Guests can enjoy vibrant salads, hearty bowls, wraps, cold-pressed juices, soups, veggie burgers, baked goods and protein-packed smoothies, alongside an expanded all-day breakfast menu. Menu highlights include Carrot’s newest Protein-Packed Sweet Potatoes, available in flavorful combinations such as Salmon Lemon Tahini, Chicken & Broccoli Melt and Turkey Avocado Fresco. Most recently, Carrot also unveiled a partnership with Miami based coffee roasters, Imperial Moto, highlighting a specialty brew crafted exclusively for Carrot. Carrot’s newest Midtown location is located at 1290 Avenue of the Americas, New York, NY 10121. Hours of operation will be from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m., offering dine-in, takeout, delivery and catering services. For more information, visit www.CarrotExpress.com or follow @EatAtCarrot. Checkers and Rally’s, the iconic double drive-thru burger and fries brand known for its legendary taste, undeniable value, and game-changing innovation, has announced the reopening of its restaurant at 3605 N. Grand Blvd, St. Louis, MO, with an updated design and enhanced guest experience. Following a previous closure due to a fire, the restaurant reopened its doors on November 10, bringing its signature bold flavors and unbeatable value back to local guests with a refreshed look and improved operations. The brand plans to host a grand opening celebration at a later date. The Checkers & Rally’s corporate team will operate the reopened restaurant, which features the brand’s updated restaurant prototype and streamlined operating model. These enhancements aim to improve operational efficiency, provide greater convenience and deliver a high-quality guest experience. The reopening underscores the brand’s continued commitment to investing in its restaurant operations and meeting the evolving needs of guests, while welcoming back loyal customers who have eagerly awaited the location’s reopening. “We continue to prioritize investments that strengthen our restaurant operations and enhance the experience we deliver to our guests,” said Peter Busse, Chief Development Officer of Checkers & Rally’s. “The reopening of this St. Louis location reflects that commitment, bringing an updated restaurant design and improved operations to a community that has shown tremendous support for the brand. We look forward to welcoming guests back and continuing to deliver the bold flavors, exceptional value and convenience they expect from Checkers & Rally’s.” Merged in 1999 to form one concept, Checkers & Rally’s primarily operates through a proven franchise model, in which owners benefit from brand recognition, operational support, and marketing resources. Potential franchise prospects can develop on less than half of an acre, which is half the size of competing drive-thru concepts. Checkers & Rally’s current strategy is targeting select markets throughout the United States, particularly in South and Central Wisconsin, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Southern California, Las Vegas, Florida, and South Carolina. Pinstripes, the family-friendly experiential dining and entertainment destination known for its interactive games and chef-driven menu of classic American cuisine reopens its doors in Orlando under new ownership today. “We are very pleased to bring Pinstripes back to Orlando to once again be part of this dynamic marketplace,” said Chairman and CEO, Robert Cornog, Jr. “This reopening reflects not only our confidence in the Pinstripes brand and business, but also this location. We look forward to welcoming guests back in, as well as the opportunity to introduce an enhanced combination of chef-driven dining, entertainment and hospitality to the local community and visitors alike.” Located within Vineland Pointe at 11643 Daryl Carter Pkwy, the fully renovated, two-story, 29,000-square-foot venue features refreshed games and entertainment. While its 16 signature bowling lanes remain, new activities are featured throughout as Pinstripes introduces a number of family-friendly games. The upgrades extend to the Pinstripes patio, which now features enhanced seating and new activities such as outdoor pool tables. The bar and lounge has also added Augmented Reality Darts, expanding entertainment offerings throughout the entirety of the venue. These enhancements give every guest the opportunity to “create their own” personalized experience. In addition to the venue’s games and entertainment, Pinstripes Orlando will offer a refreshed calendar of year-round programming ranging from family-friendly activations to grown-up fun. Music Bingo will launch on Nov. 19 and take place weekly on Thursdays, inviting guests to test their music knowledge with some healthy competition. Sips & Sounds, Pinstripes’ weekly live music series featuring local musicians, will begin Friday, Nov. 20, hosted on the patio from 6:30-9:30 p.m. Starting on Saturday, Nov. 28, Pinstripes will bring its popular Santa Brunch to Orlando for the holiday season where guests can enjoy a bottomless brunch buffet, complimentary visits with Santa and the opportunity to snap their own holiday photos. Adding to the experience, Pinstripes Orlando offers its signature, chef-driven menu that brings approachable, elevated dining to the destination. The menu features a range of shareable starters, fresh salads, wood-fired pizzas, sandwiches, burgers, pastas and entrées, alongside indulgent desserts designed for everything from casual gatherings to celebrations. Guests can pair their meal with a selection of classic and specialty cocktails, wines and beers, making the dining area and bar a natural gathering place before or after a round of games. On weekends, Pinstripes offers a signature brunch experience, featuring favorites such as chicken and waffles, shrimp cocktail, breakfast pizza and baked goods, alongside interactive stations including made-to-order omelets and fresh-carved prime rib. Pinstripes was acquired by the parent company of another “eatertainment” fixture, Punch Bowl Social, in November 2025, and its return to Central Florida is fueled by the new ownership’s investment in the brand through refreshed spaces, enhanced programming, upgraded activities, and revamped food and beverage offerings. Pinstripes Orlando is the first location to implement these upgrades which will roll out across the portfolio in the coming year. Peter Bergner, a representative of Vineland Pointe’s ownership, added, “We are excited to welcome Pinstripes back to Vineland Point – it is a great addition to the trade area. The new Pinstripes team has been a great partner in reopening the location and we are confident in the location’s future success.” For more information on Pinstripes and upcoming programming at the Orlando location visit, Pinstripes.com/Orlando. Yum China Holdings, Inc. today announced that it has hit the 20,000-store milestone, spanning over 2,800 cities and towns across China, as it celebrates the 10th anniversary of its listing on the New York Stock Exchange. Yum China celebrates the 10th anniversary of its listing on the New York Stock Exchange The Company celebrated this milestone with over 10,000 restaurant general managers (RGMs) at its annual RGM convention. This year’s event was held in Chengdu, a vibrant city renowned for its rich culinary culture. The occasion was marked by the simultaneous opening of six new stores – one for each brand it operates in Mainland China: KFC, Pizza Hut, Lavazza, Taco Bell, Little Sheep and Huang Ji Huang. Joey Wat, CEO of Yum China, commented, “Reaching 20,000 stores is a milestone made possible by the hard work of Yum China employees and the trust of our customers. 2026 marks the second year of executing our RGM 3.0 strategy, which focuses on resilience, growth and moat. In a dynamic operating environment, we remain laser-focused on execution — solving problems, turning strategy into action, and delivering sustainable profitable growth.” Targeting 30,000 Stores by 2030 From the first KFC store in China, opened in 1987, it took the Company 33 years to reach its first 10,000 stores and just six years to add the next 10,000. As shared at its 2025 investor day, Yum China is targeting 30,000 stores by 2030, meaning it expects to add the next 10,000 stores within four years. This accelerated expansion underscores Yum China’s strong execution capabilities and significant runway for growth in China. The Company plans to continue expanding through its equity-and-franchise hybrid model, supported by diverse store formats and offerings tailored to different city tiers and consumer occasions. Alongside its rapid store expansion, KFC and Pizza Hut developed side-by-side modules including KCOFFEE café, KPRO and Pizza Hut Burger Bar, capturing new consumer occasions and generating incremental sales and profits. Through solid execution and a strong commitment to shareholder value, Yum China delivered double-digit diluted EPS growth year-over-year in the first nine months of this year and in each of the past three years, and continues to target a double-digit diluted EPS CAGR from 2026 to 2028, as outlined at its 2025 investor day. Agentic AI to Support Growth at Scale Yum China’s RGM 3.0 strategy has a dual focus of innovation and operational efficiency to drive growth. Since 2023, the Company has been exploring and deploying agentic AI to enhance operational efficiency across the organization. In 2025, Yum China began piloting “Q-Smart,” an AI-enabled assistant that supports restaurant managers with data-intensive tasks such as labor scheduling and inventory management. Its latest “AI Store Assistant” builds on Q-Smart and adds a range of new capabilities. By further integrating AI and advanced technologies with restaurant operating data and connected kitchen equipment, the upgraded agent provides real-time recommendations on operating decisions. For example, it can identify changes in restaurant traffic and suggest adjustments to production and staffing, helping restaurants respond more nimbly while reducing food waste. Supporting and Caring for Frontline Teams Yum China upholds the “RGM No.1” principle, prioritizing the needs of its RGMs and frontline employees. In addition to the AI Store Assistant, Yum China launched its RGM One-Stop Service Center this year. It features a single interface where a dedicated case manager, aided by AI, supports RGM requests across IT, human resources, supply chain, finance, and other functions. Square today announced that Squaremates, an intelligent business agent that can take on complex, multi-step work across a seller’s business using its own secure workspace, is generally available to U.S. sellers¹. An evolution of Managerbot, Squaremates is the main way sellers experience Square Dashboard when they sign in: it’s where they ask questions, see what needs attention, and get work done. Alongside Squaremates, Square is also introducing an improved Square MCP (Model Context Protocol) and new Square CLI (Command-Line Interface), giving sellers and developers easy access to the Square platform, right within their own agentic tools – and the ability to build and host their own apps on Square with Squaremates Apps. “Running a business is an endless string of judgment calls that are all on the owner. How to price a new menu item, whether to add a shift, what to do about a slow week,” said Willem Avé, Square’s Global Head of Intelligence. “We built Squaremates to help share that load, and now it can take on more of the work than ever before: longer, more complex tasks that used to mean manual reconciliation and hours at a desk, now handled start to finish and handed back as something a seller can actually use. Square MCP and CLI further augment this vision. A lot of sellers already have an AI tool they like working in, and our job is to help that tool work directly with their Square business, so they can run things however’s most productive for them.” Richer Capabilities, More Time Back Managerbot launched in open beta six months ago, underpinned by two ideas: it monitors the business and proposes actions, while the seller decides; and it doesn’t just answer questions, it gets work done – all in service of helping sellers stay on top of what’s important and get time back to focus on what matters to them. Squaremates builds on that foundation, with access to cloud compute that lets it take on work spanning multiple steps or tasks and touching more parts of a business. For example, Squaremates can look at a period of sales, identify customers who have lapsed, and generate a marketing campaign or discount directed at bringing those customers back. It can review a seller’s catalog and make bulk updates across prices, descriptions, channel visibility, and even images. Or it can weigh labor costs against sales for a specified period and come back with a more cost-optimized staffing schedule to review. Squaremates also now creates rich artifacts when completing a task – usable outputs like a polished, graphical sales breakdown or a fully designed, on-brand email campaign rather than simply a block of text in a chat window. Squaremates’ reach is beginning to extend beyond Square itself. When it comes to restocking, a Squaremates capability currently in beta can check what’s running low, prepare an order, and build it directly on a supplier’s own site, ready for the seller to complete. And coming soon, a seller’s daily briefing will be able to pull in what’s waiting in their inbox alongside what’s happening in their business with permissioned access to their email account, giving sellers one place to start the day instead of several. The result: Squaremates can carry a task from start to finish, bring everything a seller needs into view before the day begins, and work directly with the third-party services sellers rely on to run their business, like suppliers, all while the seller decides what goes ahead. “Our cheese sauce is made in-house, and it’s gold. Bojangles is honoring America’s heroes by inviting guests to give back with every visit. From now through Dec. 13, participating Bojangles restaurants are raising funds for the Mae and George Siller Tunnel to Towers Foundation Scholarship Program, which provides scholarships for undergraduate degrees and accredited trade school programs to the children of Gold Star families, fallen first responders and catastrophically injured veterans and first responders. Depending on the restaurant, guests can support the campaign at checkout by rounding up their purchase, making a donation or doing both. Donors can give $1 or $5 and add their names to flags displayed in the restaurant, creating a visible show of community support. Those who donate $1 will receive a coupon for a free Bo-Berry Biscuit, and those who donate $5 will receive a coupon for a free Sausage Biscuit, both redeemable on their next visit. “Supporting military families is a cause close to our foundation’s heart,” said Ken Reynolds, Executive Director of the Bojangles Foundation. “This holiday season, we’re inviting our guests to help honor those who served by investing in their children’s futures, and every round-up and donation brings us closer to that goal.” “Our scholarship program carries the names of my parents, Mae and George Siller, who taught all seven of us that you take care of the people who take care of you,” said Frank Siller, Chairman and CEO of the Tunnel to Towers Foundation. “These children have already sacrificed more than anyone should have to. Thanks to Bojangles and its guests, every dollar raised this holiday season helps these children build the future they deserve. That’s what doing good looks like, and we are so grateful.” This is just the latest campaign in Bojangles’ ongoing commitment to supporting the military community, following its summer fundraiser in honor of America 250, in which the brand and its guests raised more than $519,000 for military families and veterans through Folds of Honor and the Veteran Golfers Association. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Kura Sushi's same-store sales declined 5.7 percent in Q4, including an 11.5 percent traffic drop. Kura Sushi’s conveyor belts give diners plenty of reasons to keep reaching for another plate, but getting them to sit down for a weekday lunch is proving more difficult. With customer visits falling and its average check reaching $29, the revolving sushi chain is testing a less expensive way through the door. An October pilot offered meal combinations at $9.99 and $11.99, giving Kura an opportunity to compete for lunch occasions that its typical ticket may put out of reach. The discounted meals accounted for 5 percent of orders during the three-day test, even though Kura promoted them only to rewards members. As an additional positive, the lower-priced options did not reduce average spending per customer, prompting Kura to expand the test ahead of a planned nationwide rollout in fiscal Q2 (December 1 through February 28). READ MORE : Kura Sushi Welcomes Profit Growth Amid Volatile Environment Kura Sushi Hits its Stride Thanks to Collaborations, Tech Investments Before introducing the meals nationwide, Kura plans to adjust the offerings to ensure the lower prices don’t hurt its profit margins. It is also developing off-premises value bundles and preparing paid advertising to reach customers who have never visited. “So if somebody only has $12, we want Kura to be a great option. But if they can spend more, we want them to come as well,” said CEO Jimmy Uba. The push follows a fiscal fourth quarter in which same-store sales declined 5.7 percent, including an 11.5 percent traffic drop. Price and mix contributed 5.8 percent, with effective pricing of 4.2 percent. Kura traced much of its traffic weakness to weekday lunches after studying customer feedback in August. The pressure stretched across markets, making the challenge less a regional issue than a question of how the chain fits into consumers’ everyday spending. The company believes it is attracting diners accustomed to paying more for sushi, pointing to sustained gains in sales mix. Winning those customers, however, has not compensated for the loss of other visits. For instance, in Q1 thus far, same-store sales have improved to negative 3.1 percent, but Uba said the change has come from mix, with traffic largely tracking its Q4 performance. Kura is responding by holding off on another price increase. A previous 3.5 percent increase rolled off at the beginning of November, and the chain chose not to replace it. Its pricing decisions can change, but the current plan calls for margin improvement without additional menu pricing. Uba said rising sushi prices across the industry create an opportunity to attract a larger audience. Kura’s challenge is making its affordability more visible without weakening customers’ perception of its ingredients. Value combinations add another traffic tool to a business that has relied on pop-culture collaborations, collectible prizes, and limited-time food offerings to bring guests back. Kura plans eight intellectual property collaborations in fiscal 2027, up from seven last year. Its Yoshi campaign runs through November and December, followed by Hatsune Miku in January and Godzilla in February and March. Four additional collaborations will follow. The company is also increasing its Kura Reserve limited-time offerings from nine to 12. Not every fourth-quarter collaboration met expectations. Kura also saw traffic change when the World Cup began and expected visits to recover after the tournament ended. That rebound did not materialize as anticipated. In terms of development, Kura is switching how it measures expansion. After establishing a presence in 25 states and nearing 100 restaurants, the company is changing from a percentage-based growth target to an annual opening count that can increase gradually. articles.title: Starbucks is Putting More Money in Employees’ Pockets
articles.titleKo: Starbucks is Putting More Money in Employees’ Pockets
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Nearly 200,000 full- and part-time employees worldwide received new Bean Stock grants on Wednesday. Starbucks is giving hundreds of thousands of employees a financial stake in its turnaround, rolling out stock grants, performance bonuses, and expanded tipping opportunities as its Back to Starbucks strategy gains traction. The coffee giant announced Thursday that nearly 200,000 full- and part-time employees worldwide received new Bean Stock grants on Wednesday. Another 130,000 employees have stock grants from previous years vesting this month, continuing a program that has provided more than $2.75 billion in pretax gains since its introduction in 1991. More than 80 percent of eligible hourly employees in North America will receive their first payout Friday through the new Best of Starbucks Reward program. Announced earlier this spring, the initiative allows eligible baristas and shift supervisors to earn up to $300 each quarter when their coffeehouses meet or exceed certain sales, operational, and customer service metrics. Starbucks has also seen a substantial increase in customer tipping since expanding its digital tipping options in July. Customers have contributed more than $22 million in additional tips through the new channels, more than doubling tipping activity. Chief partner officer Sara Kelly and COO Mike Grams outlined the investments in a company blog post Thursday. “We have strong momentum in our Back to Starbucks plan, and coffeehouse partners are at the heart of that progress,” Kelly and Grams wrote. “Every day, they bring the Starbucks experience to life through their craft, the connections they create with customers, and the way they support one another.” The investments follow a strong fiscal fourth quarter for Starbucks, which reported its third consecutive quarter of U.S. same-store sales growth exceeding 7 percent. Domestic comps rose 7.7 percent, driven by a 2.4 percent increase in traffic and a 5.2 percent increase in average ticket. Global same-store sales climbed 7.2 percent, marking the company’s fifth consecutive quarter of worldwide growth. The stock grants continue a tradition that dates back 35 years, when Starbucks operated approximately 100 locations. The company became the first major retailer to offer stock grants to eligible full- and part-time hourly employees. Since the program began, more than 2 million employees have benefited from Bean Stock. Starbucks is also investing in staffing, scheduling, and its Green Apron Service initiative to improve daily operations. The company reported that hourly employee turnover is nearly half the industry average, and nearly 95 percent of employees receive their preferred schedules. More than 3 million people applied for jobs with Starbucks in North America last year. The chain is also maintaining its commitment to fill 90 percent of retail supervisory and managerial positions through internal promotions, creating advancement opportunities for existing employees. Other benefits available to eligible workers include comprehensive health coverage, full upfront tuition coverage for a first bachelor’s degree, and up to 18 weeks of paid parental leave. A recent study by Aon found that Starbucks offered more valuable benefits to hourly retail employees than any of the more than 60 U.S. companies examined. The compensation changes also consider unionized shops. Starbucks said the Best of Starbucks Reward, weekly pay, and expanded tipping options are subject to collective bargaining at the approximately 5 percent of its U.S. locations with union representation, as required by federal law. “When partners thrive, Starbucks thrives,” Kelly and Grams wrote. The post Starbucks is Putting More Money in Employees’ Pockets appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Mildreds Evolves Menu As The Plant-Based Pioneer Enters Its 38th Year
articles.titleKo: Mildreds Evolves Menu As The Plant-Based Pioneer Enters Its 38th Year
articles.originalSummary: London plant-based restaurant group Mildreds is evolving its menu this autumn, almost four decades after opening in Soho in 1988 – when dedicated vegetarian restaurants remained a relatively niche proposition. The new menu, launches across Mildreds’ five London restaurants, is the result of several months of development led by Food and Brand Director Sarah Wasserman and the group’s senior chef team. It builds on established Mildreds dishes while putting greater emphasis on vegetables, technique, provenance and the independent producers behind the food. The menu marks an evolution for the group, grown from its original Greek street restaurant to 5 locations across London; Soho, Camden, King’s Cross, Victoria and Covent Garden, moving from vegetarian to fully vegan cooking in 2021. Wasserman , who has spent over 20 years working in the Mildreds kitchen, said the development process focused on refining what the group does best. “This menu is the work of the whole kitchen team, not just me. I’ve spent over twenty years cooking at Mildreds, and if I’ve learned anything in that time, it’s that the best dishes come from patience, which is exactly how we built this menu: tested, changed and tested again, until we were happy to put our name to every one of them. It leans more on the people who grow what we cook with and the technique behind each dish, than anything we’ve done before.” The new menu includes Handmade Beetroot and Sweet Potato Tortelloni with Beetroot Velouté and Hazelnut Pistou ; Glazed Momo Dumplings with Chilli Miso, Cucumber and Ginger Pickle ; and Oyster Mushroom and Hispi Shawarma with Sweet Potato and Chipotle Romesco . Existing Mildreds dishes have been revisited rather than simply retained. Its Kiri hodi , one of the group’s best-known dishes, centres on roast squash, with biryani pilau, cabbage thoran and tomato and lime sambol. This is a menu that places produce at its centre, with dishes such as Sambal Mushrooms , Aubergine Milanese and Shiitake Whipped Tofu built around vegetables, pulses and technique. The menu has also been shaped by Mildreds’ supplier relationships, with independent producers providing key ingredients across the estate. Clean Bean Tofu, founded by Neil McLennan, supplies handmade London tofu made from organic soya beans. Suffolk producer Hodmedod’s provides British-grown pulses and grains, as well as fermented fava bean umami paste. Bread comes from Watford bakery Seven Seeded , whose sourdough is made using four ingredients and fermented for 48 hours. Belazu supplies olive oil and Mediterranean ingredients, working with the Pons family of olive growers in Catalonia, while plant-based products from Symplicity bring traditional fermentation techniques into the kitchen. The wider pantry is supported by Brighton workers’ co-operative Infinity Foods , which has traded since 1971, while seasonal fruit and vegetables, including pumpkins and squash used extensively on the new menu, are sourced through Wild Harvest’s network of UK and European growers. Drinks follow a similar approach, with coffee from Cornwall-based Origin , tea from Rare Tea Co and wine supplied by family merchant Ellis Wines , which dates back to 1822. The bar range includes independent producers such as El Tequileño, Sapling Vodka and Jaisalmer Gin. Managing Director Sam Anstey said: “Mildreds has helped lead the way in vegetarian and vegan dining in London since 1988. Our focus has always been on serving food that people want to come back for, whether they are vegan, vegetarian or simply love good food. This menu builds on that reputation, with bold flavours, great ingredients and the care and skill of Sarah and our kitchen team.”

articles.title: Smithdown Road Favourite ‘The Tavern Co’ Opens in Liverpool City Centre with Tavern Co Social on Water Street
articles.titleKo: Smithdown Road Favourite ‘The Tavern Co’ Opens in Liverpool City Centre with Tavern Co Social on Water Street
articles.originalSummary: One of Liverpool’s most celebrated independent culinary institutions has arrived in the heart of the city centre. The team behind the multi-award-winning The Tavern Co on Smithdown Road has opened its new concept, Tavern Co Social, on Water Street. Taking over the prominent ground-floor site inside the historic New Zealand House – the former home of Hooters and the legendary Newz Bar – the venue brings fresh, modern energy to one of the city’s most iconic streets. For over three decades, The Tavern Co has been a cornerstone of Liverpool’s independent food scene, twice named the home of the “UK’s Best Breakfast” for its legendary full English and American-style morning spreads. Now, the brand has brought its community-focused ethos, established reputation and famous flavours to a wider city-centre audience. Tavern Co Social blends the nostalgic, welcoming charm of the original Wavertree landmark with a high-energy, modern social space. By day, guests can enjoy the iconic breakfast and brunch menus that built the brand’s following. As evening approaches, the 120-cover venue transitions into an intimate, lively social hub featuring a specialised tapas menu, craft beers, hearty dishes and a dedicated setup for sports enthusiasts. The space features a sleek, contemporary interior anchored by an expansive main bar, complete with more than 10 TVs positioned throughout the venue so sports fans can catch every major event from plush booths or right at the bar. This expansion marks a significant milestone for the brand under its new ownership group, which has invested heavily in modernising and securing the future of the flagship South Liverpool site since 2023. The second location represents a major vote of confidence in Liverpool’s commercial district and daytime hospitality market. Mellissa Dunleavy, General Manager of Tavern Co Social, said: “For over three decades, The Tavern Co has been a staple of Liverpool’s food scene on Smithdown Road, famous for bringing people together. Expanding into Liverpool city centre is a massive milestone for us. This new site will create over 20 full- and part-time jobs for the industry while bringing an iconic building back to life. We look forward to welcoming familiar faces from our heritage site, as well as new diners trying out Tavern 2.0 for the first time.” Tavern Co Social opened on Friday 18 September 2026 and operates daily from 8:00am. Opening Times: Sunday to Thursday: 8am until 10pm Friday and Saturday: 8am until midnight Tavern Co Social New Zealand House, 18 Water Street, Liverpool, L2 8TA

articles.title: 5 Lessons from John Peyton on Dine’s Dual-Brand Bet
articles.titleKo: 5 Lessons from John Peyton on Dine’s Dual-Brand Bet
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . The Applebee's-IHOP approach has runway for hundreds of locations. Nobody asked Dine Brands to put Applebee’s and IHOP under one roof. But according to CEO John Peyton, guests are finding plenty to like once they walk through the door: Two-thirds of checks at the company’s dual-brand restaurants include items from both menus. For Peyton, that illustrates an important distinction between responding to demand and creating something customers couldn’t quite picture beforehand. On FSR’s Restaurant Innovator podcast, he discusses how the format grew from international experimentation into a U.S. development opportunity. With 60 locations open and more on the way, the effort offers lessons that extend beyond pairing two familiar names. LISTEN TO THE FULL EPISODE HERE 1. Look for complementary demand, not just compatible brands The logic behind combining Applebee’s and IHOP starts with when people visit. IHOP brings breakfast strength. Applebee’s brings an established afternoon and evening business. Together, they create an opportunity to generate more sales from an existing building throughout the day. For IHOP operators, that means addressing a historically challenging dinner business. For Applebee’s franchisees, it means adding a breakfast occasion they weren’t serving. That distinction matters as operators contend with higher costs. Peyton sees adding an entire daypart as a different growth proposition from competing for another incremental visit. Most locations have been conversions, allowing franchisees to spread fixed costs across more sales. “That incremental revenue flows at a higher margin than the original restaurant because the fixed costs remain the same,” he says. READ MORE: Dine Brands Looks to Find New Ways to Win at Applebee’s and IHOP 2. Give customers something concrete to react to Peyton argues that a focus group would have struggled to evaluate a shared Applebee’s–IHOP experience without seeing it. Dine Brands wasn’t starting without evidence. International operators had already opened dual-brand restaurants, and Peyton visited locations before pursuing the opportunity domestically. But translating that evidence into a U.S. concept required franchisees willing to open restaurants before every detail was settled. Those early operators understood they would help refine the format as they learned what worked. “We had conversations with the first franchisees that the concept you open is not going to necessarily be the concept in two years, and together we’re going to refine it and tweak it,” Peyton says. “And so we went big and we went all in.” Research followed the experience rather than substituting for it. With restaurants operating, Dine could ask guests what they liked, what needed improvement, and how their impressions changed after visiting. One early finding: Guests largely don’t care which brand’s side they sit on, provided they can order from both menus. “One of the definitions of innovation is giving the consumer something they didn’t know they wanted,” Peyton says. Combine the experience without doubling the complexity Putting two brands together could easily mean giving the kitchen twice as much to manage. Dine Brands deliberately avoided that approach. While overseas locations had essentially combined both menus, the U.S. team streamlined the offering to keep the total item count in line with an individual brand’s menu. Overlapping products underwent a comparison process. The resulting burger, for example, uses an Applebee’s burger and an IHOP bun. Still, menu editing doesn’t eliminate the learning curve. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . AMP Up1 Hospitality is readying its roster as it prepares for the next phase of growth. In late October, the experiential dining and entertainment company behind Your 3rd Spot and forthcoming concept The Looking Glass announced three senior leadership appointments. The group promoted Chris Barrows to chief operating officer, Erin Callahan to senior vice president of operations and managing partner overseeing the Midwest, and hired Atlanta chef Joe Schafer as culinary director and executive chef. The leadership moves arrive as AMP Up1 is building The Looking Glass , an immersive social playground designed to accommodate more than 1,000 guests, set to open in downtown Atlanta in spring 2027 . Plus, the team is expanding Your 3rd Spot to a second location at Veridian—a 225-acre mixed-use development in Schaumburg, Illinois—in 2028. For founder and chief vision officer Josh Rossmeisl, the appointments are about building the operating teams and culinary capabilities needed to support those ambitions. “We’re thinking about the company we want to become, not just the one we’re operating today,” he tells FSR . “Great real estate, access to capital, and incredible ideas are all important, but ultimately, the success of our brands will be determined by the people we surround ourselves with.” “You can’t wait until you’re ready to open the next location to start building that leadership foundation,” he adds. From Hourly Employees to the C-Suite Barrows is stepping into the COO role after serving as AMP Up1’s chief people officer, bringing nearly two decades of experience in operations and talent development. Previously chief people officer, Chris Barrows now takes responsibility for company operations, developing leaders, and maintaining consistent standards as the company builds additional venues. His hospitality career began in 2007 as a host at Kings Dining & Entertainment in Boston, where he met Rossmeisl . A Georgia State University graduate with a degree in managerial sciences, Barrows advanced through floor management, assistant general manager, and general manager positions before taking on companywide responsibilities in systems, training, recruiting, and talent development. “Starting as a host taught me that the opportunity in front of you matters more than the destination you can’t control yet,” Barrows says. “I took a pay cut to be around the right people and situation. I didn’t have grand end goals, but I bet on myself to do a good job and a find a way to be successful. That decision has shaped everything since.” His advice to leaders in similar situations? “Stop fixating on where you’re going and do something with where you are. The next rep leads to the next opportunity,” he says. “That’s still how I think about growth and leadership today. The opportunities that ending came weren’t there when I started, and I like to believe that the work created them. When they came, I was ready.” As a member of AMP Up1’s founding leadership team, he helped build the recruiting practices, training programs, and leadership development systems supporting Your 3rd Spot’s Atlanta debut. His expanded responsibilities now include company operations, leadership development, and maintaining consistent standards as the portfolio grows. The promotion also puts an internal development story at the center of the company’s expansion: a former hourly employee is now responsible for leading its operations. That employee-first philosophy is baked into the company’s DNA. At the heart of the group’s success and future outlook is an innovative approach to team empowerment—one that grants employees a genuine stake in the company’s success. articles.title: Comerciários de SP e RS fecham acordo para reduzir a escala 6×1 para 5×2
articles.titleKo: Comerciários de SP e RS fecham acordo para reduzir a escala 6×1 para 5×2
articles.originalSummary: Os sindicatos dos comerciários de São Paulo e de Porto Alegre firmaram acordos coletivos e aditivos com representantes do setor empresarial para viabilizar o fim da escala 6×1 a partir de dezembro, conforme previsto na Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) 141. A negociação ocorre mesmo após a Confederação Nacional do Comércio de Bens, Serviços e Turismo (CNC) protocolar, no Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), uma ação direta de inconstitucionalidade, com pedido de medida cautelar . A entidade buscava adiar a implementação da mudança para dezembro de 2027. Com os novos acordos, cerca de 700 mil trabalhadores de São Paulo e Porto Alegre serão afetados. A emenda à Constituição que acaba com a escala 6×1 foi promulgada em 16 de outubro pelo Congresso. A sessão contou com a participação do presidente Lula (PT), que tinha na proposta uma de suas bandeiras na campanha à reeleição. Acordos são válidos a partir de 16 de dezembro O presidente do Sindicato dos Comerciários de São Paulo, Ricardo Patah, afirmou que a adoção da escala 5×2 e a redução da jornada de trabalho para 42 horas semanais entram em vigor em 16 de dezembro. Entre os setores atingidos na capital paulista estão supermercados, atacado, carnes, calçados, automóveis e aço. “O movimento sindical não quer quebrar as empresas ou enfraquecer a saúde financeira delas. Pelo contrário, vamos trabalhar conjuntamente e buscaremos valorizar o ser humano, que terá a oportunidade efetiva de ter um dia a mais com a sua família, se qualificar ou fazer o que achar melhor”, disse. O acordo na cidade de São Paulo autoriza formatos flexíveis como 5×2 e 4×3, além de bancos de horas compensatórios, proibindo a escala 6×1 tradicional. Já o Sindicato dos Empregados no Comércio de Porto Alegre (Sindec-POA) informou que o acordo abrange cerca de 100 mil trabalhadores, 22 sindicatos patronais e 30 mil estabelecimentos na capital gaúcha. Na cidade, a partir de 16 dezembro de 2026, a jornada será reduzida de 44 horas para 42h semanais, distribuídas em cinco dias de trabalho. Já em dezembro de 2027, haverá novamente a redução da carga horária, chegando a 40 horas semanais, sem redução salarial. Antecipação das folgas em Porto Alegre Em Porto Alegre, a partir de 1º de dezembro deste ano, será instituído um banco de descanso remunerado. Nas semanas de pico de vendas que antecedem o Natal e o Ano Novo, iniciadas nos dias 14, 21 e 28, os trabalhadores terão direito a duas folgas remuneradas. Nilton Neco Souza da Silva, presidente do Sindec-POA, afirmou que um destes descansos deverá ser usufruído na própria semana, enquanto o outro poderá ser utilizado em outros dias de dezembro. “Só precisa garantir que o trabalhador tenha as 8 folgas durante o mês. A grande vantagem é que a empresa poderá antecipá-las a partir de 1º de dezembro”, explicou. Para ele, a medida representa um avanço significativo, ao contemplar tanto os trabalhadores, que dependem das comissões durante as festas de fim de ano, quanto os empregadores, que buscam manter as lojas em funcionamento com o quadro completo de funcionários. “A partir de janeiro de 2027, a empresa poderá adotar a escala 6×1 em uma das semanas, se garantir as oito folgas ao longo do mês. Assim, poderá alternar semanas de 5×2 e 4×3, facilitando a organização em períodos de maior movimento no comércio”, disse. Segundo Silva, a negociação, embora exitosa para ambos os lados, foi concluída em apenas duas semanas. “Isso prova haver tempo, sim, para firmar um acordo, desmontando o argumento da CNI (Confederação Nacional da Indústria) e da CNC de que isso não seria possível e de que, por isso, seria necessário adiar a mudança para dezembro do próximo ano. Há, sim, a possibilidade de construir um acordo que beneficie a todos”, afirmou. Dino decidirá regras até sexta-feira O ministro Flávio Dino, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), disse que vai proferir uma decisão até esta sexta-feira, 13, para remover “amarras” e facilitar a negociação coletiva na implementação do fim da esc

articles.title: Shopee registra alta de 90% nas vendas na semana que antecede o 11.11
articles.titleKo: Shopee registra alta de 90% nas vendas na semana que antecede o 11.11
articles.originalSummary: A Shopee registrou crescimento de 90% no volume de vendas entre 5 e 10 de novembro, na comparação com os dias que antecederam a Black Friday de 2025. O resultado foi impulsionado pela procura por produtos de maior ticket médio, como smartphones, televisores, geladeiras, freezers e scooters, segundo a plataforma. Entre os itens sazonais, ar-condicionado e artigos de decoração natalina também ganharam destaque, com árvores de Natal e piscas-piscas entre os produtos mais buscados. “Estamos prontos para tornar o 11.11 deste ano o nosso maior dia de vendas da história da Shopee no País. Esses resultados revelam uma prévia de como os brasileiros aproveitam as oportunidades de economia no mês de maior expectativa para o varejo. Temos uma programação que conecta todo o nosso ecossistema, com benefícios, entretenimento e dezenas de milhares de ofertas em mais de 30 categorias, além de cupons especiais e entrega rápida”, afirma Felipe Piringer, diretor de Marketing da Shopee. O movimento acompanha a intenção de compra dos consumidores: 86% planejam comprar durante o 11.11 e/ou a Black Friday, de acordo com pesquisa da Shopee. Nas primeiras horas do 11.11, a plataforma registrou crescimento superior a 40% no número de acessos, impulsionado por R$ 25 milhões em cupons de desconto e vouchers de frete grátis sem valor mínimo de compra. O ticket médio por produto avançou 18% em relação às primeiras horas da Black Friday de 2025. As categorias com maior destaque foram Casa, Eletrônicos, Beleza, Esportes e Lazer e Casa & Construção. O Pix foi a forma de pagamento escolhida por 52% dos consumidores, enquanto o cartão de crédito respondeu por 35% das transações. O resultado foi influenciado principalmente pelas atividades de transportes e de informação e comunicação. Na comparação anual, o setor também apresentou recuo de 0,1%, interrompendo uma sequência de 29 resultados positivos em relação ao mesmo mês do ano anterior. Para o IBGE, variações dessa magnitude são consideradas estabilidade. Confira a análise de 10 especialistas sobre os desafios do setor de serviços e os riscos de estagnação em 2027. Lucas Minucci, professor da PIB The New College O setor de serviços continua relevante para a geração de empregos, mas a manutenção desse desempenho dependerá de maior eficiência empresarial. Juros elevados, inflação e incertezas internacionais exigem planejamento financeiro e adaptação. Para sustentar o crescimento, as empresas precisarão aumentar a produtividade, investir na formação de lideranças e integrar finanças, tecnologia e estratégia, sem depender exclusivamente da ampliação das equipes. Sidney Lima, analista da Ouro Preto Investimentos A perda de força dos serviços indica que os efeitos da política monetária restritiva estão se espalhando pela economia. O emprego e a renda ainda sustentam parte do consumo, mas famílias demonstram menor disposição para gastar e empresas, para investir. A combinação de crescimento mais fraco e inflação de serviços resistente pode levar o Banco Central a manter os juros elevados por mais tempo. Entre os riscos para 2027 estão juros elevados, endividamento das famílias e aumento dos custos operacionais. A tendência é de crescimento moderado, caso não haja avanços na política fiscal que permitam reduzir os juros. Gustavo Assis, CEO da Asset A sustentação dos serviços depende de condições financeiras mais favoráveis. A persistência da inflação, as incertezas fiscais e o custo do crédito estão entre os principais riscos para a atividade. A digitalização pode ampliar a produtividade, mas o crescimento não deve depender exclusivamente do consumo. articles.title: WeWork libera 23 unidades no Brasil para aluguel de espaços por hora
articles.titleKo: WeWork libera 23 unidades no Brasil para aluguel de espaços por hora
articles.originalSummary: A busca por maior flexibilidade no uso dos espaços corporativos está abrindo novas possibilidades para o mercado de escritórios compartilhados. A WeWork lançou o serviço On Demand em 53 unidades na América Latina, permitindo que profissionais e empresas reservem mesas de trabalho e salas de reunião por períodos que vão de meia hora a um dia inteiro. No Brasil, o serviço está disponível em 23 unidades localizadas em São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Belo Horizonte e Porto Alegre. A iniciativa também contempla Colômbia, México, Peru, Argentina e Chile. As reservas podem ser feitas pelo aplicativo móvel da WeWork ou pelo site da empresa. A contratação permite pagar apenas pelo período utilizado. No caso das mesas de trabalho, a reserva por um dia dá acesso às áreas comuns da unidade, incluindo cabines privativas e espaços de descanso. Já as salas de reunião podem ser alugadas por hora. O lançamento ocorre em um cenário de mudanças na relação dos profissionais com o escritório. Segundo o estudo “A experiência laboral de 2026 no Brasil”, realizado pela WeWork em parceria com a Offerwise, 79% dos entrevistados afirmam que a ida ao escritório é uma exigência do empregador, e não uma escolha. Se pudessem decidir, apenas 42% optariam pelo trabalho presencial. “As empresas continuam precisando de espaço e demandam cada vez mais. O que mudou foi a maneira de usá-lo”, afirma Claudio Hidalgo, presidente da WeWork para a América Latina. Com o On Demand, a WeWork busca atender profissionais que precisam de um local de trabalho ou de reunião pontualmente, sem assumir compromissos de longo prazo. A plataforma também permite que usuários brasileiros reservem espaços em mais de 300 unidades da empresa, distribuídas por 70 cidades no mundo. A companhia mantém 69 unidades na América Latina. Segundo Hidalgo, a operação regional é lucrativa em todas as localidades há mais de um ano, com taxa de ocupação superior a 80%. Para o executivo, a flexibilização do trabalho também exige uma revisão do papel do escritório nas empresas. A tendência, segundo ele, é substituir a presença baseada no controle por uma dinâmica orientada a objetivos e confiança, na qual o deslocamento até o ambiente corporativo esteja associado a uma finalidade específica. A Wework afirma que seguirá concentrada na consolidação da operação e na rentabilidade do negócio na região, ampliando modelos de uso flexível dos espaços. articles.title: California Pizza Kitchen to Deploy Automated Kiosks to U.S. Military Bases
articles.titleKo: California Pizza Kitchen to Deploy Automated Kiosks to U.S. Military Bases
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . The military initiative builds on CPK’s broader automated retail strategy to implement and operate up to 1,000 automated retail machines nationwide over the next three years. In recognition of the men and women who serve our nation, California Pizza Kitchen (CPK) today announced an initiative to bring its signature California-inspired pizzas directly to U.S. military installations through a phased deployment of automated pizza kiosks. Partnering with Ranger Group and its CEO, U.S. Army Ranger veteran, Mark “Ranger” Jones, CPK plans to roll out hundreds of automated pizza machines across installations serving the U.S. Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps and U.S. Coast Guard, with planned placements at bases across America. The military initiative builds on CPK’s broader automated retail strategy to implement and operate up to 1,000 automated retail machines nationwide over the next three years, bringing restaurant-quality CPK favorites to airports, universities, hospitals and other high-traffic locations. The machines use Turbo-chef powered cooking and touch-screen technology to deliver a freshly baked CPK pizza in as little as 90 seconds. The deployment to U.S. military installations extends that same on-demand, restaurant-quality experience to the service members who work and train on base. The initiative expands CPK’s presence beyond traditional restaurants and grocery store shelves, bringing the brand’s distinctive approach to pizza directly to the places where America’s military personnel work and train. Designed to provide convenient access to hot and fresh pizza, the machines will offer service members a high-quality and convenient meal option while on base or at sea. “As a veteran myself, I’m personally proud to bring our restaurant-quality pizzas directly to the places where our service members work and train,” said Michael Beacham, President of California Pizza Kitchen Global. “This initiative is both an expression of our gratitude and a meaningful step forward in our mission to make the California Pizza Kitchen experience more accessible wherever people are.” Bringing Great Pizza Closer to Those Who Serve The military deployment program combines CPK’s recognized brand and culinary heritage with automated foodservice technology designed for high-demand environments. Ranger Group will work with CPK and military stakeholders to coordinate and facilitate the phased deployment, including installation logistics and ongoing operational support. “As a former U.S. Army Ranger, I know how much a great meal made with quality ingredients can mean to service members and their families after a long day of training or duty,” said Mark “Ranger” Jones, CEO of Ranger Group. “This partnership with California Pizza Kitchen is personal to me. We are bringing an iconic American brand to the places where military personnel and their families work, live and serve, giving them convenient access to quality food and showing our appreciation for their sacrifice. It is an honor to help make this happen.” A New Frontier for California Pizza Kitchen The military initiative is part of CPK’s broader strategy to expand access to its signature pizzas through innovative, non-traditional dining formats. By extending the brand into locations where traditional restaurant development may not be practical, CPK is creating new opportunities to serve consumers in workplaces, transportation hubs, educational institutions and other high-traffic environments. The military rollout will proceed in phases, beginning with domestic installations and potentially expanding to additional military locations, including overseas facilities, in the future. For CPK, the initiative reflects a simple belief: great pizza should be available wherever people live, work and gather — including the men and women who dedicate their lives to serving the United State

articles.title: Vendas do varejo caem 4% em outubro e registram pior resultado para o mês desde 2023
articles.titleKo: Vendas do varejo caem 4% em outubro e registram pior resultado para o mês desde 2023
articles.originalSummary: As vendas do varejo brasileiro caíram 4,0% em outubro de 2026 em relação ao mesmo mês de 2025, já descontada a inflação, segundo o Índice Cielo do Varejo Ampliado (ICVA). O resultado representa o pior desempenho para o mês de outubro desde 2023, quando a retração foi de 4,1%. O faturamento real ficou abaixo do registrado um ano antes pelo 17º mês consecutivo. A sequência de recuos começou em junho de 2025, mas perdeu intensidade em relação a setembro , quando as vendas ficaram 4,2% abaixo do nível de um ano antes. Duráveis e serviços têm as maiores quedas As vendas de bens duráveis e semiduráveis recuaram 8,9%. Óticas e joalherias e lojas de materiais de construção estiveram entre os segmentos que mais contribuíram para o resultado negativo. Em serviços , a retração foi de 8,5%, puxada principalmente por turismo e transporte, além de autopeças e serviços automotivos. Os bens não duráveis registraram a menor retração entre os três grupos, de 0,7%. Nessa categoria, o varejo alimentício especializado se destacou pelo desempenho positivo, enquanto livrarias, papelarias e afins deram a maior contribuição negativa. Centro-Oeste tem maior retração regional O faturamento real recuou nas cinco regiões do País. O Centro-Oeste teve a maior retração (5,4%), seguido pelo Sudeste (5,2%), Nordeste (3,5%) e Norte (2,3%). O Sul registrou a menor queda (0,8%), com crescimento no Paraná (0,7%) e em Santa Catarina (0,1%). Entre os Estados, o Amapá liderou as altas (2,4%), seguido por Rondônia (1,2%) e Acre (0,8%). Na outra ponta, São Paulo teve o pior resultado, com recuo de 6,4%, à frente de Goiás (6,3%) e Rio Grande do Norte (5,6%). Varejo físico e e-commerce têm resultados distintos O faturamento nominal do e-commerce recuou 0,5% em outubro de 2026, na comparação com o mesmo mês de 2025, segundo o ICVA. No varejo físico, as vendas cresceram 1,9% no período. Os dois resultados refletem a variação da receita de vendas antes do desconto da inflação. O IPCA-15 subiu 0,3% em outubro, abaixo da alta de 0,7% registrada em setembro. Em 12 meses, o indicador acumulou avanço de 4,6%. Dos nove grupos pesquisados, oito apresentaram aumento de preços no período. Alimentação e bebidas registrou a maior alta entre os grupos, de 0,9%, acelerando ante 0,4% em setembro. A alimentação no domicílio subiu 1,0%, também acima da variação de 0,4% do mês anterior. Já a alimentação fora do domicílio aumentou 0,6%, ante 0,4% em setembro. Em Transportes, os preços avançaram 0,1%, com alta de 1,2% nos combustíveis, enquanto as passagens aéreas recuaram 9,2%. Habitação teve queda de 0,1%, influenciada pela redução de 0,9% na energia elétrica residencial, associada à mudança para a bandeira tarifária verde. Assim, embora a inflação geral tenha desacelerado em outubro, a alta mais forte dos alimentos pode ter pressionado o orçamento das famílias. O contexto ajuda a explicar o contraste entre o crescimento nominal de 1,3% e a queda real de 4,0% do ICVA, mas não permite atribuir o desempenho do varejo exclusivamente à inflação. articles.title: Temu e Correios firmam acordo para ampliar operações logísticas no Brasil
articles.titleKo: Temu e Correios firmam acordo para ampliar operações logísticas no Brasil
articles.originalSummary: A Temu assinou um Memorando de Entendimento (MOU, na sigla em inglês) com os Correios para ampliar a cooperação em logística e comércio eletrônico no Brasil. O acordo prevê a avaliação de novas soluções de entrega e serviços logísticos para empresas brasileiras que comercializam produtos por meio do Programa de Vendedores Locais da plataforma. A parceria poderá utilizar a capilaridade e a infraestrutura dos Correios para ampliar as opções de entrega e oferecer suporte aos vendedores que atuam no marketplace. A iniciativa também faz parte da estratégia da Temu de fortalecer sua operação no Brasil por meio de parcerias com empresas e prestadores de serviços locais. “Construir relações sólidas com parceiros locais é uma parte importante da nossa atuação nos mercados em que estamos presentes. A parceria com os Correios busca facilitar a experiência logística dos consumidores e, ao mesmo tempo, oferecer mais suporte aos vendedores locais para que possam expandir seus negócios online”, afirma a empresa. Segundo Emmanoel Schmidt Rondon, presidente dos Correios , o acordo abre novas oportunidades de negócios e reforça o papel da estatal como parceira logística do comércio eletrônico no País. A colaboração combina a presença nacional da empresa com a atuação da plataforma no mercado digital. A Temu iniciou suas operações no Brasil em junho de 2024 e lançou, em setembro de 2025, seu Programa de Vendedores Locais, que permite a empresas brasileiras utilizar a plataforma como canal de vendas para alcançar consumidores e ampliar sua presença no comércio eletrônico. Com a aproximação, a empresa busca fortalecer a estrutura logística oferecida aos vendedores brasileiros à medida que expandem seus negócios no ambiente digital. articles.title: Produção de veículos no Brasil sobe 2,7% em outubro ante outubro de 2025, diz Anfavea
articles.titleKo: Produção de veículos no Brasil sobe 2,7% em outubro ante outubro de 2025, diz Anfavea
articles.originalSummary: A produção de veículos subiu 2,7% em outubro, ante o mesmo mês de 2025, refletindo a perda de tração das vendas no mercado doméstico e um resultado considerado preocupante das exportações. No total, foram montadas 254,5 mil unidades, entre carros de passeio, utilitários leves, caminhões e ônibus. O volume ficou 5,1% abaixo do registrado em setembro. Divulgado nesta quarta-feira, 11, pela Anfavea , a entidade que representa as montadoras, o balanço mostra que, desde o início do ano, foram montados 2,42 milhões de veículos, o que corresponde a um crescimento de 8% ante os dez primeiros meses do ano passado. Vendas de veículos perdem fôlego Em outubro, as vendas de veículos no Brasil somaram 265,5 mil unidades. Na comparação com o mesmo mês de 2025, o crescimento foi de 1,8%. Ante setembro, as vendas encolheram 5,6%, indicando perda de fôlego do mercado. Exportações de veículos recuam quase 30% Já as exportações, de 29,1 mil veículos em outubro, recuaram 28,3% na comparação com o mesmo mês de 2025. Na margem, ou seja, ante setembro, os embarques recuaram 26,9%. No acumulado desde janeiro, as exportações agora recuam 23,5%, somando 363,1 mil veículos em dez meses. Perda de espaço no mercado externo A Anfavea classificou como “preocupantes” os resultados no comércio exterior, apontando perda de participação das montadoras do Brasil em mercados vizinhos, sobretudo para produtos provenientes da Ásia e do México. Além disso, a Argentina, principal destino das exportações brasileiras, também enfrenta retração do mercado interno, o que afeta diretamente os embarques nacionais de automóveis. Montadoras ampliam quadro de funcionários O balanço da entidade mostra ainda que as montadoras abriram 467 vagas de trabalho em outubro. As fábricas de veículos agora empregam 116,3 mil pessoas. Com informação do Estadão de Conteúdo (Daniel Tozzi e Eduardo Laguna).
