articles.title: How Restaurants Can Capture the Market While Competitors Give Up Ground
articles.titleKo: How Restaurants Can Capture the Market While Competitors Give Up Ground
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . When other restaurants in the area go quiet on local marketing channels, two things happen simultaneously: ad costs soften, and noise drops. Restaurant operators reported a net decline in customer traffic in 19 of the last 20 months, according to the National Restaurant Association . The same trend is reflected in the slowdown of new jobs in restaurants and bars from 31,500 in August to just 11,000 in September . Such indicators, together with persistent political and economic uncertainty, make the instinct to batten down the hatches, trim the marketing budget and wait out the storm fully understandable. It’s also one of the most expensive decisions a restaurant can make. When Harvard Business Review researchers studied 4,700 public companies across three recessions, only about 9 percent emerged outperforming their rivals by at least 10 percent in sales and profit growth. The approach most likely to land a company in that group was not being conservative. It was pairing operational discipline with greater investment in marketing and development. This is the same principle that led Harvard Professor John Quelch to write in 2008 that maintaining marketing spend through the recession could increase market share at lower costs than otherwise possible. Here are the investments that restaurant operators can prioritize to take advantage when competitors go on the defensive. 1. Fill the Channels Competitors Abandon When other restaurants in the area go quiet on local marketing channels, two things happen simultaneously: ad costs soften, and noise drops. An operator that merely holds marketing spend in that moment can purchase more representation on TV, social platforms, maps, radio and the like at a time when the total volume of ads is decreasing. Their share of voice (SOV), or their percentage of the market’s total advertising noise, increases without the need for any additional investment. And the gap between SOV and share of market, known as excess share of voice (ESOV), just so happens to be one of the strongest predictors of long-term share growth. An analysis of the IPA Effectiveness Databank covering the 2008–09 recession found that brands with ESOV above 8 points saw 4.5 times the annual market share growth of brands with zero or negative ESOV. Restaurants that can afford to increase their spending during a slowdown can maximize the SOV they win during the discount and the advantage they’ll have when demand returns. 2. Break Into New Markets The advantages of discounted SOV don’t have to end with a restaurant’s traditional target audience. The same equation that lets restaurants claim a bigger share of their primary market also lowers the cost of entry in adjacent markets. When competitors stop advertising their offerings in catering, private events or a neighboring suburb, establishing a new name in those spaces becomes significantly cheaper. Expansions that were too high-risk in a strong market start to make sense under these conditions. Careful digital marketing practice reduces the downside further by allowing operators to test new audiences at a minimal upfront cost before pursuing the ones that show positive feedback. 3. Keep the Test Kitchen Running Menu and concept development run on long lead times. A new prototype, a beverage program or a retooled menu can take many months to move from the test kitchen to the dining room, so cuts made today create gaps that surface in what may be a very different market. An operator who keeps development running while competitors shut down the test kitchen will be able to debut their innovations in a relatively unsaturated and potentially high-demand environment. By the time the competitors start investing in their own development programs once more, they’ll find themselves a full cycle behind. As always, development should be informed by guest data. articles.title: Reforma tributária: governo apresentará texto para facilitar adaptação
articles.titleKo: Reforma tributária: governo apresentará texto para facilitar adaptação
articles.originalSummary: O governo federal vai encaminhar ao Congresso Nacional uma proposta para criar uma regra de transição na cobrança da Contribuição sobre Bens e Serviços (CBS), novo tributo federal da reforma tributária. A medida permitirá que as empresas façam um cálculo estimado do imposto nos primeiros meses de vigência do sistema e realizem ajustes posteriormente, reduzindo dificuldades na adaptação às novas regras. O anúncio foi feito nesta quarta-feira, 11, pelo secretário especial da Receita Federal , Robinson Barreirinhas, durante coletiva de imprensa sobre o Programa de Conformidade da Reforma Tributária, no Ministério da Fazenda. Segundo o secretário, a proposta busca dar mais segurança aos contribuintes durante a migração para o modelo de crédito vinculado ao pagamento e para o sistema de split payment – mecanismo que vincula o aproveitamento de créditos tributários ao efetivo recolhimento do tributo na operação. “Para tranquilizar e ter certeza absoluta de que ninguém vai ter problema nessa transição, nós vamos propor para o Congresso Nacional uma regra opcional”, afirmou o secretário. Pela sistemática apresentada, as empresas passarão a emitir documentos fiscais dentro das novas regras a partir de janeiro de 2027. Na primeira apuração da CBS, prevista para fevereiro, o contribuinte poderá calcular o tributo com base em uma estimativa dos créditos a que terá direito. Eventuais diferenças serão ajustadas na apuração do mês seguinte. De acordo com Barreirinhas, o mecanismo funcionará como uma alternativa para contribuintes que ainda estejam se adaptando às novas regras de aproveitamento de créditos tributários. “Até que o split payment esteja totalmente implementado, principalmente nas operações entre empresas, esse modelo pode funcionar como mecanismo de transição”, disse. Regulamentação Ao defender a entrada em vigor da reforma dentro do cronograma previsto pelo governo, o secretário afirmou que a regulamentação vem sendo construída em diálogo com Estados, municípios, entidades empresariais e profissionais da contabilidade. Segundo ele, a primeira versão do regulamento recebeu quase 5 mil sugestões de aperfeiçoamento, que foram analisadas pela Receita Federal e pelos demais órgãos envolvidos na implementação. “Todas as decisões da reforma precisam ser tomadas por consenso. Isso demanda um diálogo institucional muito forte”, afirmou. Barreirinhas informou que uma nova versão do regulamento deverá ser publicada nos próximos dias e destacou que o trabalho continuará após a publicação das normas complementares previstas para este ano. Créditos para investimentos O secretário também destacou os efeitos que a reforma poderá trazer para os investimentos produtivos . Pelas novas regras, os tributos pagos na compra de máquinas, equipamentos, imóveis e outros bens de capital passarão a gerar créditos imediatos. Hoje, em muitos casos, esses créditos são recuperados gradualmente ao longo de vários anos. “Uma indústria que faça um grande investimento, por exemplo em imóveis ou equipamentos, pode ficar meses ou até anos sem pagar CBS”, afirmou. Segundo Barreirinhas, isso ocorrerá porque os investimentos passarão a gerar créditos tributários de aproveitamento imediato, reduzindo o custo dos investimentos e a necessidade de manter recursos imobilizados à espera da recuperação tributária. O secretário também destacou a previsão de ressarcimento mais rápido dos créditos acumulados: “O ressarcimento, que hoje em dia demora, às vezes, até um ano para ser processado, vai ocorrer em 30, 60 ou 90 dias, a depender da conformidade desse empresário.” Ele lembrou ainda que o Imposto sobre Produtos Industrializados (IPI) terá alíquota zerada para a maior parte dos produtos, permanecendo apenas em situações específicas destinadas à preservação da competitividade da Zona Franca de Manaus. PAR Technology Corporation, a leading technology provider powering multi-unit operators across restaurant, retail, and large-scale commerce, today announced that FSC Franchise Co. (“FSC”), franchisor of Beef ‘O’ Brady’s, The Brass Tap, and Newk’s Eatery, has selected PAR Punchh, PAR Ordering, and PAR Catering as its recommended solutions across its restaurant brands, creating a more connected technology foundation with PAR Intelligence, PAR’s agentic intelligence layer, built in. The announcement builds on the brands’ existing relationships with PAR Technology and represents the next step in FSC’s strategy to create a more connected technology foundation across its portfolio. By expanding its use of PAR solutions, FSC aims to better connect guest engagement, digital ordering, and catering while creating opportunities for more actionable insights into guest behavior and restaurant operations. “We’ve built Beef ’O’ Brady’s, The Brass Tap, and Newk’s Eatery into three distinct brands, each with its own identity and loyal following. But our franchisees shouldn’t have to navigate three different technology environments to operate their restaurants,” said Jason Saposnik, Vice President of Information Technology at FSC Franchise Co. “Standardizing on PAR gives our brands a stronger, more connected foundation for guest engagement, ordering, and catering. It helps simplify the technology experience for our franchisees and gives us the tools to continue improving how we serve our guests. PAR is the right partner at the right time for where FSC is headed.” “FSC has built three distinct brands with real followings, and the technology behind them should reflect that investment,” said Savneet Singh, CEO of PAR Technology. “When ordering, catering, and loyalty all run on the same platform across every brand, franchisees stop managing systems and start running restaurants. Every transaction feeds the same intelligence layer, every guest interaction gets smarter, and every new feature reaches all three brands at the same time. That’s what a unified platform means in practice, and that’s why brands are choosing to consolidate on PAR.” The transition will take place through a phased rollout beginning in early 2027, with each brand building on its existing PAR technology footprint: Newk’s Eatery, a fast-casual restaurant brand with more than 100 locations across 13 states, is already a PAR Punchh and PAR OPS customer. articles.titleKo: Sexy Fish Miami Extends Bubbice Ice Cream Collaboration Through December
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Following its October debut, Sexy Fish Miami is extending its popular collaboration with Bubbice, the Miami-based dessert concept known for transforming fresh ingredients and sweet treats into made-to-order ice cream. The limited-time activation will continue every Sunday through December 27, 2026, as part of the restaurant’s Sexy Sunday Brunch. At Sexy Fish’s iconic Candy Corner , guests can customize their own frozen treats using Bubbice’s signature flash-freezing technique. Starting with a rich vanilla or coconut cream ice cream base, guests can choose from an assortment of house-made desserts, delicate pastries and nostalgic sweets, including fresh strawberries, chocolate chips, cookie crumbles, brownies, cheesecake and colorful candies. The Bubbice team then flash-freezes each combination before their eyes, serving the finished ice cream in a custom Sexy Fish x Bubbice cup. “There’s something nostalgic about visiting a candy bar, picking out your favorite childhood sweets and watching them transform into a personalized ice cream creation,” said Alexa Schifman, Head of Marketing at Sexy Fish Miami. “Our collaboration with Bubbice brings out the inner child in all of us, creating a playful, family-friendly experience that celebrates the joy of indulging in something sweet and making memories together.” Sexy Sunday Brunch is offered every Sunday from 11:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., starting at $78 per person. The experience features Japanese-inspired cuisine, live entertainment and tableside service, along with a Culinary Showcase Station offering premium seafood, sushi, sashimi and tartares. Guests can also enhance their brunch experience with champagne packages, handcrafted cocktails and a selection of fine wines, available for an additional charge. Sexy Fish Miami is located at 1001 S. Miami Ave. in Brickell. Reservations can be made at sexyfishmiami.com or by calling 305.889.7888. articles.title: Krispy Kreme’s Leaner Business Delivers Results
articles.titleKo: Krispy Kreme’s Leaner Business Delivers Results
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Global systemwide sales increased 1 percent during the quarter. Krispy Kreme is discovering that selling more doughnuts doesn’t necessarily require putting them in more places. Sometimes, the better opportunity comes from making sure customers can find them in the right places. A little more than a year after launching a sweeping restructuring effort, the company is seeing favorable results from its focus on profitable distribution, operational efficiency, and franchise-led expansion. U.S. fresh delivery returned to growth in the third quarter, margins improved, and the company raised its full-year revenue outlook. The progress comes after Krispy Kreme spent much of the past year reworking its business model, including exiting approximately 1,500 underperforming fresh delivery locations, refranchising operations in Japan and the Western U.S., and reducing capital expenditures. CEO Josh Charlesworth says the company is now better positioned to expand without taking on the same level of financial obligations that accompanied its previous growth plans. “Unlocking that demand continues to be our priority as we pursue profitable U.S. expansion and capital-light international franchise growth,” Charlesworth said during the company’s third-quarter earnings call. Global systemwide sales increased 1 percent during the quarter, and Krispy Kreme continues to expect growth of 2 to 4 percent for the full year, bringing systemwide sales above $2 billion. Net revenue declined 12 percent to $328.8 million, primarily because of the refranchising transactions in Japan and the Western U.S. Organic revenue, which excludes the effects of refranchising and foreign exchange, was essentially flat. Adjusted EBITDA fell 13.1 percent to $35.3 million, largely because the company recorded a $9.3 million cybersecurity insurance recovery in the prior-year period. Excluding that one-time benefit, adjusted EBITDA increased 13 percent, and adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 240 basis points to 10.7 percent. The improvement was pronounced in the U.S., where organic revenue increased 0.9 percent, supported by fresh delivery and digital sales. Adjusted EBITDA in the segment reached $13.9 million, representing an 18 percent increase when excluding the prior-year insurance recovery. On the same basis, adjusted EBITDA margin improved 320 basis points. Much of that progress stems from changes to Krispy Kreme’s production and distribution network. The company has improved production planning, adjusted labor deployment, streamlined hub operations, and made delivery routes more efficient. Those efforts have increased sales per production hub by more than 10 percent year-over-year, allowing Krispy Kreme to make better use of its existing infrastructure. The adjustments are important to the company’s fresh delivery business, which supplies doughnuts to grocery stores, mass retailers, convenience stores, and club stores. Last year, Krispy Kreme determined that parts of its distribution network were not producing sufficient returns. The company responded by eliminating approximately 1,500 underperforming doors and shifting its attention toward higher-volume retail partners. Krispy Kreme added 715 net new fresh delivery doors year-over-year, bringing its U.S. network to approximately 7,700 locations, including franchise operations. The newer doors have higher average weekly sales than the locations the company previously exited. Fresh delivery returned to growth during the third quarter. The company sees additional opportunities with Walmart and Target, where it currently distributes doughnuts in fewer than half of each retailer’s U.S. stores. articles.title: Dave’s Hot Chicken Introduces its Hottest Spice Level Ever
articles.titleKo: Dave’s Hot Chicken Introduces its Hottest Spice Level Ever
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Coming in at 2.7 million Scoville units, Pepper X peppers were developed by PuckerButt Pepper Company, founded by American chili pepper breeder “Smokin’ Ed” Currie. Think you know Dave’s sweat-inducing Reaper pepper spice level? Meet Pepper X. Dave’s Hot Chicken is taking its signature heat to the next level with a limited-time offering featuring a spice blend made with Pepper X, recognized by Guinness World Records as the world’s hottest chili pepper. Available now for a limited time at Dave’s Hot Chicken locations nationwide, Pepper X gives heat fans a new way to experience Dave’s, while its legendary Reaper remains a permanent part of the menu. Coming in at 2.7 million Scoville units, Pepper X peppers were developed by PuckerButt Pepper Company, founded by American chili pepper breeder “Smokin’ Ed” Currie. Currie, the company’s founder and president, created both the Carolina Reaper, a former Guinness World Records titleholder, and Pepper X, which claimed the title in 2023. “From the Carolina Reaper to Pepper X, we’ve always pushed the limits of heat, and Dave’s is bringing that spirit to its hot chicken,” said “Smokin’ Ed” Currie, founder and president of PuckerButt Pepper Company. “Reaper fans already know Dave’s doesn’t mess around when it comes to heat and Pepper X takes it even further. As we always say, ‘If your butt don’t pucker, it ain’t a PuckerButt pepper.’” The Pepper X spice blend was developed in partnership with Chef Dave Kopushyan, co-founder of Dave’s Hot Chicken, whose culinary background includes working in Thomas Keller’s restaurant group. Drawing on that experience, Chef Dave worked with an extensive range of spices to build a flavor profile that goes beyond heat alone. That thoughtful approach to seasoning has been part of Dave’s DNA from the beginning, and the Pepper X spice blend is, by far, the brand’s hottest offering yet. “Reaper has become a legendary part of the Dave’s experience, and it isn’t going anywhere,” said Jim Bitticks, CEO of Dave’s Hot Chicken. “But Pepper X gives our biggest heat fans an even greater challenge for a limited time. Whether you’re here for the burn or you’re happy with our Not Hot spice level, there’s a Dave’s experience for you.” Pepper X is a temporary addition to Dave’s heat lineup. Guests can continue to choose from the brand’s seven core spice levels, starting at Not Hot and building to Reaper, so everyone can find their own favorite level of heat. The new Pepper X spice level can be ordered with Dave’s Tenders, Sliders, Bites and even Hot Mozz. The brand’s recently introduced, over-sized XL Slider also comes with any heat level you desire. For more information and to find a nearby restaurant, visit www.daveshotchicken.com or follow @daveshotchicken on social media. articles.title: Nova plataforma do MDIC identificará oportunidades de comércio com UE
articles.titleKo: Nova plataforma do MDIC identificará oportunidades de comércio com UE
articles.originalSummary: O Ministério do Desenvolvimento, Indústria, Comércio e Serviços (MDIC) lançou nesta terça-feira, 10, duas plataformas digitais para facilitar o comércio exterior e a entrada de investimentos no País. A Conecta Brasil–União Europeia (UE) reúne informações para empresas interessadas em acessar o mercado europeu. A pasta também lançou a segunda fase da Janela Única de Investimentos, com novos serviços para orientar investidores estrangeiros no Brasil. As iniciativas foram desenvolvidas em parceria com o Banco Interamericano de Desenvolvimento (BID) e buscam reduzir a burocracia, centralizar informações e ampliar as oportunidades para empresas brasileiras e investidores internacionais. Acesso à Europa Oferecida no Portal Gov.br, a plataforma Conecta Brasil–UE foi criada para apoiar principalmente micro, pequenas e médias empresas na identificação de oportunidades comerciais abertas pelo Acordo Mercosul–União Europeia. A ferramenta transforma o conteúdo do acordo e seus anexos jurídicos em informações práticas sobre: Tarifas e cotas de importação; Cronogramas de redução tarifária; Regras de origem dos produtos; Exportação de bens e serviços; Compras governamentais e investimentos; Propriedade intelectual; Requisitos regulatórios e ambientais da União Europeia; Programas de apoio à internacionalização. A plataforma também conta com a ExportAI, solução de Inteligência Artificial que usa o próprio texto do acordo como base para responder a dúvidas sobre tarifas preferenciais, regras de origem e condições para acesso aos benefícios comerciais. A União Europeia reúne 27 países e cerca de 450 milhões de consumidores. O bloco é o segundo maior parceiro comercial do Brasil e representa um dos principais mercados para a diversificação das exportações brasileiras. Novos serviços Em funcionamento desde março, a Janela Única de Investimentos recebeu um segundo módulo com novas funcionalidades para facilitar o planejamento e a execução de negócios por investidores estrangeiros. Uma das novidades é a Área do Investidor, que permite acompanhar os serviços pedidos pela plataforma. Também foram incluídos caminhos para iniciar a emissão de Cadastro de Pessoa Física (CPF) de cidadãos estrangeiros e de Cadastro Nacional de Pessoas Jurídicas (CNPJ) para empresas estrangeiras. Entre os serviços e funcionalidades incorporados estão: Acompanhamento de pedidos na Área do Investidor; Integração do sistema de Ex-tarifário; Login Único Gov.br; Orientações para emissão de CPF e CNPJ de estrangeiros; Registro de fertilizantes; Registro de marcas, patentes e contratos de transferência de tecnologia; Informações sobre remessas de capital; Serviços de apoio ao investidor oferecidos pela ApexBrasil; Orientações para obtenção de visto temporário de trabalho; Guias sobre incentivos fiscais e isenções tarifárias. A plataforma também reúne informações sobre oportunidades de mercado, tendências e setores prioritários, além de permitir que investidores acessem serviços e parceiros para estruturar seus projetos no país. Investimentos estrangeiros O lançamento da nova etapa ocorre em um período de entrada expressiva de capital estrangeiro no Brasil . Segundo dados do Banco Central citados pelo MDIC, o Investimento Estrangeiro Direto (IED) alcançou US$ 85 bilhões em 2025, maior resultado dos últimos dez anos. Em 2026, até setembro, o saldo chegou a US$ 75,7 bilhões. O IED corresponde a investimentos relacionados à participação em atividades econômicas no país. Próximas etapas Instituída pelo Decreto 12.615/2025 , a Janela Única de Investimentos foi desenvolvida pelo MDIC em parceria com o BID. A proposta é integrar sistemas governamentais e serviços do setor privado para reduzir etapas e facilitar operações. O governo prevê iniciar, em 2027, o desenvolvimento do terceiro módulo da plataforma. A próxima fase deverá ampliar a integração entre sistemas públicos, incorporar novos serviços e aperfeiçoar as funcionalidades existentes, com atenção a setores estratégicos da economi

The chocolatey, cookie-crunch center has been a fan favorite since the 1950s and continues to create lasting memories for ice cream lovers of all ages. Carvel, the iconic ice cream cake brand, announced that its fan-favorite Fudge & Crunch Cake is now available year-round at select retailers. Previously a limited-time offering, the nostalgic favorite is now a permanent part of the lineup, giving families more opportunities to enjoy one of Carvel’s most beloved cakes whenever the occasion arises. Featuring layers of chocolate and vanilla ice cream surrounding Carvel’s signature Crunchies, the Fudge & Crunch Cake delivers the unmistakable flavor and texture that have made Carvel a household name for decades. The chocolatey, cookie-crunch center has been a fan favorite since the 1950s and continues to create lasting memories for ice cream lovers of all ages. “The Fudge & Crunch Cake has everything Carvel fans love: chocolate and vanilla ice cream, our signature Crunchies, fudge topping and plenty of nostalgia,” said Kim Mrowczynski, Rich Products’ Brand Marketing Manager, Ice Cream Cakes. “Making it available year-round means there’s always a Carvel cake ready for birthdays, holidays or simply making an everyday moment a little more special.” The return of the Fudge & Crunch Cake comes at a time when consumers are increasingly gravitating toward trusted favorites and established brands. While food trends continue to evolve, classic desserts with strong emotional connections remain a staple for families looking to celebrate life’s big and small moments. Ready to serve straight from the freezer, the Fudge & Crunch Cake makes it easy to have a celebration-worthy dessert on hand for family gatherings, special occasions, or to satisfy spontaneous sweet cravings. “The magic of Carvel has always been bringing people together through memorable desserts,” added Mrowczynski. “We’re thrilled that fans no longer have to wait for a seasonal release to enjoy the cake they love.” Consumers can find the Carvel Fudge & Crunch Cake at participating retail locations nationwide. Bahama Buck’s Franchise Corporation will celebrate the 20th anniversary of its annual Free Sno Day on Tuesday, December 1, inviting guests at participating locations nationwide to enjoy a complimentary Sno (up to 12 oz.) as the brand kicks off the holiday season. The longstanding holiday tradition has grown into a nationwide community event. In 2025, Bahama Buck’s participating shops distributed 68,843 free Sno products, representing an estimated retail value of approximately $316,000 in product value, across 106 locations. The 2026 celebration is expected to bring together a similar number of participating shops, continuing a tradition that has become a meaningful part of the holiday season for guests and franchise communities. For some families, Free Sno Day marks the official beginning of the holidays. “One family in Lubbock, TX recently shared that Free Sno Day is how they kick off the holiday season every year. They shared, ‘The holidays can’t start without Free Sno Day!’ Stories like that remind us why this tradition means so much to our Bahama Buck’s family,” said Blake Buchanan, founder and CEO of Bahama Buck’s Franchise Corporation. “Celebrating 20 years of Free Sno Day is a special milestone. What started as a way to give back has become a tradition that brings communities together and helps us Bless our Guests in a meaningful way. We’re grateful to everyone who has made Free Sno Day part of their holiday season.” Guests are invited to visit participating Bahama Buck’s locations on Tuesday, December 1, to enjoy a free Sno and celebrate two decades of this holiday tradition. articles.title: Correios: campanha já recebeu mais de 100 mil cartas para o papai noel
articles.titleKo: Correios: campanha já recebeu mais de 100 mil cartas para o papai noel
articles.originalSummary: Ainda falta um mês e meio para o Natal, mas o Papai Noel dos Correios já está a todo vapor para garantir o presente de milhares de crianças em todo o Brasil. Em 2025, 305 mil cartas foram adotadas. Em 2026, mais de 100 mil cartas já foram entregues e a meta é atender 100% dos pedidos natalinos. Todo ano os Correios recebem cartas de crianças em situação de vulnerabilidade e de escolas públicas até o 5º ano do ensino fundamental, que escrevem ao Papai Noel seus desejos de Natal. Essas cartas são então selecionadas conforme os critérios da campanha, e depois disponibilizadas para pessoas que queiram fazer as doações. Quem quiser ajudar pode escolher uma carta nos pontos de adoção ou no Blog Noel. No site é possível ler a cartinha, que quase sempre é escrita a mão, mas sem a identificação da criança. É possível escolher pela idade da criança e pelo tipo de presente, que vão desde carrinhos, bonecas e bicicletas até materiais escolares. O doador, então, providencia o presente e o entrega, embalado e identificado, em um dos pontos participantes da campanha. As datas, locais e horários dos pontos de adoção e entrega, em cada estado, também estão disponíveis no Blog Noel . Como enviar uma carta As cartinhas devem ser escritas a mão e levadas pessoalmente a uma das agências dos Correios ou enviadas, depois de escaneadas, ao Blog Noel. No cadastramento é necessário informar o CPF da criança. O prazo para envio na maioria do país é até 30 de novembro, mas alguns lugares termina antes, como na Grande São Paulo, que vai até 13 de novembro. Mais informações estão no Blog do Noel. O Papai Noel dos Correios foi criado em 1989 pelos próprios funcionários dos Correios, que viam chegar à empresa cartinhas destinadas ao bom velhinho. Muitas vinham sem endereço, ou com destino ao Polo Norte. Os funcionários começaram então a escolher algumas cartas e presentear as crianças. Com o aumento no número de pedidos, os Correios decidiram, em 1997, abrir a campanha para o público geral. Desde então, segundo a empresa, mais de 7 mil cartas foram adotadas, ou seja, mais de sete mil crianças foram presenteadas. Com informações de Agência Brasil. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Wetzel’s Pretzels (Wetzel’s), the iconic brand known for its fresh, hand-rolled pretzels, has opened two new bakeries inside Walmart Supercenters in Hammond, Indiana. The openings build on Wetzel’s growing partnership with Walmart, the world’s largest retailer, as the brand continues expanding its store-within-a-store model. The new bakeries are located at 7850 Cabela Dr. and 1100 5th Ave. The new bakeries highlight Wetzel’s continued development into high-traffic retail environments, including Walmart Supercenters. Both locations will bring more flavor to the community with delicious snacks and refreshing drinks, a perfect pairing for any shopping trip. Veteran franchisee Mike Alkaki, who grew up in Northwest Indiana, will own and operate both new bakeries, marking his fourth and fifth Wetzel’s Pretzels locations. Additionally, Alkaki currently operates two bakeries at Orland Square Mall and another inside a Walmart in Romeoville, Illinois, in Chicago’s southwest suburbs. Drawing on his background in retail investment brokerage, Alkaki plans to reinvest in the community and expand his Wetzel’s portfolio throughout the Greater Chicago and Northern Indiana markets. “I’m proud to open two Wetzel’s Pretzels locations in Hammond and give back to the community that shaped who I am today. Continuing my partnership with Wetzel’s is a great honor, and the support I received makes it possible to open both stores in the same month,” said Alkaki. “I’m looking forward to serving the community and sharing the hospitality and craveable snacks our guests know and love.” The Hammond Walmart locations showcase the flexibility of the Wetzel’s concept, offering a buildout design that is adaptable to the retailer’s footprint. As the brand continues expanding in non-traditional spaces, its store-within-a-store model proves ideal for integration into Walmart locations, with further growth planned across the nation. “We’re excited to see Mike continue growing his Wetzel’s portfolio with these two new Walmart locations in Hammond,” said Eric Weigel, Brand Leader at Wetzel’s Pretzels. “Our growing partnership with Walmart demonstrates the flexibility of our concept and creates new opportunities to bring our freshly baked favorites to more communities across the country.” Wetzel’s has been sharing its signature handheld happiness ever since its founding in Pasadena, California, in 1994. The brand continues to attract a cult-like following in communities across North America through its cool SoCal feel and crave-worthy snacks that cultivate special moments of pure pretzel bliss between friends, family, and colleagues. For additional information about Wetzel’s franchise opportunity, visit https://www.wetzelsfranchising.com. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The holiday fun kicked off in NYC, where Raising Cane’s revealed a grand The Elf on the Shelf-themed window display at its Times Square Global Flagship Restaurant at 1501 Broadway. This holiday season, even The Elf on the Shelf can’t resist hand-battered, cooked-to-order Chicken Fingers! Raising Cane’s teams up with The Lumistella Company, home of The Elf on the Shelf Santaverse, for a festive, first-time collaboration bringing Scout Elf love to life through a holiday window display at its Times Square Global Flagship Restaurant in New York City, limited-edition Plush Puppies benefiting local and national charities, collectible ornaments, cozy seasonal gear and the annual children’s bike giveaways, spreading holiday cheer to families coast to coast. The holiday fun kicked off in NYC, where Raising Cane’s revealed a grand The Elf on the Shelf-themed window display at its Times Square Global Flagship Restaurant at 1501 Broadway. The window display brings Santa’s Scout Elves into the world of Cane’s, where they lose all s ELF control, parachuting in with to-go bags, cannonballing into Cane’s Sauce, skiing on crinkle-cut fries, snowboarding on Cane’s Toast, reading the secret Cane’s Sauce recipe, and cozying up with Cane III alongside holiday retail and ornaments. Located in one of the country’s most iconic holiday destinations, Cane’s annual holiday window display joins the New York City holiday window tradition for the fourth year in a row at its Global Flagship, which opened in June 2023 and is one of the busiest QSRs in the world. Beginning November 23, Customers can shop The Elf on the Shelf-themed retail and ornaments online at RaisingCanesGear.com and at the Times Square Global Flagship Restaurant, with seasonal styles and collectibles featuring Scout Elves perched on Box Combos, diving into Cane’s Sauce, sipping from Cane’s cups and giving Cane’s ONE LOVE – Craveable Chicken Finger Meals – a North Pole twist. The holiday fun heads online December 1, when Caniac Club members will receive an email invitation to play a game inspired by The Elf on the Shelf for a chance to win themed merchandise and Cane’s food rewards through January 3. Starting November 27, Customers can bring home the limited-edition The Elf on the Shelf Cane Plush Puppies, featuring the Brand’s beloved yellow Lab mascot Cane III dressed in outfits inspired by the iconic boy and girl Scout Elves. Available in-Restaurants and online at RaisingCanesGear.com for $10.99 while supplies last, the Plush Puppies continue Cane’s longtime holiday tradition of giving back, with net proceeds benefiting local and national charities. Since the first Holiday Plush Puppy made its debut in 2006, Cane’s has raised nearly $10 million through plush puppies and other initiatives. That tradition of giving continues with Cane’s commitment to donate $30 million over the next 10 years to support pets and the Communities that love them. Cane’s holiday giving continues in December with its seventh annual Holiday Bike Giveaway, a seasonal tradition inspired by Raising Cane’s owner and founder Todd Graves’ childhood memory of receiving a bike on Christmas morning. After donating 4,500 bikes and helmets to 29 Cane’s Communities in 2025, the Brand is aiming to deliver even more bikes and helmets to youth organizations across the country this holiday season. Stay in the know on all things Raising Cane’s by following @RaisingCanes on TikTok , Instagram , X and Facebook . Buffalo Wild Wings GO, the takeout- and digital-focused concept from Buffalo Wild Wings, and Dunkin’ , the largest coffee and donuts brand in the United States, are set to open on the same day this December inside a newly built travel center at 401 Getwell Road South, right at the intersection of Kyle Lane. Helen 28 LLC , the group behind the travel center, will operate the new locations, allowing the Hernando community to enjoy the two brand’s signature wings, sauces and shareable classics alongside Dunkin’ coffee, Refreshers, doughnuts and breakfast sandwiches. The wing spot joins 13 Buffalo Wild Wings locations across Mississippi, with three others already nearby in Memphis. The Hernando duo marks Helen 28 LLC’s first Buffalo Wild Wings GO and first Dunkin’, and the start of what the group expects to be a long-term partnership with Inspire Brands , with additional openings on the horizon. Hiring is underway for both establishments, with opportunities available across front- and back-of-house roles, including team members, shift leaders and an assistant manager across all shifts. Interested applicants are invited to stop by the travel center site on Saturday, Nov. 14 between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. Designed for speed and efficiency, Buffalo Wild Wings GO offers a streamlined format optimized for quick pickup and group orders. The menu centers on the items guests crave most, from bone-in and boneless wings in 26 signature sauces and dry rubs to chicken dippers, cauliflower wings, burgers, fried chicken sandwiches, wraps, fries, and desserts. A dedicated window inside the restaurant serves third-party delivery drivers and anyone who orders ahead. The restaurant forgoes its own dining room, with seating available in the travel center’s food court. Upon opening, customers can tap into some serious Buffalo Wild Wings GO value, with wing-and-fries bundles and the Pick 6 Meal for Two, starting at $19.99. The meal includes two entrées, two sides and two fountain drinks, with options to customize and upgrade. “Most communities have a handful of spots where people naturally turn to when the game is on, and our goal is for this to become the go-to in Hernando,” said Mohamed Hamoud, franchisee with Helen 28 LLC. “The best nights out rarely come down to the final score. They come from the neighbor who hosts every watch party, the youth league piling in after a big win and the friends who turn Sunday afternoons into a tradition. We want to earn a place in those stories, and we’re building a crew that cares as much as we do.” Buffalo Wild Wings GO hours will run 10 a.m. to 11 p.m. Sunday through Thursday and 10 a.m. to midnight Friday and Saturday. Dunkin’s hours will run 5 a.m. to 8 p.m. daily. For more information, visit buffalowildwingsgo.com and DunkinDonuts.com. In her new role, Amy Burhorn will draw on more than two decades of experience. Teriyaki Madness (TMAD), the Seattle-style teriyaki franchise known for cooked-to-order bowls piled high with premium proteins, fresh stir-fry vegetables and signature sauces, has named Amy Burhorn as chief financial officer (CFO). In her new role, Burhorn will draw on more than two decades of experience to oversee the accounting, finance and technology departments, working alongside the leadership team to guide the brand’s ongoing expansion. She’ll crunch plenty of numbers along the way, but one of her first priorities will be exploring how emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, can sharpen decision-making and strengthen operations across the system. Burhorn arrives from Tribe AI, where as CFO she saw firsthand what AI can do when it’s put in the hands of everyone in an organization, not just the tech team. Before that, she spent four years at Hakkoda, where she built the finance organization that took the company from startup to its 2025 acquisition by IBM. Earlier in her career, she held finance roles at Vail Resorts, Crocs and Natural Grocers, where she was part of the team that took the company public in 2012. That background makes her a natural fit for Teriyaki Madness, which has invested heavily in technology to strengthen operations and improve the franchisee experience, from streamlining back-office work to finding new ways to make every shop more efficient and profitable. Like most restaurant brands, Teriyaki Madness relies on a wide range of technology partners, from point-of-sale and back-of-house systems to online ordering, loyalty and accounting platforms, and each one produces its own stream of data. The real value comes from bringing that data together, organizing and analyzing it, and layering AI on top, then putting those insights in the hands of everyone in the organization, from the support center to franchisees in their shops. The goal is better, faster decisions that add up to well-run shops and great experiences for customers. Burhorn will lead that work, making sure every technology dollar delivers measurable value for franchisees and the business as a whole. Fast casual had a rough year for foot traffic (somebody forgot to tell TMAD). Through the first nine months of the year, same-store sales rose 6.7 percent and traffic climbed 2.7 percent, while category benchmarks sat at 0.9 percent and negative 2.1 percent. The third quarter widened that gap further, with comparable sales up 10.3 percent and traffic up 5.5 percent versus averages of 1.6 percent and negative 2.4 percent. Systemwide sales are running 28 percent ahead of last year’s pace, and TMAD is on track to close out December at 245 shops, a 22.5 percent jump in unit count. These are great trends for a CFO to walk into, Burhorn’s job now is to keep the numbers moving in the same direction. “The CFO role has changed, and while balancing the books still matters, the job today is just as much about giving franchisees the financial insight and confidence to make their next big decisions,” said Michael Haith, CEO of Teriyaki Madness. “Behind every dollar we manage is someone who believes in this brand, and Amy never loses sight of that. We’ve never been short on Madness around here, and Amy brings the method.” Burhorn holds a bachelor’s degree in business administration and a master’s in accounting from the University of Colorado Boulder, where she captained a national champion women’s club soccer team. Nearly five decades after PJ’s Coffee first opened its doors, the brand — led by brothers Paul, Steven and Scott Ballard of Ballard Brands — will officially mark its return to its original neighborhood with a celebration on Wednesday, Nov. 18, at 7700 Maple St. from 9:30-11:30 a.m. An official ribbon-cutting will take place at 10 a.m., with complimentary hot drip coffee or PJ’s Original Cold Brew™ Iced Coffee throughout the day, samples of select pastries, coffee roasts and Granitas, plus PJ’s Coffee merch and additional giveaways. As part of a renewed investment in the neighborhood and a fresh chapter for the brand, the first 25 guests will also receive free coffee for a year*. “Maple Street has always held a special place in our hearts,” said Paul, Steven and Scott Ballard, brothers and co-founders of Ballard Brands. “Having attended Tulane, we have our own memories and connections to this area, making this an especially meaningful opportunity for us. We’re excited to continue being part of the community and create a place where longtime PJ’s fans, students and new guests can gather over a great cup of coffee.” Spanning approximately 1,600 square feet, the new coffee shop features an updated design, indoor seating and an outdoor patio. Located between Carrollton Avenue and Broadway Street, Maple Street’s PJ’s Coffee sits blocks from where the brand first began in 1978, bringing a modern take on the neighborhood coffeehouse experience back to one of its most meaningful locations. Guests can expect the familiar menu that has made PJ’s a New Orleans coffee staple for nearly five decades, including hot, iced and frozen coffee beverages, its signature Original Cold Brew, classic beignets, fresh breakfast pastries and other café favorites. The space pairs those longtime offerings with a contemporary design that reflects the brand’s evolution while maintaining its connection to its New Orleans roots. Since acquiring PJ’s Coffee in 2008, the Ballard brothers have helped expand the company from its original New Orleans footprint to nearly 200 locations across the U.S. and internationally. The Maple Street opening adds a new chapter to that growth while reconnecting the brand with the community where it all began. articles.title: Handel’s Celebrates 200th Opening in Camarillo, California
articles.titleKo: Handel’s Celebrates 200th Opening in Camarillo, California
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Handel’s Ice Cream, the fastest-growing ice cream franchise in the nation, will celebrate the opening of its 200th location in Camarillo, California, on Nov. 12. The milestone comes during a record year of expansion for the 81-year-old ice cream brand, which has opened more new parlors in 2026 than in any previous year. Despite persistent inflation and uncertain consumer confidence, Handel’s continues to grow through major multi-unit development agreements and reinvestment from existing franchise owners. The brand attributes that growth in part to its unit-level economics, which rank among the strongest in the sweet treats category. “We’re thrilled to be opening our 200th location during such an incredible year for Handel’s,” said Jennifer Schuler, CEO of Handel’s Ice Cream. “Against a backdrop of persistent inflation, consumer price sensitivity and economic uncertainty, Handel’s is incredibly resilient and, in fact, even thrives in this type of environment. We keep it simple: ice cream made fresh in every store, served in generous portions at affordable prices. We want to be the kind of place where guests experience the opposite of shrinkflation. It’s a model that works for our guests and our franchise partners, as demonstrated by our 11 years of systemwide same-store sales growth.” The Camarillo opening marks the third Handel’s location for franchisees Scott and Vanessa Sonnenberg, who also operate parlors in Stevenson Ranch and Sand Canyon. It also expands Handel’s footprint in California, where the brand now has 70 parlors. The Sonnenbergs have another location planned for Simi Valley in 2027. “We’re incredibly proud to be opening Handel’s 200th location and celebrating this milestone with such a great brand,” said Scott Sonnenberg. “Handel’s has been an important part of our family’s journey, and the strength of the business model has given us the confidence to expand our ownership to multiple locations, with plans for more in the future. We’re excited to become a lasting part of the Camarillo community.” Strong Unit-Level Economics Fuel Record Franchise Development in 2026 As economic uncertainty and consumer spending pressures continue to challenge businesses across the country, Handel’s Homemade Ice Cream is proving that growth is possible with the right brand, business model and franchise partners. From January through November 2026, Handel’s has signed agreements for 75 new units, a record for the brand. Handel’s has now signed more commitments for new units in 2026 than the number of units signed during all of 2025. The majority of the agreements signed have been with multi-unit operators who are bringing Handel’s into new markets, including Chicago, while existing franchise owners continue to reinvest in the brand. While signings are the strongest in company history, Handel’s continues to set company records for new openings as well. The brand looks to open 35 new parlors by year-end and has broken into new states such as Florida, Idaho and Washington. The interest from new and existing franchisees comes as Handel’s continues to deliver strong unit-level performance. The brand reported an average unit volume of $1.1 million in 2025* and parlor-level EBITDA of 20.3% in 2024** and is currently in its 11th consecutive year of systemwide same-store sales growth. “With a 20% EBITDA margin, the unit economics are best in class for restaurant operations and make for an incredibly compelling investment,” said Erin Snyder, vice president of franchise development at Handel’s Ice Cream. “That, combined with a strong history, simple operations and whitespace to grow, makes Handel’s an attractive growth proposition for multi-unit operators. Announced via social media on Instagram and TikTok, Macdaddy is available exclusively through Piada’s website and Piada One app at participating locations from November 9 through February 15, 2027, the launch brings a fresh approach to menu innovation for the growing fast-casual brand. The limited-time bowl puts an Italian spin on a comfort food favorite, delivering the cheesy, saucy flavors of chicken parmesan in every bite. Known for his unmistakable voice, entertaining food reviews and infectious enthusiasm, Stefan is a voice and on-screen actor that has built a loyal following, known as s_johnson_voiceovers across Instagram and TikTok, where his personality and passion for food have made him a recognizable voice in the digital food community. “I’m all about food that’s big on flavor, and when Piada gave me the chance to create my own mac and cheese bowl, I knew we had to take it to the next level,” said Stefan Johnson, known as Snackdaddy. “Chicken parm and mac and cheese are two of my favorite comfort foods, so bringing them together just made sense. A line of 20 to 30 cars should have been a welcome sight for Dillas Quesadillas founder Kyle Gordon. Instead, it became a warning that his growing chain had a serious problem. Gordon was standing outside one of Dillas’ newest restaurants in the Dallas-Fort Worth area, watching customers arrive during what initially seemed like a promising opening day. The drive-thru line kept growing, but the first car wasn’t moving. When he walked inside to investigate, he discovered an operation struggling to keep up with demand. Employees were overwhelmed, preparation tasks were unfinished, and the shift leader looked terrified. This wasn’t an inexperienced team, either. Several employees had spent eight to 10 weeks training at established Dillas restaurants because construction and signage delays had pushed back the opening. The restaurant eventually recorded approximately $15,000 in sales that day and between $70,000 and $75,000 during its opening week. Those numbers should have been cause for celebration. Gordon saw something else. Dillas had ambitions of becoming a chain capable of producing $3 million to $4 million in average unit volumes. If a restaurant couldn’t handle the demand it was already attracting, expanding the concept would only multiply its problems. “My goal at Dillas, our goal, is to do this every single day,” Gordon says. The experience became a turning point for the Texas-based quesadilla chain. The brand didn’t accelerate expansion. Gordon made the difficult decision to pause development and rebuild the business from the inside out. The effort, internally known as Dillas 2.0, would eventually touch nearly every part of the operation, including menu complexity, food preparation, labor deployment, technology, and the brand’s identity. The results have been significant. Dillas has reduced drive-thru service times, improved labor efficiency, stabilized food costs, and returned to positive same-store sales and traffic growth. With 11 restaurants in its system, the company is preparing to resume expansion with a more disciplined strategy and a renewed focus on franchise development. Gordon says the original opening exposed weaknesses that had been manageable when Dillas was smaller but would become difficult to overcome as the brand grew. Kyle Gordon and his wife, Maggie, founded Dillas Quesadillas in 2013. The restaurant’s employees were dealing with complicated preparation procedures, inconsistent production forecasts, and a menu that required customers to navigate numerous combinations. Even with a relatively focused product category, the operation had become unnecessarily difficult to execute. At the time, Dillas offered 10 quesadillas and five side options through a customizable combo system. Customers had to select their quesadilla, decide whether to add a combo, and then choose among the available sides. The variety created opportunities for order inaccuracies and extended the time employees needed to become proficient. The company also relied on experienced employees to estimate how much food needed to be prepared each day. Those estimates weren’t always sufficient during periods of unusually strong demand. Gordon recognized that the system had reached its practical limits. “We basically decided we’re going to keep that quality, but we’re going to lean 100 percent into QSR plus, which is great quality, but you can you can lean on us for convenience, and you can trust us for a level of speed that you just can’t get at a fast casual,” he says. That decision represented a significant change in how Dillas viewed itself. articles.title: Tommaso Grollero from Italy Crowned World Chocolate Master 2026
articles.titleKo: Tommaso Grollero from Italy Crowned World Chocolate Master 2026
articles.originalSummary: Tommaso Grollero from Italy has been crowned World Chocolate Master 2026, earning one of the most renowned titles in international chocolate craft. The winner was announced on 27 October at Antwerp’s historic Handelsbeurs, following two days of competition among 15 regional champions at the World Chocolate Masters Grand Final. Organised by Callebaut, the World Chocolate Masters brings together leading chocolatiers from around the world to celebrate and advance the craft of chocolate. The finalists competed under the theme “Play & Taste”, taking on four challenges designed to test flavour, technique, artistry, storytelling and commercial thinking. Across the competition, the jury assessed their work for sensory excellence, technical execution, creativity and emotional expression, with taste as the ultimate measure of mastery. “I can’t believe it. Just being among the finalists was already such a great achievement. Over the past nine months, I have worked towards this moment together with my team, and I am deeply grateful to every one of them who helped make it possible. It has been an incredible journey – and winning makes it all the more special,” said Tommaso Grollero. Grollero’s creation, The Invisible , helped set him apart in a field of leading international talent. The work asks a simple question: how do you give shape to something you cannot see? Through an optical illusion, it explores the subjective nature of taste. From one viewpoint, the sculpture presents a familiar, harmonious image; shift perspective, and it transforms into an explosion of shapes and movement, revealing the complexity behind every flavour. “Across the four challenges, Tommaso Grollero showed an exceptional ability to connect flavour, technical precision and a distinctive creative vision. The title is not decided by one striking creation alone; it recognises the consistency and clarity of a chef’s approach to taste. That combination made Tommaso stand out in an exceptionally strong final,” said Amaury Guichon, Head of the World Chocolate Masters jury. Lyu Haoran of China and Keita Koshimizu of Japan completed the podium at the Antwerp Grand Final, taking silver and bronze respectively. Haoran also impressed the jury, winning the Best Bonbon and Best Share awards. Canadian superfinalist Jérémy Monsel received the Best You award, while Grollero added Best Taste and Best Design to his World Chocolate Master title. Sanghwa Lee received the jury standout award. Ian Mark, a chef with 18 years of experience competing on culinary teams, represented the UK and Ireland at this year’s global final. His previous achievements include winning numerous gold medals and accolades for Bake Off: Crème de la Crème , as well as creating the official RAF centenary cake. “The experience has been amazing. I gave it my all and couldn’t have done any more. Nothing fell over, and everything went out on time,” said Ian Mark. “I couldn’t be prouder of what I achieved. It’s been a brilliant experience.” The World Chocolate Master title recognises outstanding creativity, craft and innovation, and has served as a springboard for previous winners’ professional careers. Alongside the distinction itself, the competition offers international visibility and access to a global network of chefs and chocolate professionals. For Grollero, the title marks a major personal achievement and the beginning of new possibilities. Since its first edition in 2005, the World Chocolate Masters has grown into a global celebration of chocolate. By bringing together talented artisans and showcasing their work, it celebrates the diversity of contemporary chocolate craft and offers a glimpse of ideas that may influence the profession in the years to come.
koreanSummary: Tommaso Grollero from Italy has been crowned World Chocolate Master 2026, earning one of the most renowned titles in international chocolate craft.
The winner was announced on 27 October at Antwerp’s historic Handelsbeurs, following two days of competition among 15 regional champions at the World Chocolate Masters Grand Final.
Organised by Callebaut, the World Chocolate Masters brings together leading chocolatiers from around the world to celebrate and advance the craft of chocolate.

articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Chicken and pork are gaining attention as substitutes, along with seafood options that have become more economically attractive. The next wave of menu innovation may have less to do with discovering the next breakout ingredient and more to do with finding new ways to use what is already in the kitchen. With beef prices putting pressure on food costs, labor challenges complicating operations, and consumers seeking greater variety, restaurants are rethinking everything from protein portions to seasonings. Familiar ingredients are finding new applications, less expensive cuts of meat are gaining attention, and global flavors are giving operators opportunities to introduce new dishes without significantly expanding inventory. Two Sysco culinary experts, Anil Chacko, manager of business specialists in Houston, and Brian Fugit, manager of business specialists for Metro New York, say these developments are influencing menu decisions across the country. Their observations offer a glimpse into how restaurants are adapting to changing consumer expectations and economic conditions as they prepare for 2027. The Protein Equation One of the most immediate challenges is the cost of beef, which continues to influence purchasing decisions and menu development. Restaurants aren’t necessarily eliminating steaks, burgers, and other beef dishes, but they’re becoming more selective with portions, exploring alternative proteins, and finding creative ways to deliver value. Chicken and pork are gaining attention as substitutes, along with seafood options that have become more economically attractive. Shrimp and tuna, in particular, offer an opportunity to introduce ingredients consumers associate with premium dining at price points that are more accessible than in previous years. “Mushrooms have come right back up to the forefront,” Fugit says. “You’re seeing more shredded options with that. King oysters, upcycled shiitakes, and things along that as protein options.” Chacko says operators in South Texas are looking at the same challenges, with chicken, pork, and seafood becoming attractive additions. Beef continues to command strong consumer demand in the region, however, meaning restaurants must find ways to preserve popular menu items without allowing ingredient costs to overwhelm profitability. That has created opportunities for cuts that previously received less attention. Flat iron steaks, for example, can deliver a compelling beef experience without the expense associated with ribeyes, filets, and New York strips. Cooking techniques are helping restaurants make those substitutions more appealing. Fugit notes velveting, a technique associated with Chinese cooking that can improve the tenderness of less expensive cuts of meat. Seasonings are another relatively inexpensive way to create variety. Instead of introducing entirely new proteins or building dishes around costly specialty ingredients, operators can use spice mixtures, dry rubs, and sauces to create different flavor experiences with existing inventory. “People want to see the the maple bourbon dry rubs,” Fugit says. “It’s also a very quick and easy way to change the entire dish and then pivot from that. So if you’re working with neutral proteins carrying three or four dry spices, it’s a great way to target a few different audiences without needing a tremendous amount of skill involved.” Hot honey shows how a relatively simple condiment can create excitement around familiar foods. Its continued popularity has encouraged restaurants to experiment with additional flavor combinations that can be incorporated into existing dishes. articles.title: O consumidor não ficou mais pobre. Ficou mais seletivo
articles.titleKo: O consumidor não ficou mais pobre. Ficou mais seletivo
articles.originalSummary: Existe uma contradição interessante no consumo brasileiro. De um lado, os indicadores mostram um mercado de trabalho relativamente aquecido, aumento da renda e uma massa salarial que continua crescendo. De outro, famílias pressionadas, endividadas e cada vez mais cuidadosas na hora de abrir a carteira. Segundo dados do IBGE , a massa de rendimento real habitual dos brasileiros chegou a R$ 387,5 bilhões em setembro de 2026, crescimento de 4,7% em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior. É dinheiro novo entrando na economia. Mas, curiosamente, isso não significa que o consumidor esteja necessariamente mais disposto a gastar. O Banco Central ajuda a explicar essa aparente contradição. Em agosto, o endividamento das famílias alcançou 50,1%, enquanto o comprometimento da renda com o pagamento de dívidas chegou a 29%. A Selic permanece em 13,75% ao ano , e a inflação acumulada em 12 meses até setembro estava em 4,58%. Ou seja, parte importante da renda adicional já tem destino antes mesmo de chegar ao desejo de consumo. Mas talvez a questão mais interessante não esteja nos números, e sim no comportamento. O consumidor brasileiro não deixou de desejar. Continua querendo viajar, trocar de celular, frequentar restaurantes, renovar o guarda-roupa e experimentar coisas novas. O que mudou foi a maneira como distribui suas prioridades. Ele pode economizar na compra do supermercado, pesquisar preços em três aplicativos, trocar de marca e aproveitar uma promoção. Mas não necessariamente abrirá mão daquela viagem planejada há meses. Pode escolher uma roupa mais barata e continuar disposto a pagar caro por um bom restaurante ou por uma experiência que considere especial. Parece contraditório? Não é. É o mesmo consumidor fazendo escolhas diferentes, de acordo com o valor que atribui a cada experiência. Durante muito tempo, o varejo se acostumou a segmentar consumidores por renda, idade, classe social e localização. Essas informações continuam importantes, naturalmente. Mas talvez já não sejam suficientes para explicar o comportamento de compra. Duas pessoas com a mesma renda podem ter prioridades completamente diferentes. E uma mesma pessoa pode ser extremamente sensível a preço em uma categoria e pouco sensível em outra. Isso muda bastante a conversa sobre estratégia. O desafio das empresas não é simplesmente descobrir onde estão os consumidores com maior poder aquisitivo, mas entender onde eles estão dispostos a gastar. É uma diferença enorme. Para a indústria, significa rever propostas de valor, embalagens, marcas e arquitetura de preços. Para o varejo, significa ir além da promoção como principal instrumento de conversão. Significa conhecer melhor as missões de compra, entender as categorias que geram valor e identificar onde o cliente aceita pagar mais e onde não aceita pagar nada além do necessário. Existe também uma armadilha nessa discussão: acreditar que o consumidor mais seletivo é necessariamente um consumidor que procura apenas o menor preço. Não é. Ele procura a melhor relação entre aquilo que entrega e aquilo que recebe. E essa percepção muda de acordo com a ocasião, a necessidade e o momento de vida. O varejo que entender isso terá uma vantagem importante. Já aquele que continuar olhando apenas para renda, fluxo de pessoas e volume de vendas poderá descobrir tarde demais que está atraindo consumidores, mas não necessariamente conquistando sua preferência. No final, talvez a grande mudança não seja o consumidor ter menos dinheiro ou mais dinheiro. É que ele está atribuindo um significado diferente a cada real que gasta. E uma pergunta deveria estar presente nas reuniões de planejamento das empresas: estamos realmente entendendo o que faz nosso consumidor escolher onde gastar seu dinheiro ou continuamos tentando vender aquilo que sempre vendemos, esperando que ele continue comprando como sempre comprou? articles.title: Anthropic mira avaliação superior a US$ 1 trilhão em IPO
articles.titleKo: Anthropic mira avaliação superior a US$ 1 trilhão em IPO
articles.originalSummary: A Anthropic, desenvolvedora do assistente de inteligência artificial (IA) Claude, pretende ofertar 825 milhões de ações em sua abertura de capital (IPO), por US$ 70 a US$ 78 cada, segundo prospecto atualizado apresentado nesta terça-feira, 10, à Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC, a CVM dos EUA). A operação poderá movimentar entre US$ 57,75 bilhões e US$ 64,35 bilhões. Do total, 801,35 milhões de ações serão vendidas pela empresa e 23,65 milhões, por acionistas atuais. A Anthropic não receberá recursos da parcela vendida pelos acionistas. A companhia solicitou listagem na Nasdaq, sob o código ANT. O prospecto também prevê uma opção para os bancos coordenadores adquirirem até 123,75 milhões de ações adicionais, o equivalente a 15% da oferta inicial, conforme a demanda. Caso a opção seja integralmente exercida, a operação poderá alcançar 948,75 milhões de papéis e movimentar até US$ 74 bilhões, considerando o teto da faixa indicativa de preços. Após o IPO e a colocação privada, a Anthropic prevê um total de 13,09 bilhões de ações de diferentes classes. No teto da faixa proposta, esse número implica avaliação de cerca de US$ 1,02 trilhão, embora inclua papéis detidos por uma subsidiária integral, não considerados em circulação para fins contábeis. Paralelamente, Google e Nvidia se comprometeram a comprar US$ 10 bilhões em ações cada uma em colocação privada condicionada à conclusão do IPO. A AMD investirá US$ 2,5 bilhões. Broadcom, Micron e Microsoft investirão US$ 1 bilhão cada. A TSMC, US$ 500 milhões. O aporte conjunto soma US$ 26 bilhões e será realização em ações da classe N, sem direito a voto. Parte do compromisso do Google já havia sido assumida anteriormente. Com o preço de US$ 74 por ação, ponto médio da faixa, a Anthropic estima captar US$ 84,6 bilhões líquidos no IPO e na colocação privada, após despesas e comissões. Os recursos serão destinados a operações, pessoal e investimentos em capacidade computacional e infraestrutura. O prospecto lembra que a receita alcançou US$ 17 bilhões no terceiro trimestre de 2026, alta de 1.127% na comparação anual. Nos nove meses até setembro, o faturamento somou US$ 33,24 bilhões, enquanto o prejuízo operacional foi de US$ 1,26 bilhão. Estadão Conteúdo/Pedro Lima Imagem: Divulgação O post Anthropic mira avaliação superior a US$ 1 trilhão em IPO apareceu primeiro em Mercado&Consumo .

articles.title: Benihana Express Could Change the Brand’s Growth Trajectory
articles.titleKo: Benihana Express Could Change the Brand’s Growth Trajectory
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Benihana's same-store sales increased 0.7 percent in the third quarter. Benihana is finding new ways to bring customers into its restaurants, and its parent company sees an opportunity to take the brand into an entirely different segment of the industry. The Japanese steakhouse chain delivered 2.7 percent comparable traffic growth during the third quarter, helping The ONE Group Hospitality record its second consecutive quarter of positive consolidated transactions. Benihana’s same-store sales increased 0.7 percent, even as the company’s overall comparable sales declined 0.4 percent. KFC is giving its most loyal fans more to love this November with Finger Lickin’ Fan Fest, a limited-time celebration packed with even more ways for KFC Rewards members to get rewarded. From November 11 through November 30, KFC Rewards members can earn 2X points on purchases made through the KFC app or KFC.com, helping fans rack up points toward free food twice as fast. And when it’s time to cash them in, there’s a lot more to choose from: KFC is more than doubling the number of items available in its Secret Recipe Vault, where Rewards members can redeem points for free KFC, expanding from about a dozen choices to 24 different menu items and combos across its 250, 500, 750 and 1,000-point tiers. The timing comes as consumers head into an expensive holiday season with affordability top of mind. The latest Consumer Price Index showed prices up 3.7% year over year in September, while Deloitte found that 38% of shoppers qualify as “holiday value seekers.” With people turning to “ moneymaxxing ” tactics, including loyalty programs, to make the most of their spending, Finger Lickin’ Fan Fest comes at the perfect time before the holidays. Between football watch parties, Friendsgiving, holiday travel and family gatherings, fans have plenty of reasons to order throughout November to get more value every time they choose KFC. “Our KFC Rewards members are some of our biggest fans, and Finger Lickin’ Fan Fest is all about giving them even more back,” said Melissa Cash, Chief Marketing Officer, KFC U.S. “With double points and an expanded Secret Recipe Vault, we’re giving fans more ways to get rewarded for the food they already love.” With an expanded Secret Recipe Vault across four different tiers, members have more flexibility to use their points on what they’re craving, whether they want a quick snack, a side to round out their order or a full meal. New additions include: 250 points: Biscuit 500 points: Large Side, Pot Pie, 2 Pieces of Chicken and 3 Tenders 750 points: Classic Chicken Sandwich Combo, 6 Wings, 3-Piece Tender Combo and 2-Piece Chicken Combo 1,000 points: Big Box 3-Piece Chicken, Big Box 5-Piece Tender and 4-Piece Combo Not a member yet? Torali Italian-Steak, the signature restaurant on the 12th floor of The Ritz-Carlton, Chicago, has unveiled its fall and winter menus under Executive Chef Damion Henry, bringing a seasonal perspective to the restaurant’s signature blend of contemporary steakhouse dining and coastal Italian influences. Spanning breakfast, lunch, dinner and cocktails, the refreshed menus showcase seasonal produce, ingredients from regional producers and Italian-inspired preparations suited to Chicago’s colder months. Among the highlights are slow-braised meats, dry-aged specialties designed for sharing and a beverage program featuring cocktails named for the city’s iconic streets and neighborhoods. “I love working with fall and winter ingredients, whether it’s mushrooms, squash or a beautiful cut of meat that benefits from slow cooking,” said Henry. “There’s something special about taking those familiar, comforting flavors and giving them a fresh perspective. Hearty Italian Fare & Steakhouse Classics At dinner, Italian preparations meet traditional steakhouse classics, with several dishes designed for sharing. Alamo Prime Steakhouse, a new Texas steakhouse blending exceptional cuts of beef, Mexican-influenced flavors and genuine hospitality, will officially open its doors on Thursday, November 12, at Grandscape in The Colony. Led by Managing Partner and Executive Chef Jacob Williamson, the new concept from Identity Hospitality Group, a hospitality group led by Managing Partner and industry veteran Marlon Tapanes, brings a fresh perspective to the traditional steakhouse, combining thoughtfully sourced ingredients, a robust beverage program and a warm, inviting atmosphere designed for everything from celebratory dinners and date nights to family gatherings and casual evenings out. Located at 5765 Grandscape Blvd., the 5,200-square-foot restaurant will accommodate approximately 170 guests, including bar seating. Inspired by the rich culture, history and hospitality of Texas, with a particular nod to San Antonio’s heritage, Alamo Prime is built around the belief that the best experiences happen around a full table. At the heart of Alamo Prime is a commitment to genuine hospitality, with an emphasis on creating an experience that feels both elevated and welcoming. Rather than reserving the steakhouse experience for special occasions, Alamo Prime aims to become a place guests return to regularly, whether gathering around the table with family, entertaining clients or enjoying cocktails and dinner at the bar. “Having lived in San Antonio, I developed a real appreciation for the city’s rich history, culture and the way hospitality is so deeply woven into everyday life,” said Marlon Tapanes, Managing Partner of Identity Hospitality Group. “There’s something special about the way people gather around a table there. It’s about more than just the food. It’s about the people you’re sharing it with and the memories you create together. With Alamo Prime, we wanted to bring a piece of that spirit to DFW. Our vision is a place where the table is always full—full of great food, drinks, friends, family and conversation—and where everyone feels welcome.” A defining part of Alamo Prime’s identity is its commitment to Texas agriculture and building lasting relationships with local farmers, ranchers and purveyors. Approximately 50 percent of the restaurant’s Prime beef is sourced from Texas farms and ranches, reflecting the restaurant’s dedication to supporting producers across the state and showcasing the quality and diversity of Texas ingredients. At the helm of the kitchen is Managing Partner and Executive Chef Jacob Williamson, a Dallas native and fourth-generation Texan with more than 15 years of culinary experience. Throughout his career, Williamson has built lasting relationships with Texas farmers, ranchers and local purveyors, making locally sourced, seasonal ingredients a signature of his culinary approach. His longstanding commitment to supporting Texas producers aligns with Alamo Prime’s own philosophy of prioritizing local sourcing and building meaningful relationships with the people behind its ingredients. “We wanted to create a steakhouse that celebrates the quality of Texas ingredients while feeling like a place people can enjoy any night of the week,” said Williamson. “Of course, the steaks are a major part of what we do, but there’s so much more to the experience. From the relationships we’ve built with local ranchers and farmers to the flavors we’re bringing to the menu, every detail has been thoughtfully considered. Our goal is to serve exceptional food while making every guest feel genuinely welcome.” The culinary program celebrates Texas ingredients and ranching traditions with Mexican influences woven throughout the menu.
