articles.title: Southerleigh Hospitality Group to Open Haute South in San Antonio’s River North District
articles.titleKo: Southerleigh Hospitality Group to Open Haute South in San Antonio’s River North District
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Southerleigh Hospitality Group is bringing Haute South to River North in San Antonio, announcing the relocation of its popular Southern-inspired concept from The RIM to Make Ready Market, located at 203 8th Street. Slated to open in early December 2026, the move marks a new chapter for Haute South and another milestone in the group’s strategic growth, expanding its portfolio into the fast-casual dining space with a concept rooted in the bold flavors of the Texas Gulf Coast. The relocation follows the group’s expansion of Southerleigh at San Antonio International Airport (SAT) earlier this year, reflecting its vision to bring its distinctive culinary concepts to new audiences and dining environments beyond traditional full-service restaurants. Together, these developments signal the group’s continued evolution and commitment to growing its presence across San Antonio and beyond. Having built a loyal following at The RIM, Haute South will retain its signature approach to Southern cooking while embracing a more approachable, fast-casual format. Its new home at Make Ready Market, a locally curated food hall in San Antonio’s vibrant River North District, places the concept among an eclectic mix of independently owned culinary destinations. Known for bringing diverse food experiences together under one roof, Make Ready Market offers an ideal setting for Haute South to showcase its signature Southern comfort food and Texas Gulf Coast-inspired flavors to a new audience of locals and visitors. Menu highlights include: Texas Raw Oysters: Served with classic cocktail sauce, BBQ mignonette, fresh horseradish and lemon. Caviar Service: An elevated indulgence for guests looking to start with something special. Pimento Queso: Southern-inspired queso blended with pimento, with pickled jalapeños served on the side. Famous Fried Chicken: Texas-raised chicken, pressure-fried to golden perfection and served with a fried biscuit and signature Haute Sauce. Southern Fried Chicken Sandwich: A crispy fried chicken breast served as a Southern comfort-food favorite. Texas Gulf Shrimp Basket: Half a pound of Gulf shrimp, lightly breaded or blackened, accompanied by comeback and rémoulade sauces. Guests can also enjoy Haute South’s daily Happy Hour from 4–7 p.m., featuring select specials including $1.50 single oysters, $3 Southerleigh Gold Lager, $4 El Perrito Margaritas and $9 Tsar Nicoulai caviar bumps. “We’re incredibly proud of everything Haute South has built at The RIM, and we’re excited about what this next chapter represents,” said Jeff Balfour, Co-founder of Southerleigh Hospitality Group. “Make Ready is a destination that attracts curious, food-loving guests who appreciate quality, creativity and a great dining experience. This move gives us an opportunity to bring the best of Haute South to a more approachable, fast-casual setting while staying true to our Texas Gulf Coast roots. It’s also an important step in our vision for growing the concept and expanding our presence in the fast-casual dining landscape.” Haute South’s current location at The RIM will close November 15, 2026, with the team preparing for its debut at Make Ready Market in early December. Guests can follow Haute South and Southerleigh Hospitality Group on social media for opening updates and additional announcements. “Haute South captures what we love about San Antonio’s food scene: local roots, great food, and a loyal following. Their full bar is a welcome addition to Make Ready, and we’re excited to have them in River North,” said Jenine Cournoyer, General Manager, Make Ready Market. articles.titleKo: COJE Management Group Names Colin Lynch Executive Chef of Upcoming Boston Concepts

COJE Management Group, the hospitality company behind some of Boston’s most celebrated restaurants and nightlife destinations, has named Colin Lynch executive chef of two forthcoming concepts at 10 Post Office Square. The appointment comes as COJE prepares for a major expansion at the downtown Boston address, tripling its existing footprint. The new space will introduce a two-level Nomadic Italian restaurant and, beneath it, a private members club where the kitchen takes its cues from itameshi, the Japanese reinterpretation of Italian cuisine. In his new role, Chef Lynch will be at the helm of both the restaurant and the club, working alongside COJE Chief Culinary Officer Tom Berry, who continues to oversee creative direction and culinary operations across the hospitality group. “Chef Colin Lynch has helped define Boston’s culinary identity, and we’re proud he’s chosen to continue his story here with COJE,” said Chris Jamison, CEO of COJE Management Group. “We’re making a significant investment in the future of 10 Post Office Square, and Colin is an important part of that vision. He began his career at Barbara Lynch Gruppo, where he rose from chef de cuisine at No. 9 Park to executive chef of the restaurant group, helping develop award-winning concepts including Menton and Sportello. articles.title: Ata do Copom indica que desaceleração da economia não conteve inflação
articles.titleKo: Ata do Copom indica que desaceleração da economia não conteve inflação
articles.originalSummary: A ata do Comitê de Política Monetária (Copom) divulgada nesta terça-feira, 10, indica que a atividade econômica brasileira dá sinais mais claros de desaceleração, enquanto a inflação continua pressionada. Nesse cenário, o Banco Central reforçou a avaliação de que a Selic deverá permanecer em nível restritivo por mais tempo. Segundo o documento, os indicadores mais recentes apontam para uma “moderação mais acentuada da atividade econômica, principalmente em setores mais cíclicos”. Apesar da perda de fôlego da demanda, a inflação voltou a acelerar e permanece acima do limite de tolerância da meta definida pelo Conselho Monetário Nacional (CMN). Mercado de trabalho A ata também destaca o comportamento do mercado de trabalho. Embora a taxa de desemprego permaneça em níveis historicamente baixos, o crescimento da ocupação perdeu força. “A taxa de desemprego mantém-se em patamares historicamente baixos, enquanto o crescimento da taxa de ocupação vem apresentando desaceleração.” Os rendimentos médios perderam força na margem, mas continuam crescendo acima da produtividade do trabalho. O Copom observa que eles “ainda crescem em termos reais a uma taxa superior à da produtividade do trabalho”, aspecto monitorado pelo BC por seus possíveis reflexos sobre a inflação. Outro ponto de preocupação é a piora das expectativas de inflação. As projeções do mercado para os próximos anos continuaram se afastando da meta de 3%. Na avaliação do comitê, “em um ambiente de expectativas desancoradas, como é o caso do atual, exige-se uma restrição monetária maior e por mais tempo do que outrora seria apropriado”. A ata também voltou a destacar a importância da política fiscal para o controle da inflação. Segundo o documento, incertezas sobre a estabilização da dívida pública e um eventual esmorecimento do esforço de reformas estruturais e disciplina fiscal podem dificultar a convergência da inflação para a meta. O Copom reiterou ainda a “necessidade de políticas fiscal e monetária harmoniosas”. Cenário externo Além dos fatores domésticos, o Banco Central avalia que o cenário internacional se tornou mais adverso desde a reunião anterior. A ata atribui essa mudança ao prolongamento dos conflitos no Oriente Médio , que elevou os preços do petróleo, e à manutenção de condições monetárias restritivas nas economias avançadas. Segundo o documento, esse ambiente exige cautela dos países emergentes em um contexto marcado por “elevação da volatilidade de preços de ativos e commodities ”. Choques de oferta O Copom afirma que o cenário atual combina sinais mais claros de desaceleração da economia doméstica com quatro choques de oferta: a alta do petróleo provocada pelos conflitos no Oriente Médio; os efeitos do El Niño sobre a produção agrícola e os custos de energia; os impactos do fim da escala 6×1 sobre os custos do trabalho; e a desvalorização do real frente ao dólar. O Copom avalia que esses fatores continuam pressionando o cenário inflacionário. Ao mesmo tempo, considera que a desaceleração mais intensa da atividade econômica pode reduzir o risco de que esses choques se espalhem para outros setores da economia e gerem pressões inflacionárias mais persistentes. articles.title: Cartões movimentam R$ 1,2 tri no 3º trimestre; crescimento é de 6,6% em um ano
articles.titleKo: Cartões movimentam R$ 1,2 tri no 3º trimestre; crescimento é de 6,6% em um ano
articles.originalSummary: O setor de cartões movimentou R$ 1,2 trilhão em volume transacionado (TPV, na sigla em inglês) no terceiro trimestre de 2026, de acordo com a Associação Brasileira das Empresas de Cartões de Crédito e Serviços ( Abecs ), em coletiva de imprensa. O resultado representa um crescimento de 6,6% em relação a igual período de 2025. O número representa um desaceleração , considerando que no segundo trimestre a expansão havia sido de 7,7% e no primeiro de 8,3%. Os cartões de crédito movimentaram R$ 874,2 bilhões, uma alta de 10% em 12 meses. Já os cartões de débito recuaram 1% no período, a R$ 245,4 bilhões, enquanto o cartão pré-pago registrou recuo de 2,2%, a R$ 96,6 bilhões. O presidente da Abecs, Giancarlo Greco, classificou os números como robustos, sobretudo no crédito, apesar do trimestre desafiador para a economia. Segundo ele, o cenário atual favorece produtos com limite de crédito, o que ajuda a explicar o avanço dessa modalidade e a queda do débito. No terceiro trimestre, os brasileiros efetuaram 12,4 bilhões de transações com cartões, uma alta de 2,3% no confronto anual. Isso significa que foram feitos 135 milhões de pagamentos por dia, em média. Do total de transações no trimestre, 5,8 bilhões de operações foram com cartões de crédito, alta de 6,2%. No débito, foram 4,2 bilhões de operações, alta de 0,4%. Projeções A Abecs reduziu a previsão do crescimento do volume transacionado com cartões em 2026, para o intervalo de 7,5% a 9,5%. A previsão anterior era de expansão entre 9,5% a 11,5% este ano. Com essa nova previsão, esses meios de pagamento podem movimentar entre R$ 4,88 trilhões a R$ 4,97 trilhões em 2026. Em 2025, os cartões cresceram 10,1%, com TPV de R$ 4,55 trilhões. Greco ressaltou que o ano começou forte para o setor, mas perdeu ritmo no segundo trimestre e voltou a mostrar desaceleração no período mais recente. Entre os fatores, citou o menor crescimento do comércio e o endividamento das famílias . “Isso fez com que revisássemos a projeção, muito em função do comportamento da economia”, disse em entrevista coletiva. Com informação do Estadão de Conteúdo (Altamiro Silva Junior). articles.title: Starbucks acelera expansão e amplia presença no Nordeste com estreia no Ceará
articles.titleKo: Starbucks acelera expansão e amplia presença no Nordeste com estreia no Ceará
articles.originalSummary: A Starbucks, operada no Brasil pela Zamp , prepara uma nova rodada de expansão e vai chegar ao Ceará. Até o fim de 2026, a rede planeja inaugurar cerca de 10 unidades em São Paulo, Belo Horizonte e Fortaleza. A capital cearense marca a estreia da marca no estado e reforça sua presença no Nordeste. Por lá, estão previstas duas lojas no Fortaleza Airport e uma no Shopping Iguatemi Bosque. A expansão traz ainda novos formatos de loja. Em 2027, a Starbucks pretende abrir duas unidades no Beto Carrero World, uma delas na área temática Cowboyland. “Nossa conexão com o Brasil é de longa data. Junto com a Zamp, estamos fortalecendo essa base por meio de um crescimento planejado e com propósito, focado em oferecer as experiências certas, nos lugares certos”, afirma Ricardo Arias-Nath, vice-presidente sênior global de Café e Chá e presidente da Starbucks para América Latina e Caribe. À medida que amplia sua presença no Brasil, a rede também tem incluído produtos inspirados nos hábitos de consumo dos brasileiros em seu cardápio. Um exemplo é o Cafezinho Brasileiro, lançado com referência à tradição nacional de consumo da bebida. O cardápio também inclui produtos conhecidos, como pão de queijo, Brigadeiro e Frappuccino, além de bebidas desenvolvidas localmente, como o Média Pingado. Para o fim do ano, a Starbucks prepara o lançamento de bebidas especiais de Natal e o retorno do Panettone ao cardápio, com produtos disponíveis nas lojas de todo o País. Marca abre três lojas no Rio de Janeiro A Starbucks retomou a expansão no Rio de Janeiro com a abertura de três lojas na cidade. A primeira foi inaugurada no Shopping Tijuca, seguida por unidades no Aeroporto Internacional Tom Jobim (Galeão) e no Shopping Rio Sul, em Botafogo. A abertura das unidades marca o retorno da rede a regiões do Rio de Janeiro onde já esteve presente e integra o plano de expansão no País. A empresa prevê cerca de 30 novas lojas no Brasil até o fim de 2026. As lojas seguem o conceito global Community Coffee House , com diferentes configurações de assentos e espaços destinados a encontros, trabalho e permanência dos clientes. articles.title: Nick the Greek Opens in Indio, California
articles.titleKo: Nick the Greek Opens in Indio, California
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Nick the Greek, a national chain serving authentic Greek street food, is now open in Indio, marking its debut in the Coachella Valley. The new location is locally owned and operated by husband-and-wife Freeman and Kelly Swank and their son Tony. For more than a decade, Nick the Greek has proved that “The Best Things in Life are Greek” through a diverse and enticing menu of tasty pitas, bowls, salads, desserts and more — now available to Indio locals and visitors at the brand’s newest Nick the Greek location. “We decided to open a Nick the Greek in Indio to meet local demand for Greek food and, after experiencing Nick the Greek’s food and hospitality ourselves, we knew this is what we wanted to introduce to our community,” said Freeman Swank. “As local residents for 15 years, we are proud to bring an authentic Greek street food experience to our neighbors and seasonal festival goers while looking forward to expanding with additional Nick the Greek restaurants throughout the Coachella Valley.” Established in 2014 by cousins Big Nick, Little Nick and Baby Nick Tsigaris — all named after their grandfather per Greek tradition — Nick the Greek satisfies the desire for healthy, flavorful and authentic Greek cuisine in a fast casual environment without compromising quality. Drawing on multigenerational restaurant entrepreneurship and countless visits to Greece, the street-food-inspired menu boasts flavorful gyro meats cooked in-house on a traditional vertical rotisserie, charbroiled souvlaki skewers, zesty sauces, fresh vegetables and authentic Greek treats, including baklava and Greek donuts. In meeting the high demand for Greek street food, Nick the Greek has carved out a sizeable and attractive niche in the ultra-competitive fast casual space — a marketplace differentiator that continues to underpin the brand’s rapid growth. Since 2023, Nick the Greek has nearly doubled its store count and continues to accelerate expansion efforts throughout the nation. articles.title: Grupo brasileiro compra dona das marcas Maguary e Dafruta por 80 milhões de euros
articles.titleKo: Grupo brasileiro compra dona das marcas Maguary e Dafruta por 80 milhões de euros
articles.originalSummary: O Carlsberg Group anunciou que assinou acordo para vender a Empresa Brasileira de Bebidas e Alimentos SA (Britvic Brazil), fabricante de sucos como Maguary e Dafruta, ao Grupo José Augusto Vieira (Grupo JAV) pelo valor de 80 milhões de euros. Segundo comunicado, a conclusão da transação é esperada até dezembro de 2026, sujeita a aprovações regulatórias. A Carlsberg informou que decidiu vender a operação brasileira após uma revisão estratégica. A companhia havia assumido o controle da Britvic Brazil em janeiro de 2025, quando adquiriu o negócio internacional de refrigerantes da Britvic plc. Do lado comprador, Frank Vieira, acionista do Grupo JAV, disse que a aquisição é um marco para o grupo e reflete “confiança de longo prazo” no mercado brasileiro. A Carlsberg disse que o BofA Securities atuou como assessor financeiro exclusivo, e o escritório Lefosse como assessor legal. Movimentações de compra agitam o setor de alimentos Outra movimentação envolvendo aquisições no setor de alimentos envolve a JBS . A companhia apresentou uma proposta para comprar os cerca de 18% das ações da Pilgrim’s Pride que ainda não pertencem ao frigorífico brasileiro ou a suas subsidiárias. O Conselho de Administração da norte-americana Pilgrim’s Pride informou, em documento enviado à Comissão de Valores Mobiliários dos Estados Unidos (SEC, na sigla em inglês), que formará um comitê especial de membros independentes para avaliar a proposta não vinculante apresentada pela acionista controladora JBS N.V. Segundo o documento, não há garantia de que a oferta resultará na conclusão da transação. Caso a transação seja validada pelo comitê independente e pela maioria dos votos dos acionistas minoritários não afiliados, as ações da Pilgrim’s deixarão de ser negociadas publicamente e a empresa terá seu registro cancelado na Bolsa de Nova York. *Conteúdo elaborado com auxílio de inteligência artificial, revisado e editado pela Redação do Broadcast, sistema de notícias em tempo real do Grupo Estado Com informação do Estadão de Conteúdo (Luísa Laval). articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Amy D’s Italian is set to open Spring 2027 at 7511 Main Street in Downtown Frisco, bringing Chef Amy DiBiase’s Italian heritage and more than two decades of culinary experience to The Patios at the Rail, a catalytic development in the heart of Downtown Frisco. The two-level restaurant from Nack Hospitality will offer an elevated yet approachable Italian dining experience, equally suited for date nights, family dinners and everything in between, featuring handcrafted pasta, wood-grilled specialties and an upstairs Aperitivo Lounge. Raised in Maine, DiBiase learned to cook beside her Italian grandmother and in her family’s restaurants before earning degrees from Johnson & Wales University. She went on to lead the kitchens at Tidal and the InterContinental Hotel in San Diego and most recently served as Executive Chef of Elaine’s Kitchen. “Some of my favorite memories are of making pasta with my grandmother, and that’s the feeling I want every guest to have at Amy D’s,” says DiBiase. “I look forward to bringing that to Frisco, with the best ingredients from Texas and Italy.” Amy D’s is a partnership between DiBiase and Donny Churchman, founder and CEO of Nack Companies and developer of The Patios at the Rail. It arrives as Downtown Frisco gains momentum following the city’s $83 million makeover of The Rail District, and fills a gap downtown for elevated Italian that’s still family-friendly. Amy D’s is the first of several planned Nack Hospitality concepts, with DiBiase leading culinary direction and operations across the group. “When we developed The Patios at the Rail, we wanted to establish a destination that would help redefine Downtown Frisco,” says Churchman. “Amy D’s represents everything we envisioned for The Patios: great food, exceptional hospitality and an atmosphere that gives people another reason to fall in love with Downtown Frisco.” The chef-driven menu pairs ingredients sourced from Texas and Italy with regional Italian inspiration, moving from antipasti and housemade focaccia to handcrafted pastas, wood-grilled specialties and seasonal sides made for sharing. A dedicated pasta room lets guests see the craft behind every plate. The bar pours Italian-focused wines, classic and signature cocktails and spritzes, plus housemade shrubs, Italian sodas and alcohol-free spritzes. Upstairs, the Aperitivo Lounge will host Aperitivo Hour Tuesday through Saturday from 4 to 7 p.m. On Friday and Saturday nights, “Dopo Notte”, late-night service carries the evening forward with cocktails, wine and Italian-inspired bites from 10 p.m. to 1 a.m. Designed by Maybeck Design, the 4,700-square-foot space pairs a warm neighborhood dining room of walnut, creamy stone and aged brass, centered on the bar and working pasta kitchen, with a moodier, speakeasy-inspired second floor in deep olive, bronze and saturated red. The enclosed rooftop space features lush greenery, layered lighting, and bold furnishings, creating a lively yet sophisticated setting for gathering, celebrating and enjoying an evening out. Sliding glass panels can open the space to the outdoors when weather permits, offering a seamless indoor-outdoor experience. A 20-seat private dining room provides an intimate setting for special occasions. “Our vision for Amy D’s was to create a restaurant that feels timeless without feeling traditional,” says Danielle Harbeck, founder and CEO of Maybeck Design. Amy D’s Italian will initially serve dinner Tuesday through Saturday from 4 to 10 p.m., with plans to introduce a special Sunday Italian Lunch at a later date. Inspired by the Sundays Chef Amy spent gathered around her grandmother’s table, the multi-course, family-style experience will celebrate the tradition of sharing good food and making memories with loved ones. Additional menu and opening details will be announced soon. For updates, visit www.amydsitalian.c

articles.titleKo: Sweetgreen Sees Progress, but the Real Work Lies Ahead
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Same-store sales fell 6.4 percent in Q3, including a 4.9 percent traffic decline. Sweetgreen’s collaboration with Molly Baz gave customers a reason to talk about the brand—and come back for lunch. For CEO Jonathan Neman, it also offered a lesson in how the company should approach its next round of menu launches. The pickle-heavy partnership worked because culinary, marketing, and restaurant operations came together, he said. Sweetgreen wants to carry that coordination into 2027, with six major “experience windows” and smaller drops between them. Planning further ahead gives teams more time to refine recipes, prepare restaurants, and train employees. “The lesson is a little bit fewer, but bigger, better things,” Neman said during Sweetgreen’s third-quarter earnings call. READ MORE : Sweetgreen Introduces Incentive Plan with $200,000-Plus Potential for Restaurant Managers Sweetgreen Finds More Ways to Grow After a Wraps Win, Sweetgreen Faces a Fresh Setback That approach comes as the fast casual begins to regain traffic following a summer setback. Same-store sales fell 6.4 percent in Q3, including a 4.9 percent traffic decline. Sweetgreen estimates the disruption surrounding cyclospora headlines reduced traffic by approximately 500 basis points. By October, comps were up about 5 percent, driven by approximately 4 percent transaction growth. Neman said momentum improved further heading into November. The recovery is coming primarily from existing customers visiting more frequently and lapsed guests returning. New-customer acquisition is improving, Neman said, but remains a smaller contributor. The Baz collaboration brought three limited-time offerings to restaurants, including the Big Dill Caesar Wrap. Neman described it as one of Sweetgreen’s strongest recent brand moments and sees potential to make the Chef in Residence a repeatable platform. “The Molly collaboration really resonated both from a social and brand awareness perspective, but it was also delicious and well executed, and customers really just loved it,” he said. Sweetgreen did not quantify the partnership’s sales contribution. But it reinforced the role wraps are playing in improving frequency and reaching younger diners. Wrap incidence has remained in the high teens, with a recent increase following the collaboration. The Chicken Caesar Wrap now has the menu’s highest return rate, according to Neman. Those lower-priced options carry a trade-off. Wraps help bring customers back but pressure sales mix. Sweetgreen is reducing its reliance on discounts while maintaining everyday entry points alongside premium offerings. The next opportunity sits at dinner, which accounts for only about one-third of sales after 5 p.m. Sweetgreen is preparing to put Plates back in the spotlight with larger rotisserie-style chicken and a freshly baked sourdough chocolate chip cookie. The preparations extend beyond marketing. Sweetgreen has strengthened oven infrastructure, cooking tools, and kitchen-leader training as it expands further into hot food. That work connects to a broader issue the chain has been addressing throughout its turnaround: getting more restaurants to perform like its best ones. Forty locations set peak-hour records during September and October. Yet Neman said the gap between top-performing and median restaurants remains significant. “It is a clear reminder that two restaurants can have the same menu, equipment, and systems and still deliver very different experiences,” he said. “The difference is the head coach.” Sweetgreen’s new head coach incentive plan , taking effect in Q1 2027, ties compensation more closely to restaurant volume, sales growth, and tenure. articles.originalSummary: A Boca Rosa, marca de maquiagem fundada por Bianca Andrade, inaugurou um escritório corporativo em São Paulo para acompanhar o crescimento do negócio, e a nova sede amplia a capacidade de 60 para até 100 colaboradores. “O escritório é símbolo de um momento muito importante pra Boca Rosa. Conforme a empresa vai crescendo e se desenvolvendo, precisamos que a nossa estrutura acompanhe essa evolução. Queremos que as pessoas se sintam parte da construção da marca”, afirma Bianca Andrade, fundadora e CEO da Boca Rosa. A mudança também reorganiza o dia a dia da equipe. Times que antes estavam espalhados por diferentes andares agora dividem o mesmo pavimento, o que deve facilitar a integração entre as áreas e a troca de ideias. O espaço ganhou mais salas de reunião, ambientes para conversas individuais, copa ampliada e melhorias em conectividade e ergonomia. A identidade visual do espaço reúne os tons de rosa da marca e elementos característicos, como a boquinha. O ambiente também inclui áreas voltadas ao conforto dos colaboradores e espaços para eventos internos, encontros e reuniões com parceiros da Boca Rosa. O crescimento da equipe segue no radar da companhia, que avalia continuamente as necessidades da operação e as oportunidades de incorporar novos talentos de forma estratégica e sustentável. articles.title: Gás do Povo libera vale-recarga para 3,1 milhões de famílias
articles.titleKo: Gás do Povo libera vale-recarga para 3,1 milhões de famílias
articles.originalSummary: A Caixa Econômica Federal libera nesta terça-feira, 10, o vale-recarga do programa Gás do Povo para cerca de 3,1 milhões de famílias. A iniciativa do governo federal permite a retirada gratuita de um botijão de gás de cozinha de 13 quilos (GLP) em revendedoras credenciadas. Segundo a Caixa, mais de 15 milhões de famílias foram contempladas pelo programa. Como retirar o botijão Para receber a recarga, o responsável familiar deve procurar uma das 27 mil revendedoras que aderiram ao programa em todo o País. A validação do benefício é feita eletronicamente, na maquininha azulzinha da Caixa, por uma das seguintes opções: Cartão com chip do Bolsa Família : apresentação do cartão e uso da senha; Cartão de débito da Caixa: com senha da conta; CPF: informado na maquininha, com código de validação enviado por SMS ao telefone cadastrado na Caixa. A consulta ao direito ao benefício e à lista de revendedoras participantes pode ser feita pelos seguintes canais: Aplicativo Meu Social – Gás do Povo; Site do Ministério do Desenvolvimento Social; Portal Cidadão Caixa; Atendimento Caixa Cidadão: 111 ou 0800-726-0207; Site da Caixa; Disque Social: 121. Frequência do benefício Os vales são liberados no dia 10 de cada mês. A quantidade de recargas disponíveis ao longo do ano depende do número de integrantes da família registrado no Cadastro Único (CadÚnico). A periodicidade é dividida da seguinte forma: Famílias com dois ou três integrantes: um vale a cada três meses; Famílias com quatro ou mais integrantes: um vale a cada dois meses. Quem tem direito? A seleção dos beneficiários é feita pelo Ministério do Desenvolvimento e Assistência Social, Família e Combate à Fome (MDS). Para ser escolhido, é preciso ter: Inscrição no Cadastro Único; Renda familiar mensal de até meio salário mínimo por pessoa; Cadastro atualizado há pelo menos 24 meses. Famílias que recebem o Bolsa Família têm prioridade no acesso ao programa. Redução da pobreza energética O Gás do Povo é uma política pública federal que substitui o Auxílio Gás dos Brasileiros e busca ampliar o acesso ao gás de cozinha entre famílias de baixa renda. O programa oferece a recarga gratuita de botijões de GLP de 13 quilos em estabelecimentos credenciados e tem previsão de alcançar cerca de 50 milhões de pessoas. Para participar, os estabelecimentos precisam estar cadastrados na Agência Nacional do Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis (ANP), regulares junto à Receita Federal, ter conta corrente de pessoa jurídica na Caixa e utilizar a maquininha azulzinha. A Caixa é responsável pela operacionalização do benefício e pelo sistema de adesão das revendedoras. Dúvidas podem ser esclarecidas pelo Disque Social 121, pelo canal FalaBR ou pelo SAC da Caixa, no telefone 0800 726 0101. O atendimento humano do Disque Social funciona de segunda a sexta-feira, das 7h às 19h. O atendimento eletrônico está disponível 24 horas por dia. Com informações de Agência Brasil Imagem: Marcello Casal/Agência Brasil O post Gás do Povo libera vale-recarga para 3,1 milhões de famílias apareceu primeiro em Mercado&Consumo .

articles.title: Como saúde e longevidade estão transformando a indústria de alimentos
articles.titleKo: Como saúde e longevidade estão transformando a indústria de alimentos
articles.originalSummary: Durante décadas, a indústria de alimentos construiu seu crescimento em torno de sabor, conveniência e indulgência. Esses atributos continuarão sendo determinantes. Porém, uma nova dimensão ganha força: a capacidade dos alimentos de entregar benefícios concretos de saúde, nutrição e qualidade de vida. Essa mudança acompanha uma transformação mais ampla no comportamento do consumidor. Em uma sociedade que envelhece e quer viver mais e melhor, alimentação deixa de ser apenas uma questão de prazer ou praticidade e passa a ser parte ativa da estratégia de saúde e longevidade. Os consumidores estão cada vez mais atentos à composição nutricional dos produtos e aos seus impactos na composição corporal, prevenção, energia e cognição. Nesse contexto, poucos ingredientes representam essa transformação tão claramente quanto o whey protein. Antes restrito ao universo esportivo, o whey começa a ocupar um espaço muito mais amplo na alimentação cotidiana, tornando-se plataforma de inovação para diferentes categorias de alimentos e bebidas. Os números mostram a velocidade dessa mudança. Em estudo inédito no Brasil, a Bain & Company estima que o mercado brasileiro de concentrados e isolados proteicos derivados do leite passou de aproximadamente US$ 170 milhões em 2021 para cerca de US$ 360 milhões em 2025. O crescimento revela também uma sofisticação da categoria: enquanto o WPC-80, principal referência do mercado, cresceu cerca de 9% ao ano em volume, o WPI, segmento de maior concentração proteica, avançou mais de 20% ao ano no período. Ainda assim, o Brasil tem menos da metade do consumo per capita de WPC-80 dos Estados Unidos. Para os próximos cinco anos, a expectativa é de que o crescimento continue, em torno de 7% ao ano em volume. Um dos principais aceleradores dessa transformação será o avanço das terapias emagrecedoras, os GLP-1 . De acordo com a última edição do Consumer Pulse (pesquisa anual da Bain com mais de 2 mil consumidores) , o Brasil já apresenta adoção relevante: cerca de 11% da população já utilizou ou utiliza essas medicações, próximo ao patamar americano de 15%. As projeções indicam que mais de 20% dos brasileiros poderão ter usado essas terapias até 2030. O impacto sobre a alimentação é direto. Ao reduzirem o apetite e promoverem perda de peso, essas terapias colocam uma questão central: como perder gordura preservando massa muscular. Nesse contexto, a proteína deixa de ser um suplemento esportivo e passa a ser uma ferramenta nutricional. Os consumidores que usam GLP-1 apresentam consumo de whey protein quase duas vezes superior ao dos praticantes de atividade física que não utilizam essas terapias. E o efeito não é passageiro: a queda de patentes em 2026 deve baratear o acesso, novas formulações em comprimido devem ampliar a adesão, e o efeito rebote tende a gerar ciclos recorrentes de uso. Além do GLP-1 Mas a transformação não se limita a quem usa GLP-1. Os praticantes de atividade física que não recorrem a essas terapias respondem por 60% da demanda total de whey no Brasil. A busca por longevidade e melhor composição corporal já criou novos hábitos em uma parcela crescente da população. O medicamento apenas acelera uma mudança que já estava em curso. A indústria começa a responder. Empresas de alimentos e bebidas reformulam portfólios e criam produtos que combinam proteína, fibras e outros atributos funcionais para seus consumidores. A próxima geração de produtos deverá ser transparente quanto aos benefícios que entregam, como saciedade, praticidade, suporte à manutenção muscular e adequação a usuários de GLP-1. Esse espaço de inovação também altera a dinâmica competitiva. Marcas insurgentes, construídas em comunidades digitais de saúde e bem-estar, capturaram consumidores ao associar produtos a objetivos claros de performance. articles.title: Yo-Chi confirms second UK site to open in Clapham
articles.titleKo: Yo-Chi confirms second UK site to open in Clapham
articles.originalSummary: Australian frozen yoghurt brand Yo-Chi has announced it will open its second UK venue on Bromell’s Road in Clapham later this year, four months after making its UK debut in Notting Hill. The 1,850 sq ft site will have seating for 60 guests indoors and a further 30 outdoors. It follows the opening of the brand’s first UK venue on Notting Hill Gate in August, which attracted queues of more than five and a half hours on its opening day. Since launching in the UK, Yo-Chi has served more than 100,000 bowls, with its Signature Tart flavour proving the most popular among customers. The Clapham venue will operate the brand’s self-serve, pay-by-weight format, offering ten signature frozen yoghurt flavours and real açaí, alongside a toppings station featuring more than 30 ingredients. These include fresh fruit, choc chunk cookie cake and mini mochi.

articles.title: Outback Steakhouse is Getting Better. Now It Needs More Customers
articles.titleKo: Outback Steakhouse is Getting Better. Now It Needs More Customers
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Outback Steakhouse's same-store sales rose 1.9 percent in Q3. Outback Steakhouse is giving servers fewer tables and customers another reason to leave their grills untouched. The harder task is getting more people through the door. Bloomin’ Brands’ third-quarter results showed progress inside its largest chain’s restaurants, with guest satisfaction improving for a fifth consecutive quarter. But those gains have not translated into traffic growth. Outback’s same-store sales increased 1.9 percent, supported by higher average checks, as visits declined 1.5 percent. The company is resisting another immediate menu price increase to help close that gap. Bloomin’ delayed planned fourth-quarter pricing at Outback and Bonefish Grill, accepting a smaller near-term sales contribution as it works to make dining out worth the expense. “We just don’t feel we need to take more pricing than inflation. It really boils down to that,” CEO Michael Spanos said during the earnings call. READ MORE : Outback’s Journey to Reignite a ‘Remarkable Dining Experience’ Continues Why Outback is Reducing Table Counts for Servers Outback Steakhouse Sees First Traffic Growth in Years as Turnaround Gains Traction The decision captures the balancing act behind Outback’s turnaround. Bloomin’ is paying for better food, additional service capacity, restaurant refreshes, and more advertising in a business still losing customers. Savings from scheduling, purchasing, and utility controls are helping fund those improvements without pulling resources from the dining experience. Across its U.S. portfolio, comparable sales increased 1.9 percent, with traffic declining 1.8 percent and average check rising 3.7 percent. Sales growth trailed the Black Box Intelligence benchmark by 120 basis points, and traffic lagged by 180 basis points. Total revenue reached $944 million, compared with $929 million a year earlier. Excluding approximately $13 million associated with a gift card accounting estimate change, revenue was essentially flat. The adjusted loss widened to 17 cents per share from 3 cents. Adjusted restaurant-level operating margin declined 20 basis points to 9.3 percent, and adjusted operating margin fell to 0.3 percent from 0.8 percent. Commodity inflation reached 4.6 percent, and labor inflation was 3.5 percent. Outback’s recovery starts with making those restaurant investments visible to guests. Its updated service model limits servers to four tables during peak hours, compared with six historically. Front-of-house hospitality training followed in August. Spanos said the smaller sections reduce the strain created when an unexpected absence leaves a server covering too many tables. Employees are earning the same amount or slightly more under the new model, helped by lower tip-sharing obligations and modestly higher tip percentages. The changes are registering in customer feedback. Outback’s service, atmosphere, and likelihood-to-return scores each improved three points from a year earlier. Value increased two points, and food improved one point. Spanos said the chain’s scores now match or exceed key competitors. Steak preparation is another priority. The steak lineup launched last November continues to earn strong guest ratings, and multiunit operators will complete annual steak certification training again next month before certifying restaurant teams. Outback also finished expanding its chargrill equipment, giving kitchens more cooking capacity across steak and other proteins. That work preceded October’s Best Steaks Ever campaign. Spanos said the company wanted restaurant execution and service in place before making a larger advertising push. Bloomin’ increased annual marketing investment by $10 million, concentrated in the second half. By year-end, its media allocation is expected to reach approximately 60 percent digital and 40 percent tradition

articles.title: Restaurant Technology Should Fit the Manager’s Workflow, Not the Other Way Around
articles.titleKo: Restaurant Technology Should Fit the Manager’s Workflow, Not the Other Way Around
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . The most effective restaurant technology should complement existing operations rather than compete for attention. Restaurant managers operate in an environment where priorities can change by the minute. Between overseeing employees, managing schedules, addressing unexpected staffing issues, and ensuring guests have a positive experience, their attention is constantly being pulled in different directions. Technology is supposed to help simplify these responsibilities, yet too often, it introduces additional steps into an already demanding workday. Over the years, we’ve spent considerable time speaking with restaurant owners, franchisees, operators, and general managers about the challenges they face. One thing that continues to stand out is how much responsibility falls on the people managing daily operations. While restaurants have adopted technology to improve everything from scheduling and inventory management to hiring and employee communication, the effectiveness of these systems ultimately depends on how well they fit into the manager’s existing workflow. Hiring is a particularly good example. A manager may post a position, receive applications throughout the day, and then have to remember to log into a separate platform to review candidates. Meanwhile, they’re managing a busy lunch service, responding to employee questions, or handling an unexpected absence. By the time they return to the hiring process, valuable time may have passed, and promising candidates may have already pursued other opportunities. The challenge isn’t necessarily a lack of technology. It’s that many systems still require managers to actively seek out information rather than making relevant information easily accessible when it’s needed. Technology Should Reduce Work, Not Create More of It Restaurant managers are rarely sitting behind a desk throughout the day. They’re moving between the kitchen, dining room, and their teams, responding to operational demands as they arise. Their phones have naturally become an important part of how they communicate, coordinate schedules, and manage day-to-day responsibilities. Hiring technology should recognize this reality rather than expect managers to adopt an entirely different workflow. When a candidate applies for a position, that information shouldn’t remain unnoticed simply because a manager hasn’t had time to check a dashboard. Providing timely notifications can help managers stay informed about new applications and determine when action is required. The objective isn’t to encourage managers to spend more time on their phones, but to reduce the effort involved in staying connected to the hiring process. Beyond notifications, technology should help streamline the administrative responsibilities that often slow recruiting down. Organizing applications, screening candidates against job requirements, managing communication, and coordinating interviews are all areas where the right tools can make a meaningful difference. Instead of requiring managers to manually review every application and track each interaction, a well-designed system should help identify relevant candidates and make the next steps easier to manage. At Swob, this philosophy has influenced how we’ve approached restaurant hiring. By bringing job distribution, candidate management, and screening into one centralized system, while providing text notifications when candidates apply, our goal is to make recruiting more manageable for restaurant operators. Technology should support the hiring process by organizing information and reducing repetitive tasks, while leaving the final decisions in the hands of the people who understand their teams and businesses best. articles.title: Birley Bakery Brings A Taste Of Christmas To Burlington Arcade
articles.titleKo: Birley Bakery Brings A Taste Of Christmas To Burlington Arcade
articles.originalSummary: A Dedicated Festive Shop Opens In The Heart Of Mayfair This Christmas, Birley Bakery brings a taste of its signature festive magic to Mayfair. On Monday 2nd November, the independent bakery opened a seasonal shop at House 51 Burlington Arcade, nestled in the heart of London’s most storied shopping arcade. The third location in London, joining Birley Bakery and Birley Chocolate in Chelsea Green, is dedicated entirely to gifting and the delicious rituals of the festive season. A JEWEL BOX FOR THE FESTIVE SEASON Measuring 15 square metres, the shop is a jewel box in every sense. Like the beautiful packages within, the walls of the store are adorned with the fantastical scenes of birds taking part in a hot chocolate ceremony, inspired by the gilded motifs of 19th-century Japonisme and Birley’s carefully sourced ingredients. It is a fitting home within Burlington Arcade, which opened in 1819 “for the sale of jewellery and fancy articles of fashionable demand” and is still watched over by its famous Beadles. True to one of Burlington Arcade’s Regency-era rules that frowns on hurrying, few will choose to rush past Birley’s festive windows abundant with gifts. THE ART OF CHRISMAS GIFTING The Burlington Arcade site focuses exclusively on Birley’s Christmas and gifting collection, with every item a perfect present or festive indulgence. At the heart of the selection available is Birley’s chocolate: signature chocolates in their crimson boxes, festive creations such as a white chocolate Snowman , a milk chocolate Father Christmas and a handcrafted Chocolate Christmas Tree, the perfect addition to any festive table. The countdown to Christmas is made all the sweeter with Birley’s Advent Calendars , in classic and deluxe editions, each with unique handcrafted chocolate behind every one of its 24 doors. Festive baking also takes pride of place with Christmas essentials such as richly fruited Mince Pies and Christmas Cake , alongside the full panettone range. In addition to the signature Three Chocolate Panettone and the Classic Panettone for which Birley has become so well known, the Macallan Whisky Panettone made in collaboration with the world-renowned distillery returns for a second year. A Cinnamon & Caramel Panettone also joins the festive menu for the first time. Enriched with a touch of candied orange and generous swirls of blond chocolate infused with Ceylon cinnamon, the completely new panettone is hand-finished with a cinnamon‑spiced glaze and delicate inserts of almond paste infused with the same warm spice. For those who like to add a personal touch, visitors are invited to curate their own Christmas hamper from the offering in store, building a bespoke gift as individual as its recipient, beautifully packed and ready to give. Hampers can be filled to the brim with other Birley favourites including chocolate-coated nuts, candied Marrons Glacés and Birley’s own Christmas crackers, which are new this year and each contain a gold paper crown, a classic festive joke and dark chocolate Christmas-tree treats. A WARMING CUP TO GO As no winter stroll is complete without something warming in hand, the shop will serve Birley’s rich hot chocolate to take away in its festive red and gold cups and perfectly balanced for every palate. “ Christmas is always a special time for us at Birley Bakery, so I’m delighted that we’ll be at Burlington Arcade this year. In the heart of Mayfair, it feels like a very natural setting for our Christmas collection, panettones and Birley Chocolate, ” commented Vincent Zanardi, Director & Executive Head of Bakery and Pastry.

articles.title: Bottega By San Carlo Unveils New Chapter At Selfridges Manchester With Elevated Italian Dining Experience
articles.titleKo: Bottega By San Carlo Unveils New Chapter At Selfridges Manchester With Elevated Italian Dining Experience
articles.originalSummary: Bottega by San Carlo at Selfridges Manchester reopened on Thursday 15th October following a refurbishment, unveiling a new iteration of the restaurant that elevates the full Bottega experience. Bringing together design, authentic Italian food and expertly crafted cocktails, the refreshed restaurant offers guests a true taste of Italy in the heart of Manchester. The newly refurbished Bottega introduces a fresh interior scheme evoking the spirit of craftsmanship. Art is woven into the new space with a collection curated by San Carlo’s in-house art curator, Katie Forrester, bringing together expressive portraits and contemporary colourful assemblages from local galleries and artists. The new collection adds personality to the space, bringing more colour, character and creativity into the Bottega experience. The food offering has also been updated with San Carlo’s new autumn/winter menu, featuring a selection of seasonal dishes. Highlights include Carpaccio di Barbabietola, pairing delicate beetroot carpaccio with creamy goat’s cheese, asparagus and toasted herb breadcrumbs, finished with a yuzu honey dressing. Carpaccio di Vitello features slow-cooked, thinly sliced veal with silky celeriac cream, wild mushrooms, Grana Padano and fresh black truffle, while Insalata di Zucca combines roasted pumpkin with chestnut mushrooms, ricotta salata, toasted hazelnuts and fresh black truffle. Rigatono Affumicato con Monkfish pairs smoked rigatoni with monkfish, a rich bisque and fresh chives. Pasta and signature dishes include Risotto Zucca e Tartufo, a pumpkin risotto finished tableside in a pecorino wheel and topped with fresh black truffle, alongside Beef Cheek, featuring slow-braised beef cheek with creamy mashed potatoes, red wine jus and salsa verde. The menu also features dishes prepared and finished tableside, including Cartellata Zucca e Tartufo, pumpkin-filled large ravioli with sage butter and shaved black truffle, and Vitello Valdostana, crispy veal stuffed with Fontina cheese and ham, topped with wild rocket, Grana Padano and rosemary oil. The drinks offering takes guests on a liquid journey through La Dolce Vita, with a drinks list inspired by the grand hotels, legendary bars, personalities and glamour of 20th-century culture. Moving from Venice and Milan to Rome, each cocktail carries its own story, bringing the character and romance of some of Europe’s most iconic drinking destinations into the new Bottega experience. Highlights include the Hemingway Martini, inspired by Ernest Hemingway’s visits to The Gritti Palace in Venice, where the Martini became part of his ritual – ice cold, uncompromising and timeless. Bellini 1948 is inspired by Giuseppe Cipriani’s creation of the iconic Bellini at Harry’s Bar in Venice, where white peach and sparkling wine became a legend. Campari Seltz is a two-ingredient serve inspired by Milan in 1915 and the drink that helped define the aperitivo ritual. The Negroni Sbagliato draws on the story of Milan’s Bar Basso, where a “mistake” saw sparkling wine replace gin in a Negroni, while The Audrey pays tribute to Audrey Hepburn and the golden age of Roman glamour with an elegant and delicate serve. Together, the cocktails bring Bottega’s storytelling to life through the drinks menu, complementing the new interior and seasonal food offering. First opened at Selfridges Manchester Exchange Square in 2013, Bottega has been part of San Carlo’s Selfridges story for more than a decade. The reopening marks a new chapter for the restaurant, building on its longstanding presence within the store while bringing a refreshed expression of Bottega to the Manchester dining scene. During the refurbishment, guests were able to continue enjoying San Carlo at Gran Café, located within Selfridges Manchester. articles.title: Cacau Show prepara maior Natal da história com 12 milhões de panetones
articles.titleKo: Cacau Show prepara maior Natal da história com 12 milhões de panetones
articles.originalSummary: A Cacau Show prepara a maior operação de Natal de sua história, com a produção de 12 milhões de panetones em 2026, volume 20% superior ao registrado em 2025. O anúncio foi feito pelo fundador e CEO da companhia, Alexandre Costa, durante coletiva de imprensa nesta terça, 10. A produção chega a uma capacidade de 8 mil unidades por hora. Segundo o executivo, 90% dos panetones da marca são recheados e cobertos com chocolate puro. “Esse é o maior Natal da história da nossa empresa”, afirma Costa. A empresa também destaca o alcance de seu programa de fidelidade, que reúne 35 milhões de clientes. Segunda maior data para a marca, atrás apenas da Páscoa, o Natal deste ano deve registrar crescimento de 25% na Cacau Show em comparação com 2025. De acordo com Daniel Roque, vice-presidente de negócios da companhia, o período natalino representa entre 18% e 20% do faturamento anual, considerando apenas os produtos sazonais. “Crescemos dois itens em panetones, motivados pela nossa fábrica em Linhares, no Espirito Santo. Então, agora, estamos produzindo praticamente tudo. Estamos com a nossa independência, e isso fez com que apostássemos ainda mais nos produtos e conseguíssemos diversificar o portfólio”, destaca Roque. Cacau Show e a aposta no entretenimento A Cacau Show vem apostando fortemente na diversificação de negócios, o que inclui, além da ampliação das linhas de produtos, a oferta de experiências. O Cacau Park , parque temático da empresa em Itu, interior de Sâo Paulo, será inaugurado no ano que vem. O parque vai contar com mais de 50 atrações distribuídas em cinco áreas temáticas, todas inspiradas no universo do cacau. O complexo terá mais de 950 mil m² de área construída e incluirá dois hotéis temáticos, que juntos somarão 1.330 quartos, além de boulevard com lojas, restaurantes, centro de convenções e espaços culturais. Segundo Alexandre Costa, as lojas do parque também vão vender cerca de 5 mil SKUs, incluindo itens como bonés e pijamas. A previsão é receber mais de 3 milhões de visitantes por ano. Programado para abrir ao público em dezembro de 2027, atualmente, o parque conta com três atrações finalizadas, sendo uma delas a maior montanha-russa da América Latina, com 55 metros de altura. Dentro do parque, além das atrações, haverá um complexo de hotéis, que totaliza cerca de mil suítes, além de uma cozinha central, que ainda está em construção. Quando finalizada, ela contará com 7 mil m², 20 fornos, 33 câmaras frias, uma operação de produção 24 horas por dia, sete dias por semana (24×7), com 128 colaboradores, 1.128 posições de pallets e capacidade de produção de 50 mil refeições. Roque explica que o parque chega para integrar esse universo da marca, que começou apenas no chocolate, passou pelas lojas e hoje abraça toda a experiência do consumidor, incluindo o entretenimento. “O entretenimento entra na nossa estratégia porque conecta consumidor e marca em um espaço de memória afetiva, daquelas coisas que a pessoa vai lembrar para a vida inteira. Nós brincamos que não é nem share of pocket, nem share of happiness, mas é share of life. Nós passamos a participar muito da vida das pessoas a partir desse momento”, acrescenta. O repórter viajou a convite da Cacau Show. Imagem: Mercado&Consumo/Luisa Mitschein O post Cacau Show prepara maior Natal da história com 12 milhões de panetones apareceu primeiro em Mercado&Consumo .

articles.title: Lee’s Famous Recipe Chicken Plans Remodels in Richmond, Indiana
articles.titleKo: Lee’s Famous Recipe Chicken Plans Remodels in Richmond, Indiana
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Sixty years after his grandfather helped build Lee’s Famous Recipe Chicken, Jack Omer is helping shape what comes next. Lee’s Famous Recipe Chicken is known for its famous recipe fried chicken, homestyle sides and brewed in-house iced tea, and Weston Lee, LLC, led by Jack Omer, is continuing its investment in Richmond, Indiana, with remodels planned for both of its local restaurants as part of a broader effort to refresh the brand while preserving the traditions that have defined it for generations. The remodels are part of Lee’s Reframing the Fame initiative, a brandwide effort to modernize the restaurant experience while staying true to the food and heritage that have made Lee’s a favorite for 60 years. Planned improvements include refreshed colors, updated furniture and fixtures, new digital menu boards and significant updates to the buildings’ interiors and exteriors. “This remodel is very symbolic. It’s about much more than aesthetic updates; it’s about breathing new life into the brand as we celebrate 60 years,” said Jack Omer, franchisee and president of Weston Lee, LLC, and grandson of co-founder Harold Omer. “We know we serve best-in-class fried chicken, and now our restaurants will have an appearance that reflects the quality of the food we serve.” Work began Monday, Oct. 19, at the Richmond East location at 1801 E. Main St. The Richmond West location at 2410 W. National Road is scheduled to begin its remodel Nov. 9. During construction, the dining rooms will be temporarily closed, but the drive-thrus will remain open so guests can continue enjoying Lee’s throughout the remodel. The Richmond projects are part of a broader effort to refresh Weston Lee’s portfolio of Lee’s Famous Recipe Chicken restaurants across Indiana, including locations in Muncie, Connersville and New Castle. “We are excited to continue the remodel process across our entire portfolio,” said Brad Lucas, franchisee and chief operating officer of Weston Lee. “These restaurants are part of communities that have supported Lee’s for decades, and we see these remodels as an opportunity to invest in those communities while ensuring our restaurants are ready to serve guests for years to come.” For more information, visit LeesFamousRecipe.com or follow Lee’s on Facebook and Instagram . GoTo Foods, the platform company behind seven beloved and iconic foodservice brands, today announced the appointment of Brandon Coleman as President, McAlister’s Deli and Deli Brands, effective November 2, 2026. In his role, Coleman will be responsible for driving brand growth, innovation, profitability and operations for the company’s deli brands, which include McAlister’s Deli and Schlotzsky’s Deli. Drawing on his experience as both a franchisee and operator, Coleman will work closely with internal teams and franchise partners to identify opportunities, share best practices and deliver a consistent guest experience. “Brandon’s deep expertise on both sides of franchise operations will be invaluable as we build on the brand’s strong foundation and enter its next chapter of growth,” said Omer Gajial, CEO, GoTo Foods. “Our focus will be on clearly communicating what makes McAlister’s special and giving guests even more reasons to visit. In less than two years, he grew EBITDA approximately twelvefold, delivered six consecutive quarters of positive sales and traffic growth and improved the brand’s Google guest rating from 3.8 to 4.7 stars. Previously, Coleman served as Chief Executive Officer at TGI Fridays and in leadership roles at Dave & Buster’s, Del Frisco’s Grille, Romano’s Macaroni Grill and Brava Partners, where he advised restaurant brands and private equity firms. articles.title: Is Gen Z Really Drinking Less?
articles.titleKo: Is Gen Z Really Drinking Less?
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Chili’s bar program exemplifies how a drink never stands alone; it must make sense within the restaurant’s food, brand and value proposition. Few questions hang over full-service restaurant operators and beverage leaders more heavily right now than whether the next generation of drinkers is going to show up at all. Earlier this fall, a group of industry experts took that question on during an FSR NextGen panel at QSR Evolution Conference in Atlanta. Their answer is more optimistic—and more demanding of operators—than the prevailing narrative suggests. Gen Z is not abandoning alcohol so much as abandoning the automatic drink order. Younger guests are moving between full-strength cocktails, low-ABV drinks, and nonalcoholic options depending on the occasion, and beverage programs increasingly have to earn every sale. “We’ve all heard that Gen Z doesn’t drink,” says Ian O’Neil, director of consumer intelligence at Rubix Foods. He notes that people often overlook the generation’s actual age range, which currently spans from roughly 14 to 29. “So, we’re judging an entire generation when half of them can’t legally drink,” he says. “Maybe let’s pump the brakes.” Recent research supports his skepticism. In the U.S., the beverage alcohol participation rate among legal-drinking-age Gen Z consumers reached 71 percent during the first half of 2026, up from 68 percent two years earlier, according to IWSR’s twice yearly Bevtrac survey of consumer behavior. That put the generation roughly in line with the 70 percent participation rate recorded across the overall U.S. population. Morning Consult found a similar trajectory. Between late 2024 and mid-2026, Gen Z adults were the only generation whose consumption increased in all nine categories the firm tracks. Weekly-or-more drinking at bars and restaurants made the largest jump, rising from 26.1 percent to 31.8 percent. Some of that growth is a function of more Gen Z consumers reaching legal drinking age and moving into their mid-to-late 20s, when alcohol consumption has historically peaked. But aging does not tell the whole story. When Morning Consult held age constant, the share of 21- to 29-year-olds who drank at all was essentially flat, while weekly-or-more bar and restaurant drinking still rose by roughly five percentage points. In other words, more young adults are not necessarily taking up drinking, but those who do drink are doing so more often—particularly on-premises. Nonalcoholic Isn’t a Zero-Sum Game The explosion of mocktails and other nonalcoholic options isn’t always the substitution story it is often framed as. Gen Z’s adoption of low- and no-alcohol beer climbed from 37.5 percent in late 2024 to 40.8 percent in mid-2026, according to Morning Consult. That tied millennials for the highest rate among any generation. Yet regular alcohol consumption and bar frequency among Gen Z rose over the same period. The findings point to an additive consumer: Young adults are incorporating NA options alongside alcohol rather than necessarily replacing one with the other. A guest might choose a cocktail during one occasion, a mocktail during another, or alternate between the two over the course of an evening. For operators, moderation and alcohol consumption aren’t competing bets. The same customer can—and increasingly does—participate in both. “Nonalcoholic beverage trends and alcohol beverage trends kind of pass things back and forth,” O’Neil says, pointing to functional beverages as a current example. “I wouldn’t say that one goes up and one has to go down.” That distinction is important at a time when softer alcohol volumes can be mistaken for evidence that consumers have stopped drinking. Hawaiian Bros Island Grill is bringing its island-inspired fare to the San Fernando Valley. Ohana Island Foods, Inc., led by father-daughter franchise operators Heather Goss and Terry Jones, has signed a five-unit development agreement to open restaurants across the West San Fernando Valley, marking the first California development commitment for the fast-growing restaurant concept. For Goss, bringing Hawaiian Bros to the San Fernando Valley marks a new chapter in her restaurant career and an opportunity to further invest in the community she has long called home. A San Fernando Valley native, Goss joined Jack in the Box in 2003 and rose through restaurant operations and leadership before becoming a franchise operator in 2015. Today, she and her father own and operate 16 Jack in the Box and Del Taco restaurants across Ventura County, the San Fernando Valley and Pasadena. Jones holds nearly 40 years of restaurant industry experience, bringing extensive multi-unit ownership and operational expertise as the family prepares to introduce Hawaiian Bros to California. “Hawaiian Bros stood out to us because of the quality of the food, simplicity of the operations and strong sense of family behind the brand,” said Heather Goss, President of Ohana Island Foods, Inc. “Having spent years building our restaurant business in the San Fernando Valley, we see a great opportunity to introduce a fresh, unique dining concept to the area. Bringing Hawaiian Bros’ island-inspired food and hospitality to the community where I grew up and still live makes this opportunity especially meaningful.” “Heather started on the line in a Jack in the Box and worked her way up to running her own restaurants and multi-unit portfolio. That path is exactly what we look for,” said Grant Kreutzer, Senior Vice President of Franchise Development at Hawaiian Bros. “She knows how these restaurants run from every seat, and she’s opening them in the community she grew up in. Multi-unit franchisees based in California have been asking for Hawaiian Bros development opportunities, and we couldn’t have picked a better team to introduce us there.” Founded in 2018, Hawaiian Bros has built its growth around a streamlined restaurant model and a menu inspired by the traditional Hawaiian plate lunch. Its kitchens operate without fryers, freezers or microwaves, supporting consistent food preparation and efficient restaurant operations. Guests can choose from chicken glazed with sweet, savory or spicy sauces, or smoked pork served alongside steamed white rice and macaroni salad or vegetables, all prepared fresh in-house. The menu also features tropical Dole Soft Serve for dessert. Hawaiian Bros now has 80+ restaurants across 14 states, with the majority franchisee-owned and operated. Its development pipeline includes more than 350 additional restaurants under agreements spanning 20 states and over 75 markets, supported by 13 multi-unit franchisees. articles.title: Bubbakoo’s Burritos Opens in Concord, North Carolina
articles.titleKo: Bubbakoo’s Burritos Opens in Concord, North Carolina
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Bubbakoo’s Burritos, the award-winning Mexican-fusion restaurant concept known for its bold flavors and creative menu, is expanding its North Carolina presence with the opening of its first restaurant in the Greater Charlotte region on Tuesday, Nov. 10. Located at 3805 Concord Pkwy S., Suite 140, the new restaurant is locally owned and operated by Dhyan Shah and will bring the brand’s signature customizable menu to residents, families and visitors throughout the Concord area. Conveniently situated along Concord Parkway South, the restaurant offers a new dining option for the surrounding community, including local businesses, shoppers and visitors traveling to nearby Charlotte Motor Speedway. Guests can enjoy Bubbakoo’s diverse menu of burritos, bowls, tacos, quesadillas and more, featuring fresh ingredients, bold flavor combinations and the freedom to customize every order. “What really drew us to Bubbakoo’s was the creativity behind the menu and the welcoming atmosphere that makes the brand stand out,” said Shah. “Concord is a growing community with a great mix of families, businesses and visitors, and we saw an opportunity to bring something unique to the area. We want to create a place where people can enjoy a great meal, try something new and keep coming back.” The Concord restaurant opens just in time for guests to enjoy several November specials and seasonal favorites. On Veterans Day, Wednesday, Nov. 11, Bubbakoo’s will honor veterans and active military members with a free chicken or beef burrito or bowl with valid military ID at participating restaurants. Guests can also enjoy the Southwest Chicken Shredder, a limited-time Signature Creation inspired by the brand’s skateboarding roots, along with ongoing Taco Tuesday specials and other rewards throughout the month. “We’ve seen a strong response from guests at our existing North Carolina restaurants, and that enthusiasm has given us great momentum as we continue expanding across the state,” said Chris Ives, CEO of Bubbakoo’s Burritos. “Bringing Bubbakoo’s to the Greater Charlotte region for the first time is a significant step in that growth, and we see tremendous potential to connect with new guests in Concord and the surrounding communities.” Over the past 17 years, Bubbakoo’s Burritos has become a fan favorite for its unique menu, superb customer service, and welcoming dining environment. Living up to its promise to “create something different,” the brand offers more than 12 signature flavors that fuel its ever-evolving lineup, from the Papi Hibachi steak and shrimp Burrito to the Crispy Buffalo Chicken Quesadilla, Nashville Hot Crispy Chicken Burrito, California Steakhouse Burrito, and more. Guests are encouraged to blend creativity with the fresh, high-quality ingredients Bubbakoo’s has to offer. Bubbakoo’s Burritos has established a prominent U.S. presence across the country, creating a dedicated legion of fans. Since its inception in 2008, Bubbakoo’s has grown from its Jersey Shore roots to more than 150 locations across 17 states. The brand has been recognized among Entrepreneur’s Franchise 500, QSR Magazine’s Top 50 Contenders, and the Inc. 5000 list of the fastest-growing private companies in America. articles.title: Omni Fort Worth Hotel Names Cynthia Romstadt Executive Chef and Corey BeCoats Executive Sous Chef
articles.titleKo: Omni Fort Worth Hotel Names Cynthia Romstadt Executive Chef and Corey BeCoats Executive Sous Chef
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Omni Fort Worth Hotel is pleased to introduce an expanded culinary leadership team with the appointment of Cynthia Romstadt as Executive Chef and Corey BeCoats as Executive Sous Chef, alongside the recent promotion of Radames Garcia to Banquet Chef. Together, these culinary leaders bring extensive experience, creativity and local expertise to further elevate dining across the hotel’s restaurants, banquets and special events. Leading the team is Cynthia Romstadt, an award-winning culinary leader with more than 15 years of experience overseeing premier hospitality, resort and private club dining operations. Most recently, Romstadt served as Executive Chef at Colonial Country Club in Fort Worth, where she directed culinary operations across multiple dining venues, led culinary programming during a significant food and beverage renovation and oversaw hospitality for the renowned Charles Schwab Challenge PGA TOUR tournament. Nationally recognized for her leadership and innovation, Romstadt has been honored as one of Club + Resort Business’ 40 Under 40 and named among BoardRoom Magazine’s Top 30 Female Leaders. Throughout her career, she has built a reputation for elevating culinary programs, mentoring future hospitality leaders and creating memorable guest experiences through thoughtful, ingredient-driven cuisine. “I am thrilled to join Omni Fort Worth Hotel and become part of such an iconic property in the heart of Fort Worth,” said Romstadt. “For me, hospitality is about creating meaningful experiences that guests remember long after they’ve left the table. I look forward to collaborating with this talented team, celebrating the flavors of our region and continuing to elevate the culinary experiences we offer our guests and community.” Raised in the mountains of Western North Carolina, Romstadt’s passion for cooking began in her grandmother’s kitchen and evolved into a career rooted in seasonality, craftsmanship and hospitality. Her leadership philosophy centers on developing culinary talent, fostering collaboration and creating memorable experiences that leave guests feeling genuinely cared for. Joining Romstadt is Corey BeCoats as Executive Sous Chef. In his role, BeCoats serves as the operational leader of the culinary department and partner to the Executive Chef, overseeing day-to-day kitchen operations and supporting execution across the hotel’s food and beverage outlets. A graduate of Le Cordon Bleu, BeCoats brings executive-level culinary leadership experience and a passion for creating memorable dining experiences while mentoring the next generation of chefs. The hotel also recently promoted a rising culinary leader. Radames Garcia has advanced to Banquet Chef, where he oversees banquet culinary operations and plays a key role in delivering exceptional experiences for meetings, events and social functions throughout the hotel. Garcia brings a diverse culinary background and leadership experience developed through positions with Omni Hotels and several respected dining establishments. “With the addition of Cynthia and Corey, along with the well-earned promotion of Radames, we are building an extraordinary culinary leadership team,” said Michael Hiltabidel, General Manager of Omni Fort Worth Hotel. “Their combined expertise, passion and commitment to hospitality will continue to elevate the dining experiences that make Omni Fort Worth Hotel a premier destination for both visitors and locals.” With its new culinary leadership team in place, Omni Forth Worth Hotel continues to build on its commitment to thoughtful, locally inspired dining while developing the next generation of culinary talent across the hotel’s restaurants, banquet and special event offerings. articles.title: Cactus Club Cafe to Open Flagship Stores in Uptown Houston and Miami
articles.titleKo: Cactus Club Cafe to Open Flagship Stores in Uptown Houston and Miami
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Cactus Club Cafe confirmed two new U.S. flagships set to open in 2027: Uptown Houston and Miami South Beach. Following recent successful openings in Boston’s Back Bay and Downtown Miami, these locations mark the brand’s entry into Texas and its second restaurant in Miami, accelerating its position as one of North America’s fastest-growing restaurant collections. Cactus is elevated everyday dining, creating a sense of occasion, even when there isn’t one. The vibe is upbeat, stylish, and polished, not pretentious–fueled by energetic music, great people, and spaces that feel as good as they look. Their chef-driven menu delivers bold, refined dishes with something for every craving. Fresh yet familiar, it’s easy to love and easy to come back to. The menu is helmed by Executive Chef Greg McCallum and the Test Kitchen team of culinary experts. “Joining our team in Houston or Miami is an exciting opportunity for ambitious hospitality professionals,” said Andrew Latchford, President of Cactus Club Cafe. “As we expand into these new markets, we remain committed to what defines Cactus Club Cafe: food people love, a consistently great dining experience, and a vibrant atmosphere.” Miami South Beach Spanning nearly 9,000 square feet, Cactus South Beach will be an anchor go-to for visitors and locals alike in South of Fifth. Completely transforming the heritage location at 850 Commerce Street, the space will seat over 200 guests across a lounge, dining room, mezzanine, and patio. Highlights include a striking floor-to-ceiling backlit wine display and a vibrant, gallery-like layout anchored by artwork from acclaimed artists Daniel Mazzone and Giovanni DeCunto. Both locations are designed by Jeffrey Beers International, with architecture by Bergmeyer Architecture and lighting design by Think L and Ian Marsh Lighting. Houston Uptown Spanning two levels, nearly 12,900 square feet, and 345 seats, Houston Uptown will be Cactus’ largest U.S. location. The design features a dedicated lounge, dining room, patio, and a two-story entrance tree. Artwork curated specifically for Texas includes a custom mural by Taylor Smith, Western-inspired pop art, and pieces by Giovanni DeCunto. Hiring is officially underway for Houston Uptown. With nearly 40 years of experience advancing hospitality careers, Cactus provides long-term growth and leadership opportunities. Candidates can apply online or attend the Houston career fair on Dec. 1 and 2 at cactusclubcafe.com/hiring/united-states/.
