articles.title: New Mexican-Inspired Concept El Punto Opens at San Diego’s Liberty Station
articles.titleKo: New Mexican-Inspired Concept El Punto Opens at San Diego’s Liberty Station
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . The new Mexican-inspired restaurant El Punto officially opens tonight at San Diego’s Liberty Station, the former site of historic Naval Training Center, San Diego. The family-friendly and dog-friendly concept will initially offer dinner service only from 4:00 – 10:00 p.m., seven days a week. Restaurant founder Gerry Torres made the announcement. Torres, who was born in Mexico City and spent most of his childhood in San Diego and Tijuana, also founded San Diego-area taqueria chain City Tacos (est. 2014) and full-service restaurants Fonda del Barrio (est. 2025) and Tour de Tapas (est. 2024). El Punto is a full-service restaurant featuring entrées and shareables from Executive Chef Eduardo Baeza, as well as select tacos from the City Tacos menu. Diners will have three options for ordering food and drinks within the 8,800-square-foot indoor/outdoor space: from wait staff, self-serving QR codes at tables throughout the patio, and a walk-up counter. The menu will feature selections like: Tiradito de Atún – Fresh pressed tuna tossed in our bold Black Panther sauce, served alongside spring mix with thinly sliced lime, mango, radish, and serrano chile. Finished with a drizzle of olive oil and sesame oil, served with tostadas or tortilla chips. Aguachile Negro – Fresh shrimp marinated in our Black Panther leche de tigre, a bold black sauce made with chiltepín chiles, garlic, ginger, serrano, and lime. Tossed with crisp cucumber, onion, fresh blueberries, and creamy avocado. Served with tostadas or tortilla chips. Filete de Pescado – Fish fillet glazed in a bold zarandeado sauce made with mustard, Valentina, and guajillo Buffalo sauce, and lime, fresh cilantro, and a drizzle of chile macha oil. Served with a side of refried beans & rice. Puerco Adobo – 6 oz. pork tenderloin served in a rich chile Colorado sauce made with guajillo chiles, orange, achiote, and cinnamon. Accompanied by roasted sweet potato, crispy kale, and a sprinkle of toasted amaranth. Roasted Cauliflower – Fire Roasted Cauliflower dressed in a creamy jocoque ranch, topped with kale, cotija cheese, finished with a tamarind and balsamic reduction. Tostaditas de Jaiba – Gulf Crab meat & Flounder fish ceviche tostadas (3) with capers, garlic, onion & cilantro, finished with a chili oil drizzle. Beverages are available at both a container bar and Michelada bar station. The beverage menu features a cocktail program curated by Bar Director Rudy Corona, as well as draft beer and coffee. El Punto has an indoor dining room, as well as extensive outdoor dining options via lounge seating and high tops with bar stools. All patio seating is covered, and televisions are dispersed throughout the outdoor area. The kids area, which is separated from the patio dining spaces by the main entryway, will have games like at City Tacos’ OB Playground in Ocean Beach. The enclosed dog park allows pets to roam and play without a leash. “We are blessed to call Liberty Station ‘home’ for El Punto,” Torres said. “It’s such a tremendous gathering place that all San Diegans can enjoy – with free parking to boot. We believe we are providing a dining option that is decadent, but affordable and casual. There is something on the menu for everyone, including several healthy options.” Brunch and lunch service will be added in the coming weeks. articles.title: East London Brewing Co to open The Black Horse Tap in Walthamstow
articles.titleKo: East London Brewing Co to open The Black Horse Tap in Walthamstow
articles.originalSummary: East London Brewing Co. will open The Black Horse Tap, a new pub above its brewery on Walthamstow’s Blackhorse Beer Mile as the independent brewer marks 15 years in business. Opening later this month, The pub, set to accommodate 80 covers inside and a further 80 outside, will feature a drinks list including East London Brewing Co.’s heritage cask range, alongside hop-forward keg beers, lagers and a weekly-changing selection of guest cask ales from independent UK breweries. The offer will also include agave-focused cocktails, independent wines and spirits. Food will be cooked in a dedicated open-fire kitchen, which will launch with a residency from Play With Fire until the end of the year. Chef Matt Purkis, formerly of Lagom and Ibai, will serve reworked pub classics and sharing plates cooked over fire and wood smoke alongside Sunday roasts.

articles.title: Why Claudio Obertelli is returning to London’s restaurant scene
articles.titleKo: Why Claudio Obertelli is returning to London’s restaurant scene
articles.originalSummary: The restaurateur behind Sticky Fingers and Ménage à Trois is back in the London restaurant scene with Torino, a three-storey Italian restaurant, bakery and rooftop at Paddington Square. Claudio Obertelli has returned to restaurant ownership with the opening of Torino, his latest venture in partnership with friend Peter Fulton. Spanning 5,000 sq ft across three floors, the new concept has opened at 1A Paddington Square, marking Obertelli’s return to the industry after a period working in hospitality consultancy. Obertelli first entered the restaurant business at 21 and went on to build a portfolio of 11 venues across London and New York. His previous ventures included Kensington institution Sticky Fingers, which he created with Rolling Stones bassist Bill Wyman, and Ménage à Trois, which had sites in Knightsbridge and New York. After selling his restaurant group, Obertelli turned to consultancy, advising hospitality businesses on international expansion.

articles.title: UK hospitality spending grows despite decline in restaurant transactions
articles.titleKo: UK hospitality spending grows despite decline in restaurant transactions
articles.originalSummary: UK consumer spending on hospitality and leisure continued to grow in October, with spending on eating and drinking rising 2.3% year-on-year, according to the latest Barclays Consumer Spend report. Within the sector, bars, pubs and clubs recorded the largest increase with a 4.7% growth in spending, alongside a transaction growth of 5.7%. Takeaways and fast food also saw positive growth, with spending up 3.4% and transactions increasing by 4.1%. However, restaurants, cafes and bakeries recorded more modest growth. Spending increased by 0.5%, while transaction volumes fell by 1.6%.

articles.title: Fim da escala 6×1 exige planejamento; veja como preparar sua empresa
articles.titleKo: Fim da escala 6×1 exige planejamento; veja como preparar sua empresa
articles.originalSummary: A redução da jornada de trabalho e o fim da escala 6×1 exigirão mudanças na organização das empresas, especialmente no varejo, que precisa conciliar a cobertura das operações, o controle de custos e a produtividade. O tema foi discutido em uma live realizada pela Federação do Comércio de Bens, Serviços e Turismo do Estado de São Paulo ( FecomercioSP ), que reuniu representantes da entidade e especialistas em direito do trabalho e gestão de pessoas para analisar os impactos da Emenda Constitucional 141. A Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) 221/2019 foi aprovada no dia 14 de outubro pelo Senado Federal . No dia 16, foi oficializada com a promulgação da Emenda Constitucional nº 141/2026. Kelly Carvalho, assessora da FecomercioSP, destaca os desafios econômicos que a mudança representa para as empresas, principalmente diante da proximidade de datas importantes para o comércio, como Black Friday e Natal. Segundo ela, a reorganização das operações precisa considerar os períodos de maior movimento, a disponibilidade de mercadorias e a capacidade de atendimento ao consumidor. Um dos pontos de atenção é a gestão de estoques, já que, com equipes menores em determinados períodos, as empresas podem enfrentar dificuldades nos processos de recebimento, armazenagem, etiquetagem e envio de produtos. O resultado pode ser a indisponibilidade de mercadorias nas lojas ou atrasos nas entregas, comprometendo a experiência de compra. Como alternativa, Kelly recomendou que as empresas negociem com fornecedores a antecipação de pedidos de produtos com maior demanda e reorganizem atividades operacionais para períodos de menor fluxo de consumidores. Ela também ressaltou a importância de mapear os dias e horários de maior movimento para adequar as escalas às necessidades de cada operação. “Essa mudança, essa análise do planejamento da empresa, ela já tem que começar agora e ser aperfeiçoada de acordo com o dia a dia da empresa ao longo de 2027. Nós já temos um processo que as empresas já têm esse momento para fazer isso. Sabemos muito bem que é um prazo curto, que temos duas datas muito importantes para o varejo, Black Friday e Natal. Então, é importante que já se leve em conta isso”, afirma. Mudanças trabalhistas e custos Além dos impactos na operação, a Emenda Constitucional 141 também traz mudanças que exigem atenção à gestão de pessoas. A nova regra estabelece a redução gradual da jornada semanal de 44 para 42 horas e, posteriormente, para 40 horas. Também prevê dois descansos semanais remunerados (DSRs) e a possibilidade de perda de efeito de cláusulas previstas em acordos e convenções coletivas que sejam incompatíveis com as novas disposições. Esses aspectos foram abordados no segundo bloco da transmissão, com a participação de Rodrigo Chagas Soares, advogado, professor de Direito do Trabalho e sindical no INSPE e membro do Conselho de Emprego e Relações de Trabalho da FecomercioSP; Marisa Salgado, partner na Cigno Brasil; e Karina Negrelli, assessora jurídica da FecomercioSP. Soares destaca que, entre as principais mudanças trazidas pela Emenda Constitucional 141, estão a redução gradual da jornada semanal de 44 para 42 horas e, posteriormente, para 40 horas, além da previsão de dois descansos semanais remunerados (DSRs), totalizando oito folgas por mês. “Eventualmente, será necessário analisar cada caso para determinar se uma cláusula ou escala de trabalho é, de fato, incompatível com a previsão de redução da jornada e de dois descansos semanais remunerados. O Tribunal poderá ser chamado a avaliar essas situações, cabendo à Justiça do Trabalho analisar a questão”, ressalta Soares. Karina explica que as empresas já podem começar a reorganizar as escalas de trabalho para contemplar os DSRs e a jornada de 42 horas semanais, sem necessidade de regulamentação adicional. articles.title: Swig Expanding in Northern Colorado with 10-Unit Deal
articles.titleKo: Swig Expanding in Northern Colorado with 10-Unit Deal
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Swig has signed a multi-unit franchise agreement with experienced franchisees Marc and Zach Rogers to bring the brand to Northern Colorado. The 10-unit deal will accelerate Swig’s growth in the West region and introduce its highly customizable drink experience to new communities, including Fort Collins, Loveland, and Greeley. The father-and-son duo plan to open their first location by June 2027, further advancing Swig’s nationwide franchise growth. The father-and-son team brings extensive restaurant and franchising experience to Swig, with backgrounds spanning restaurant operations, multi-unit ownership and franchise development. Zach grew up in the restaurant industry and has spent 15 years working his way from busboy to franchise owner, including returning to the industry following his military service. Marc has spent decades in restaurant franchising, working across six different concepts while also establishing strong ties to the Colorado market through his ownership of a local brewery. Together, they bring the industry knowledge and local connections to support Swig’s growth throughout Northern Colorado. “Having spent decades in the restaurant industry, I’ve seen firsthand what it takes to build a successful brand, and Swig has created something that really stands out,” said Marc Rogers. “Between its loyal customer following, innovative menu and strong business model, we see tremendous potential to bring Swig to more communities across Northern Colorado. Having the opportunity to grow this business alongside my son makes it even more meaningful, and we’re looking forward to building something special together.” As the creator of the dirty soda category, Swig continues to lead the growing beverage segment by delivering the customization, convenience and “Daymaking” moments of connection that today’s consumers seek. “Colorado continues to be an exciting growth market for Swig, and partnerships with experienced operators like Marc and Zach are key to bringing our brand to new communities,” said Alex Dunn, CEO of Swig. “Their extensive restaurant backgrounds, local market knowledge and commitment to building successful businesses make them exactly the type of franchise partners we’re looking for as we continue expanding our footprint. We’re confident they’ll play an important role in introducing the Swig experience to even more guests across the state.” Swig designed its franchise model for efficiency and convenience, with a drive-thru-centric footprint that can operate in as little as 800–850 square feet. Without the need for complex kitchen infrastructure, Swig’s streamlined model helps operators reduce labor demands, lower build-out costs and efficiently scale across multiple locations. “As we continue scaling Swig nationwide, our focus remains on building a franchise system that supports sustainable, long-term growth for our operators,” said Todd Smith, President of Swig. “We’re seeing strong interest from experienced multi-unit operators who recognize the opportunity within the dirty soda category and the potential to introduce Swig to new markets. Agreements like this one reflect that momentum and reinforce our confidence in the brand’s continued expansion.” Founded in 2010 in St. George, Utah, Swig has grown from a single drive-thru concept into a nationally expanding brand with more than 150 locations across 16 states. Swig’s simple, scalable model, loyal customer base and personalized beverage experience continue to fuel its growth and resonate with consumers across generations. Swig is actively seeking qualified multi-unit operators to support its continued national expansion. Ideal franchise candidates bring proven experience in restaurant operations and a commitment to delivering exceptional guest experiences at scale. articles.title: Supera mira 400 franquias impulsionada pelo envelhecimento da população
articles.titleKo: Supera mira 400 franquias impulsionada pelo envelhecimento da população
articles.originalSummary: A Supera, rede de franquias de estimulação cognitiva, planeja ampliar sua presença no Brasil em meio ao avanço da economia da longevidade . A empresa pretende chegar a 400 contratos de franquia assinados nos próximos três anos, com a abertura de pelo menos 150 novas unidades até 2028. Para sustentar o plano de expansão, investirá R$ 5 milhões no fortalecimento da estrutura comercial, na captação de novos franqueados e na implantação de um novo modelo arquitetônico para as escolas. Atualmente, a rede conta com 250 unidades em operação, atende cerca de 28 mil alunos e registrou faturamento de R$ 187 milhões em 2025. A estratégia de crescimento prevê prioridade para capitais e cidades de médio porte. Entre os mercados considerados estratégicos estão Acre, Roraima e Rondônia. O movimento acompanha o aumento da demanda por serviços relacionados à saúde cerebral, memória e qualidade de vida. Embora, de acordo com a Supera, a metodologia seja voltada a diferentes faixas etárias, os idosos representam aproximadamente 79,5% dos alunos da rede. O público também inclui crianças, adolescentes e adultos, entre eles mulheres na menopausa e profissionais interessados no desenvolvimento de habilidades cognitivas e socioemocionais. Além da ampliação da rede, a Supera projeta crescimento de aproximadamente 35% no faturamento em 2027. O plano de expansão aposta em franqueados com participação ativa na operação, especialmente profissionais com experiência ou afinidade com as áreas de educação e saúde. O investimento inicial para abrir uma franquia parte de R$ 159.990, incluindo taxa de franquia, implantação, capital de giro e showroom. Em 2025, a lucratividade média informada pela empresa foi de aproximadamente 25%, enquanto o tíquete médio mensal por aluno ficou em torno de R$ 400. articles.title: Shopee e Britânia realizam ativação de beleza em São Paulo no 11.11
articles.titleKo: Shopee e Britânia realizam ativação de beleza em São Paulo no 11.11
articles.originalSummary: A Shopee e a Britânia promovem uma ativação conjunta na Praça da Baleia, em São Paulo, no 11.11 , das 11h às 17h, como parte da Temporada de Compras da plataforma. A iniciativa busca aproximar os consumidores dos produtos de cuidados pessoais da marca por meio de experiências presenciais e ofertas on-line. Durante a ação, os visitantes poderão testar escovas, modeladores e secadores, conhecer lançamentos e aproveitar serviços de cabeleireiro, sorteios, brindes e cupons de desconto. Com o conceito “Com você, em todas as suas versões”, o Beauty Truck apresenta soluções da Britânia para diferentes rotinas de autocuidado. A iniciativa também integra as comemorações dos 70 anos da marca. “Essa parceria integra nossa programação especial para a Temporada de Compras e reforça nosso propósito de conectar consumidores e marcas de forma ao longo de todo o ano. No 11.11, nossa principal data dupla, e na Black Friday, ampliamos essa proposta com ofertas, cupons e experiências que tornam a jornada de compra ainda mais atrativa para nossos usuários”, afirma Felipe Lima, diretor de Desenvolvimento de Negócios e Operações Fulfillment da Shopee. Na Shopee, os consumidores poderão encontrar ofertas especiais em produtos de cuidados pessoais, como escovas secadoras, cacheadores e secadores de cabelo. No 11.11, a plataforma disponibilizará 500 cupons de R$ 15 de desconto em compras a partir de R$ 99, válidos exclusivamente na data. “Queremos que as pessoas tenham a oportunidade de conhecer nossos produtos de perto e descobrir como eles podem contribuir para suas rotinas de autocuidado. O retorno do Beauty Truck pelo segundo ano reforça nosso compromisso de estar próximos dos consumidores, criando experiências que geram conexão com a marca e mostram, na prática, como nossos produtos podem acompanhar diferentes momentos e versões de cada pessoa”, afirma Emanuelle Henche, gerente de Marketing e Comunicação da Britânia. Além da ativação em parceria com a Shopee, a Britânia promove ações próprias do Beauty Truck em São Paulo, no Parque Villa-Lobos, nos dias 28 e 29 de novembro, durante o fim de semana da Black Friday. A iniciativa também passará por Curitiba e Salvador, levando experiências de beleza e autocuidado aos consumidores. articles.title: Fim das bets e Bolsa Família: varejo alimentar tem melhor resultado do ano em outubro
articles.titleKo: Fim das bets e Bolsa Família: varejo alimentar tem melhor resultado do ano em outubro
articles.originalSummary: O varejo alimentar registrou em outubro o melhor desempenho mensal de 2026, com crescimento de 6,4% no faturamento em mesmas lojas na comparação com o mesmo mês de 2025. O resultado foi impulsionado por fatores como o reajuste de 15% no Bolsa Família e a proibição das apostas esportivas para beneficiários de programas sociais, além da antecipação de compras provocada pelo calendário de pagamentos. Segundo o Radar Scanntech, relatório mensal elaborado pela empresa de inteligência de dados para o varejo, o avanço no faturamento foi quase o dobro do registrado em setembro, quando o indicador cresceu 3,3%, e ficou acima do acumulado do ano, de 3,5%. As unidades vendidas permaneceram praticamente estáveis, com alta de 0,1%, interrompendo a sequência de quedas dos meses anteriores. “Outubro foi o melhor mês do ano, mas parte desse resultado veio da antecipação dos salários. O sinal mais importante é a estabilidade das unidades depois de meses de queda. Se isso se sustentar, o canal alimentar chega à alta sazonal de fim de ano em boa posição, mas o acumulado do ano ainda mostra queda de 0,6% em unidades, afirma Felipe Passarelli, head de Inteligência de Mercado da Scanntech. De acordo com a Scanntech, o aumento da renda disponível das famílias, associado ao reajuste de 15% no Bolsa Família, em vigor desde 19 de outubro, e à proibição das apostas esportivas para beneficiários de programas sociais, desde 25 de setembro, contribuiu para o resultado. O efeito calendário também teve influência: o pagamento de salários previsto para o início de novembro caiu na sexta-feira, 30 de outubro, antecipando as compras para o dia 31. Sem esse efeito, o faturamento teria crescido 4,2%, enquanto as unidades vendidas teriam recuado 0,9%. O consumidor também levou mais produtos por compra, com alta de 1,2% nas unidades por tíquete, compensando parcialmente a queda de 1,1% no fluxo de clientes nas lojas. O volume vendido avançou 0,6%. Inflação e comportamento de consumo A inflação desacelerou em outubro para 0,51%, ante 0,91% em setembro, segundo a métrica da Scanntech. O índice geral foi influenciado pela queda nos preços do café (-2,4%) e do leite UHT (-1,8%). Já a Cesta Básica registrou alta de 0,97%, pressionada pelo tomate (+21,5%), arroz (+4,2%) e carne bovina (+2,6%). Em 12 meses, a inflação acumulada chega a 5,01%. Entre as cestas analisadas, Perecíveis liderou o crescimento do faturamento, com alta de 9,5%. O destaque foi a categoria de legumes, que avançou 36,3%, principalmente em razão do aumento dos preços do tomate e da cebola, impactados pelas condições climáticas. As temperaturas médias mais elevadas também favoreceram o consumo de bebidas. Os energéticos registraram crescimento de 46,4% no faturamento e de 38% nas unidades vendidas. Desempenho regional e por formato de loja Todas as regiões brasileiras apresentaram crescimento no faturamento em outubro. O Centro-Oeste liderou, com alta de 8,3%, seguido pelo Sul (+8,2%), Norte (+8%) e Nordeste (+7,1%). O Sudeste teve o menor avanço, de 4,9% considerando Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro e Espírito Santo, além de São Paulo, que registrou alta de 5% no faturamento. A região foi a única com retração nas unidades vendidas. Em São Paulo, a queda foi de 1%, enquanto nos demais estados do Sudeste chegou a 1,2%. Entre os formatos de loja, os supermercados com dez ou mais checkouts lideraram o crescimento em faturamento, com alta de 7,1% e avanço de 0,2% nas unidades. O atacarejo, por sua vez, registrou a maior expansão em unidades vendidas, de 1,7%, e crescimento de 6% no faturamento. Os formatos menores tiveram retração nas unidades. Os supermercados de um a quatro checkouts registraram queda de 5%, apesar da alta de 8,6% nos preços. O faturamento avançou 3,2%. Já as lojas com cinco a nove checkouts cresceram 6,8% em faturamento, mas tiveram recuo de 1,1% nas unidades. Promoções ganham espaço As ofertas representaram 26,8% das vendas do varejo alimentar em outubro, aumento de 1 ponto percentual em r
koreanSummary: O varejo alimentar registrou em outubro o melhor desempenho mensal de 2026, com crescimento de 6,4% no faturamento em mesmas lojas na comparação com o mesmo mês de 2025.

O resultado foi impulsionado por fatores como o reajuste de 15% no Bolsa Família e a proibição das apostas esportivas para beneficiários de programas sociais, além da antecipação de compras provocada pelo calendário de pagamentos.

Segundo o Radar Scanntech, relatório mensal elaborado pela empresa de inteligência de dados para o varejo, o avanço no faturamento foi quase o dobro do registrado em setembro, quando o indicador cresceu 3,3%, e ficou acima do acumulado do ano, de 3,5%.

articles.title: Insomnia Cookies Has New Look and Bigger Vision for the Future
articles.titleKo: Insomnia Cookies Has New Look and Bigger Vision for the Future
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Insomnia Cookies has spent more than two decades building a business around the of delivering warm cookies to people when they crave them most. That idea, first developed by founder Seth Berkowitz in his University of Pennsylvania dorm room in 2003, has grown into an international chain with more than 375 bakeries. Now, as the company pursues an ambitious expansion strategy, it’s giving its brand a makeover. Insomnia unveiled a refreshed visual identity Monday, replacing its illustrated moon logo with a photograph of a half-eaten chocolate chunk cookie. The changes extend to packaging, typography, photography, and marketing, all tied together by a new tagline, “Always Warm Since 2003.” The company partnered with creative agency &Walsh on the project, which aims to preserve Insomnia’s personality and late-night roots while making the brand relevant to a wider range of customers and occasions. “Insomnia created the warm cookie delivery category in 2003, and after 23 years, this felt like the right moment to remind people who we’ve always been,” Berkowitz says. “We’ve grown from a college dorm room concept to more than 375 bakeries across the U.S., Canada, and U.K., and our customers now turn to us for far more than late-night cravings.” The refresh comes during a significant period of change for Insomnia. Krispy Kreme, which acquired a majority stake in the cookie chain in 2018, sold that ownership position to Mistral Equity Partners and Verlinvest in 2024 . The doughnut company subsequently sold its remaining 34 percent stake in 2025 , giving Insomnia an opportunity to pursue its growth plans under new ownership. Berkowitz, who continues to serve as CEO, previously told QSR magazine that Insomnia sees room for 1,800 domestic bakeries. The company has historically concentrated on college campuses and urban neighborhoods, but it is pursuing opportunities in suburban markets, transportation hubs, tourist destinations, and sports arenas. That expansion creates a new challenge. How does a company closely associated with college students and late-night cravings appeal to customers who may now be ordering cookies for office parties, birthdays, and family gatherings? Before developing its new identity, Insomnia conducted qualitative consumer research with Gen Z and millennial participants through dscout. The findings revealed that customers frequently associated the brand with experiences and memories instead of specific products. Participants recalled late-night study sessions, celebrations with friends, and moments of relaxation. According to the research, 75 percent of respondents said they ordered Insomnia for comfort instead of a sugar rush. In a separate question, all respondents who answered associated ordering the brand with winding down instead of winding up. “What stood out was how often customers talked about the memories around their cookies, from late-night studying to celebrations with friends,” Berkowitz says. “They associated us with comfort and connection, not just a sweet treat.” Those findings became the foundation of the “Always Warm Since 2003” campaign, which connects the temperature of Insomnia’s cookies with the emotional experiences customers associate with the brand. The company also recognized an opportunity to maintain relationships with customers as their lives change. Someone who discovered Insomnia during college might now order cookies for an office celebration, a family gathering, or an afternoon treat. Reaching those customers requires expanding the occasions when Insomnia comes to mind without abandoning the identity that attracted them originally. “Our college roots and late-night delivery will always be part of who we are. But the same customer who discovered us during a study session may now order cookies for an office celebration, family gathering or afternoon treat,” Berkowitz

articles.title: Grupo Pereira abre portas para a diversidade com 2 mil vagas para diferentes perfis
articles.titleKo: Grupo Pereira abre portas para a diversidade com 2 mil vagas para diferentes perfis
articles.originalSummary: O Grupo Pereira realiza, até o dia 13 de novembro, próxima sexta-feira, a Semana da Diversidade, iniciativa voltada à ampliação do acesso ao mercado de trabalho e à valorização de diferentes perfis profissionais. A ação oferece 2 mil vagas de emprego para jovens, profissionais com 50 anos ou mais, imigrantes, pessoas LGBTQIAPN+, pessoas com deficiência (PCDs), pessoas negras e egressos do sistema prisional , por meio do programa Reeducandos. As oportunidades disponíveis abrangem diferentes áreas operacionais e administrativas, nas bandeiras Fort Atacadista e Supermercados Comper. Os interessados podem comparecer a uma das lojas das redes participantes da ação, entre os dias 9 e 13 de novembro, das 8h às 11h ou das 13h às 17h, levando documentos pessoais e currículo. Também é possível realizar o cadastro on-line pelo site . “Para o Grupo Pereira, promover a diversidade é reconhecer o potencial das pessoas e ampliar as oportunidades para que encontrem espaço para desenvolver suas habilidades e construir uma trajetória profissional. A Semana da Diversidade reforça nosso compromisso com um ambiente de trabalho inclusivo, que valoriza e acredita que diferentes experiências contribuem para o crescimento do negócio”, afirma Simone Cotta, Head de Comunicação Corporativa e ESG do Grupo Pereira. As vagas estão distribuídas entre as regionais da companhia, em Santa Catarina, Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul, São Paulo, Rio Grande do Sul e Distrito Federal. Entre as principais funções estão operador de caixa, operador de loja, auxiliar de carga e descarga, repositor, técnico em carnes, atendente de farmácia, promotor de cartões e atendente. Pilar de diversidade As oportunidades abrangem diferentes níveis de experiência e áreas de atuação, permitindo que candidatos com diferentes trajetórias profissionais participem do processo seletivo. Atualmente, o Grupo conta com 44,2% de mulheres em cargos de liderança, 2.646 profissionais imigrantes (sendo 1.802 refugiados), 970 colaboradores PCDs, 228 reeducandos e 18,2% do quadro formado por profissionais com mais de 50 anos. Aos 68 anos, Neuza Maria Passos mostra que a trajetória profissional não precisa terminar depois de uma certa idade. Operadora de loja do Fort Atacadista, ela ficou cerca de três anos fora do mercado de trabalho, período em que realizava apenas trabalhos pontuais para complementar a renda. Ao encontrar uma oportunidade na rede, decidiu se candidatar e conquistou uma nova colocação profissional. “Eu tinha um pouco de medo de não conseguir acompanhar, principalmente por causa das tecnologias, mas fui aprendendo com a ajuda dos colegas e hoje me sinto muito mais confiante. O trabalho também faz muito bem para a minha mente, é quase uma terapia. Tenho muita disposição e ainda quero continuar trabalhando”, diz Neuza. A estratégia também passa pelo acolhimento de profissionais vindos de outros países, que atuam em diferentes áreas da operação, contribuindo com novas experiências, perspectivas e culturas. Um deles é César Meneses, imigrante venezuelano que trabalha no Grupo há quatro anos. “Meu primeiro emprego no Brasil foi aqui no Grupo Pereira. Entrei na área de carga e descarga do Fort Atacadista e, depois de um tempo, tive a oportunidade de ir para a manutenção, em uma loja do Supermercado Comper, onde estou há dois anos. Crescer dentro da empresa e continuar fazendo parte dessa equipe é motivo de muito orgulho para mim”, conta Meneses. articles.title: Panda Express to Launch Triple Chocolate Rangoons with Ghirardelli
articles.titleKo: Panda Express to Launch Triple Chocolate Rangoons with Ghirardelli
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Panda Express is turning one of its most beloved appetizers into dessert with the launch of Triple Chocolate Rangoons. Marking Panda’s inaugural partnership with GHIRARDELLI Chocolate Company, the limited-time offering reimagines the brand’s signature crispy rangoon with a triple dose of premium chocolate, delivering an indulgent finale to any meal. Available beginning Nov. 10 through Jan. 11, 2027, or while supplies last, the dish will roll out as a regional test at participating locations across Chicago, Dallas, Indianapolis, Los Angeles, Miami, Phoenix, Salt Lake City, San Diego, San Francisco Bay Area and West Palm Beach. Each crispy rangoon is stuffed with a smooth chocolate cream cheese filling made with Ghirardelli Semi-Sweet Chocolate Chips and Ghirardelli Chocolate & Cocoa Sweet Ground Powder, then finished with a drizzle of Ghirardelli’s Black Label Chocolate Sauce and a dusting of powdered sugar. Golden and crispy on the outside with a warm, gooey center, Triple Chocolate Rangoons deliver a craveable ‘crack-open’ moment that blends comfort-food nostalgia with dessert-shop indulgence. “Rangoons are one of our top-selling menu items because they’re crispy, comforting, and instantly recognizable. We wanted to take that fan-favorite format and reimagine it into an unexpected dessert,” said Adrian Lok, Director of Culinary Innovation at Panda Express. “The breakthrough was crafting a warm, gooey chocolate center that hits the sweet spot between a fudgy brownie and a lava cake. It’s a comforting, indulgent treat you didn’t know you needed at the end of a Panda meal.” “At Ghirardelli, we’re passionate about crafting premium chocolate experiences with high-quality ingredients and rich, layered flavor. We’re thrilled to partner with Panda Express as our first collaboration in the Asian quick-service restaurant space, bringing our chocolate to a creative new dessert that reimagines a familiar favorite,” said Dave Dulyx, VP of Professional Products & Licensing at Ghirardelli. “Triple Chocolate Rangoons showcase three distinct Ghirardelli chocolate elements working together to create layers of chocolate flavor and texture in every bite, resulting in a dessert that’s indulgent, satisfying and uniquely unexpected.” The post Panda Express to Launch Triple Chocolate Rangoons with Ghirardelli appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Schlotzsky’s Franchisee Files for Bankruptcy
articles.titleKo: Schlotzsky’s Franchisee Files for Bankruptcy
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . A Schlotzsky’s franchisee in North Texas filed for bankruptcy after struggling with profitability and mounting financial obligations. JPrieto Hospitality filed for bankruptcy protection November 5 in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Western District of Texas. The company, led by managing member Jorge Prieto, is seeking to reorganize its finances and continue operating its remaining restaurants. According to Schlotzsky’s 2026 FDD, JPrieto operated eight restaurants at the end of 2025, with two additional franchise agreements terminated during the year. Meanwhile, the company’s bankruptcy filing identifies five restaurant locations in Fort Worth (two), Mansfield, Grand Prairie, and Cedar Hill. JPrieto reported $8.26 million in revenue in 2024 and $8.2 million in 2025, according to court documents. Its 2025 federal tax return showed just $45,051 in ordinary business income, representing a profit margin of roughly 0.5 percent. Revenue totaled $4.12 million from the beginning of 2026 through the November 5 bankruptcy filing. Prieto attributed the company’s financial difficulties to changing economic conditions in the Fort Worth market, including reduced business activity and work slowdowns. JPrieto explored selling its business or assets, restructuring its obligations, and refinancing debt before turning to bankruptcy. Court documents list approximately $533,000 in assets and $351,000 in liabilities. Schlotzsky’s franchisor GoTo Foods is its largest unsecured creditor, owed approximately $148,642. Other creditors include food distributor Ben E. Keith, owed $35,000, TCR Heating & Air, owed $19,422, and Cooling Equipment Specialist, owed $18,776. JPrieto believes its remaining restaurants can support a successful reorganization, aided by new marketing efforts and improved operating performance. “JPrieto anticipates that continued operations with remaining stores will generate sufficient net income to formulate a confirmable plan,” Prieto said in the court filing. JPrieto is the latest restaurant franchisee to seek bankruptcy protection in 2026, following filings involving operators of Wendy’s , Dave’s Hot Chicken , Outback Steakhouse , and Denny’s . The financial difficulties have also affected another GoTo Foods brand. Quality Fresca, a Moe’s Southwest Grill franchisee , filed for bankruptcy in August after shrinking its portfolio from 69 restaurants to 38. articles.title: Parque temático de Ayrton Senna é inaugurado em Gramado
articles.titleKo: Parque temático de Ayrton Senna é inaugurado em Gramado
articles.originalSummary: O Senna Super Experience, atração imersiva dedicada à trajetória de Ayrton Senna, será inaugurado na primeira quinzena de dezembro, em Gramado (RS). O espaço terá mais de 30 ativações distribuídas em 14 ambientes temáticos, com ingressos a partir de R$ 99 e entrada por horário agendado. O percurso foi desenvolvido para apresentar a trajetória do tricampeão mundial de Fórmula 1 a partir de valores associados à sua carreira, como superação, excelência e evolução constante. A proposta não é seguir o formato de um museu, mas oferecer experiências interativas que aproximem os visitantes dos desafios vividos pelo piloto. “Queremos permitir que os fãs se aproximem da trajetória do Ayrton, vivendo desafios e relembrando grandes momentos por meio de experiências imersivas, muito além de um museu. O Senna Super Experience convida cada visitante a viver essa mentalidade campeã, como uma inspiração atemporal”, afirma Bianca Senna, CEO global da Senna Brands. A atração também busca reunir diferentes gerações de admiradores de Senna, conectando quem acompanhou sua carreira nas pistas a quem conhece sua história e legado. Parceria e operação O projeto é uma parceria da Senna Brands, empresa responsável pela gestão das marcas Senna e Senninha, com operação do Grupo JGM. Fundador do Super Carros Gramado, o grupo atua no setor de entretenimento da região e também está envolvido no desenvolvimento de uma atração da franquia Transformers na cidade. “Nós acreditamos que o Senna, considerado o maior piloto de todos os tempos, merecia um lugar onde seus fãs pudessem vivenciar uma experiência inédita. Um legado dessa dimensão merece ser sentido, compartilhado e transmitido às próximas gerações. Nada melhor do que Gramado para receber e dar vida a essa atração única”, destaca Gustavo Mandelli, do Grupo JGM. A iniciativa amplia a atuação da Senna Brands no segmento de experiências. A empresa já desenvolve o Senna Club, plataforma vinculada à Fórmula 1, e a Ayrton Senna Racing Day, corrida de rua realizada no Autódromo de Interlagos há 21 edições. articles.title: Gás do Povo: governo prorroga vigência do auxílio até 2031
articles.titleKo: Gás do Povo: governo prorroga vigência do auxílio até 2031
articles.originalSummary: O governo federal publicou nesta segunda-feira, 9, no Diário Oficial da União (DOU), medida provisória que prorroga até 19 de novembro de 2031 a vigência do auxílio Gás do Povo. Em nota, a Secretaria de Comunicação Social (Secom) da Presidência da República informou que a iniciativa assegura a continuidade do programa que, atualmente, atende cerca de 15 milhões de famílias, totalizando 45 milhões de pessoas. “A prorrogação garante a manutenção de uma política pública voltada ao enfrentamento da pobreza energética e à ampliação do acesso ao gás de cozinha para famílias de baixa renda”, destacou o comunicado. Ainda de acordo com a Secom, a medida considera o peso do gás liquefeito de petróleo (GLP) no orçamento doméstico das famílias mais vulneráveis. “Ao assegurar a continuidade do programa, o governo federal busca contribuir para que essas famílias tenham condições adequadas de preparar seus alimentos, fortalecendo a segurança alimentar e nutricional.” Vales Na próxima terça-feira, 10, o programa vai disponibilizar 3,1 milhões de vales para recarga gratuita do botijão de gás de cozinha. Desse total, 380,5 mil serão destinados a novas famílias beneficiárias e 2,7 milhões a famílias já participantes. O investimento, de acordo com o governo federal, supera R$ 337 milhões. O programa conta com uma rede de 27.160 revendas credenciadas. Para participar, a família precisa ter renda de até meio salário mínimo por pessoa, estar inscrita no Cadastro Único, com dados atualizados nos últimos 24 meses e sem pendências cadastrais, incluindo Averiguação Cadastral e indício de óbito do responsável familiar. Além disso, o CPF do responsável familiar deve estar regularizado na Receita Federal. Notícias falsas No fim de outubro, a Secom publicou alerta à população sobre informações falsas que circulavam nas redes sociais relacionadas a programas como o Gás do Povo. A nota divulgada à época garantia a continuidade do benefício. Dúvidas O governo federal orienta a população a verificar informações em canais oficiais antes de compartilhá-las. Dúvidas sobre programas sociais podem ser esclarecidas pelo Disque Social 121. articles.title: Crocs e Carmed lançam coleção com espaço para hidratante labial
articles.titleKo: Crocs e Carmed lançam coleção com espaço para hidratante labial
articles.originalSummary: A Crocs e a Carmed se uniram para lançar uma coleção limitada que combina elementos das duas marcas em calçados e acessórios. A colaboração chega ao Brasil em 17 de novembro de 2026, com modelos adultos e infantis do Classic Clog, Bae Clog e Bag Charm. A coleção traz estampas de cerejas pretas sobre bases rosas e off-white, além de Jibbitz exclusivos. Os produtos também incorporam espaços para encaixar e transportar o hidratante labial Carmed “Oi, Tchurma”. Nos modelos Classic Clog adulto e infantil, o acessório fica na alça traseira. Já o Bag Charm conta com uma tampa que permite carregar o hidratante e pode ser personalizado com Jibbitz. “A Crocs se torna ainda mais forte quando seus produtos icônicos se transformam em uma plataforma para cultura e autoexpressão. Nossa colaboração com a Carmed mostra como uma marca global pode criar algo profundamente relevante para o público local, unindo duas comunidades apaixonadas por meio da personalização, da colecionabilidade e de uma perspectiva genuinamente brasileira. Estamos muito felizes em celebrar a primeira colaboração da Crocs com uma marca brasileira”, afirma Ricardo Sobral, VP da Crocs Brasil. O lançamento também inclui o retorno do Carmed de cereja, agora integrado à colaboração. A coleção reúne itens com diferentes propostas e preços, que variam de R$ 139,99 a R$ 599. Como parte da estratégia de lançamento, as marcas promovem uma live de pré-lançamento em 16 de novembro, às 19h, com transmissão simultânea nos canais @crocsbrasil do TikTok e do YouTube. A apresentação terá a participação de Karla Felmanas e das Besties, com detalhes dos produtos e interação com o público. Carmed Crocs Classic Clog Kids: R$ 319 Carmed Crocs Classic Clog: R$ 439 Carmed Crocs Bae Clog: R$ 599 Carmed Crocs Bag Charm: R$ 139,99 A coleção estará disponível a partir de 17 de novembro de 2026, nas lojas Crocs do Brasil, no site crocs.com.br e no TikTok Shop da marca. Os produtos serão comercializados em edição limitada, enquanto durarem os estoques. “Assim como os fãs de Crocs, nossa comunidade adora colecionar, personalizar e expressar sua personalidade, uma relação que ajudou a transformar Carmed em uma marca que já ultrapassou R$ 2 bilhões em faturamento desde o lançamento. Por isso, ver o ‘Oi, Tchurma’ ganhar vida nessa parceria é tão especial: conseguimos unir esses dois universos de forma divertida e autêntica, criando algo único para nossas besties e para os fãs de Crocs”, afirma Karla Felmanas, vice-presidente da Cimed e head de Carmed e Flavy. articles.title: Traição, espionagem e negócios bilionários: entenda o caso que envolve o CEO da Nvidia
articles.titleKo: Traição, espionagem e negócios bilionários: entenda o caso que envolve o CEO da Nvidia
articles.originalSummary: A Nvidia abriu uma investigação independente para apurar se seu presidente-executivo, Jensen Huang, foi alvo de uma operação de inteligência estrangeira. A decisão foi anunciada no domingo, 8, depois que o executivo admitiu ter sido infiel à mulher e de a mídia internacional apontar que ele manteve um relacionamento com Alice Huang, empresária chinesa que autoridades americanas suspeitam ter sido recrutada por Pequim para obter informações sobre o executivo. O caso reúne suspeitas de espionagem, negócios bilionários envolvendo chips de Inteligência Artificial e a relação extraconjugal de um dos principais nomes da indústria de tecnologia. A apuração também ocorre em meio à disputa entre Estados Unidos e China pelo domínio da Inteligência Artificial e às restrições americanas à exportação de semicondutores avançados para o território chinês. Em uma mensagem enviada aos funcionários da Nvidia, Jensen reconheceu a infidelidade e pediu desculpas à mulher e aos filhos. “Não há justificativa para o que fiz”, afirmou. Ele também disse ter decepcionado colegas, integrantes do conselho, parceiros e acionistas, e declarou que pretende reconquistar a confiança deles. A empresa informou que uma comissão formada por integrantes independentes do conselho, com apoio de advogados externos, ficará responsável pela investigação. Segundo a Nvidia, o grupo examinará todas as informações disponíveis. A companhia afirmou não ter motivos para acreditar que dados confidenciais da empresa ou informações relacionadas à segurança nacional dos Estados Unidos tenham sido comprometidos. Jensen apoia a apuração e continuará no cargo durante o processo. Alice Huang e o papel dela no caso Alice Huang, também conhecida como Huang Le, é cidadã chinesa e não tem parentesco com Jensen, apesar do sobrenome em comum. Ela teria ocupado um cargo de alto escalão na Megaspeed International, empresa de tecnologia sediada em Singapura que atua no setor de computação em nuvem e oferece capacidade de processamento para sistemas de Inteligência Artificial. Segundo reportagem do New York Times , autoridades americanas concluíram que Alice teria sido recrutada pela China para coletar informações sobre Jensen e a Nvidia. A suspeita é que ela tenha usado sua proximidade com o executivo para obter dados sobre os planos da fabricante de chips e sua atuação no mercado de Inteligência Artificial. As alegações não foram comprovadas publicamente, e Alice não se manifestou sobre as acusações. A empresária tem poucas informações disponíveis em registros públicos. Um perfil atribuído a ela em uma base chinesa de dados sobre investimentos indica passagens pelo banco HSBC e por emissoras de televisão do país, como a CCTV e a Hunan TV. Os dois foram vistos juntos em eventos do setor de tecnologia. Em 2024, uma fotografia de uma festa da indústria mostrou Jensen sentado ao lado de uma mulher identificada como Alice. Em maio de 2025, durante a feira Computex, em Taiwan, eles participaram de um jantar em um restaurante chinês. Imagens divulgadas na ocasião mostraram os dois em clima de proximidade e deixando o local no mesmo carro. A relação da Megaspeed com a Nvidia A Megaspeed é uma empresa de Singapura que aluga capacidade computacional para companhias que desenvolvem e operam sistemas de Inteligência Artificial. Em seu site, se apresenta como parceira comercial da Nvidia na oferta de serviços de computação em nuvem na região Ásia-Pacífico. A empresa entrou no radar das autoridades americanas em 2024, sob suspeita de ajudar companhias chinesas a obter chips avançados da Nvidia, apesar das restrições impostas por Washington. Segundo registros comerciais citados pelo New York Times , a Megaspeed e uma afiliada na Malásia compraram mais de US$ 4,8 bilhões em equipamentos da fabricante ao longo de dois anos. articles.title: Topgolf Lowers Prices by Average of 20 Percent Across All Locations
articles.titleKo: Topgolf Lowers Prices by Average of 20 Percent Across All Locations
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Topgolf is announcing its lowest prices ever, reducing gameplay rates by an average of more than 20 percent across all 100+ U.S. venues, effective today, November 9. This is not a limited-time promotion and there’s no code required. This is a fundamental shift in Topgolf’s pricing structure, designed to make the experience more affordable and accessible than ever before. This move comes as a direct response to guest feedback. Over the past six months, Topgolf surveyed thousands of guests, analyzed social conversations and conducted in-person interviews at venues. The message was consistent: guests love Topgolf. In a survey, 78% of respondents cited social connection and 72% cited the food, drinks and service as key reasons they visit. But high cost was the number one reason guests said they don’t come back more often. “After joining Topgolf in February, I spent my first 100 days visiting our more than 100 U.S. venues and I heard a common theme from our guests: our experience is unmatched, from high-quality food to games and the ability to connect through friendly competition, but our prices are too high to keep them coming back,” said David McKillips, CEO at Topgolf. “I want our guests to know that we heard them and are now introducing our lowest prices ever. Topgolf has always been about more play for all and by reducing the price of gameplay, we’re backing that commitment up with real, meaningful action. The cost of fun just got more affordable.” The pricing announcement follows Topgolf’s recently announced multi-year partnership with TMRW Sports to bring TGL presented by SoFi and WTGL experiences to Topgolf venues and Toptracer Range facilities nationwide. Paired with ongoing additions across food and drink menus, new arcade games rolling out at all U.S. venues by end of year, merchandise, and special events, Topgolf continues to find new ways to give guests more fun to experience, increasing the value of each visit. Topgolf’s new pricing applies to gameplay at all U.S. venues, making the brand’s signature blend of entertainment, food, drink and technology-driven games more accessible to avid golfers, casual players and anyone looking for a great reason to gather. articles.title: Portillo’s Trades Aggressive Expansion for Smarter Growth
articles.titleKo: Portillo’s Trades Aggressive Expansion for Smarter Growth
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Portillo's same-restaurant sales increased 1.4 percent. Portillo’s is preparing to say goodbye to several restaurants as it rethinks what successful expansion should look like. The Chicago-based chain plans to close a mid-to-high single-digit number of underperforming locations outside its home market, with most closures expected during the fourth quarter. The decision comes after an extensive review of restaurant sales, profitability, and future operating potential, and signals a significant change in how the company plans to grow. CEO Brett Patterson, who took over earlier this year, is making it clear that expansion will no longer be measured simply by the number of restaurants opened. “A site will not advance simply because we want another restaurant. The economics have to work,” Patterson told investors during the company’s third-quarter earnings call. READ MORE : Portillo’s Cuts Corporate Jobs in Bid to Reset the Business Under New CEO, Portillo’s Begins to Play the Long Game Again Portillo’s Remains Committed to ‘Crack the Code’ in Texas The closures are part of a larger effort to repair Portillo’s financial performance after years of aggressive development produced disappointing returns. The company expects material cash and noncash charges associated with the closures, primarily during Q4. Specific locations and costs have not been disclosed as Portillo’s evaluates its lease obligations. Patterson identified several problems with the company’s previous expansion strategy, including poor real estate decisions, excessive restaurant concentration in certain markets, and insufficient brand awareness. Some newer restaurants were built in locations where customers had to travel considerable distances. Others opened too close to existing Portillo’s restaurants, redistributing sales instead of attracting additional customers. The company also discovered that some locations outside Chicago lacked signage explaining what Portillo’s actually served. Those mistakes have prompted a fundamental reassessment of the company’s development ambitions. “We ramped up so quickly in those markets and plugged in a lot of infills as all we did is redistributed sales from those geographic areas,” Patterson said. “And so that put a lot of pressure on the business models.” The changes arrive as Portillo’s reported encouraging third-quarter results. Same-restaurant sales increased 1.4 percent, improving 260 basis points sequentially from Q2. Revenue climbed 7 percent to $194.1 million, supported by $10.3 million from newer restaurants. Transactions declined 0.7 percent, although that represented a 270-basis-point sequential improvement. Average check increased 2.1 percent, driven by menu pricing. Restaurant-level adjusted EBITDA increased to $40.1 million, with margins expanding 50 basis points to 20.7 percent. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $26.5 million, compared with $21.4 million a year earlier. The improvement came despite elevated beef costs and difficult comparisons against last year’s breakfast testing and promotional discounts. Limited-time offerings, including the Char’diniera Dog and Dr Pepper Shake, helped stimulate transactions without aggressive discounting. Patterson believes menu innovation can play a larger role in restoring customer frequency. “When you give them good news and you give them news that resonates with the brand, they’ll come visit,” he said. “It doesn’t have to be at a discount. Actually, it shouldn’t be at a discount.” The company recently introduced OREO desserts, which CFO Kevin Kalicak said were performing well early in Q4. Same-restaurant sales during the opening weeks of the quarter were running ahead of Q3 trends. articles.title: Savvy Sliders Continuing Growth Momentum Into 2027
articles.titleKo: Savvy Sliders Continuing Growth Momentum Into 2027
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Savvy Sliders, the Michigan-born slider brand known for its bigger, better, bolder approach to its menu lineup is finishing 2026 with strong development momentum that includes a growing national presence and an expanding pipeline of new operating partners expected to fuel growth through 2030 and beyond. Founded in 2018 in Commerce Township, Michigan, Savvy Sliders now operates over 50 locations across seven states including Michigan, Ohio, Texas, Louisiana, Florida, Indiana and Mississippi. With more than 50 additional locations in development or under franchise agreements, the brand is building a foundation for its next phase of national expansion into several new markets, including Oregon, Kentucky, Illinois, Nevada and New York, further extending its reach and establishing a presence in key growth markets across the country. A Strong Finish to 2026, With More Openings Ahead Savvy Sliders is entering the final weeks of 2026 with a strong wave of recent restaurant openings in Michigan (Detroit and Monroe) and Texas (Pasadena), with an additional 11 restaurants in the final stages of construction expected to open before year-end. Upcoming openings include Medford, Oregon; Dearborn, Michigan; Canton, Ohio; and Matteson, Illinois, along with the grand reopening of a restaurant in Flint, Michigan. These openings represent an important next step in the brand’s development strategy, bringing Savvy Sliders into new communities while continuing to build density and strengthen its presence in established markets. “More opportunity lies ahead for Savvy Sliders than ever before,” said Sonny Asker, Chief Operating Officer of Happy Group. “We’re building momentum with experienced franchise partners who believe in the brand and its growth potential. Our focus is turning that opportunity into new restaurants, supporting our operators and building a stronger foundation for long-term growth. We’re just getting started.” Multi-Unit Development Agreements Build Long-Term Growth Pipeline Looking ahead to 2027 and beyond, Savvy Sliders has secured several multi-unit agreements that reflect growing interest from experienced franchise operators and developers looking to bring the brand into new or emerging markets. As development advances, each new restaurant is expected to create approximately 30 to 40 local employment opportunities, contributing to economic activity and community investment in the markets Savvy Sliders serves. As the brand continues to expand, its focus remains on disciplined development, franchisee support, operational consistency and delivering a distinctive guest experience. “Our goal has always been to build a strong brand that delivers great food, creates opportunities for our team members, and makes a difference in the communities we serve,” added Sonny Asker. “As we grow, our Bigger, Better, Bolder, More 2 Love philosophy will continue to guide us, both in what we serve to our guests and how we give back to our guests.” The post Savvy Sliders Continuing Growth Momentum Into 2027 appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Leilão de itens do Banco Master reúne de raquete mata-mosquitos a cadeiras de R$ 100 mil
articles.titleKo: Leilão de itens do Banco Master reúne de raquete mata-mosquitos a cadeiras de R$ 100 mil
articles.originalSummary: Uma caixa-bar de R$ 42 mil, uma poltrona por R$ 47 mil, dois quadros por R$ 30 mil, uma raquete elétrica que mata mosquitos em um combo de itens de R$ 6 mil e conjuntos de 20 cadeiras de escritório por R$ 100 mil. Esses são alguns dos itens do leilão dos móveis e objetos de escritório que pertenciam ao Banco Master e ao Will Bank, instituições ligadas ao banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro. O pregão começou nesta segunda-feira, 9, às 9h30, pela plataforma Kwara, com 445 lotes de móveis, decoração, eletrônicos e equipamentos utilizados nos escritórios dos bancos. Na primeira hora de disputa, alguns itens já acumulavam milhares de ofertas. A poltrona Tetê, por exemplo, começou de R$ 25 mil e chegou a registrar mais de 2 mil lances em menos de uma hora de leilão. A oferta foi encerrada com quase o dobro do lance inicial, saindo por quase R$ 48 mil, em consulta realizada pela reportagem. O leilão ofertou ainda um lote com aproximadamente 25 cadeiras Verus Interwave, da Herman Miller. O valor alcançou R$ 50.010, após 627 lances. Já um conjunto de aproximadamente dez cadeiras do mesmo modelo estava cotado em R$ 28.540, com 611 ofertas. Também havia itens com valores bem mais modestos. Cerca de 40 minutos após o início do pregão, um lote com nove suportes e acessórios era ofertado por R$ 70, ainda sem lances. Uma sanduicheira Cadence, por R$ 157, recebeu sete ofertas, e monitores Dell tinham valores de R$ 171 e R$ 211. Também estavam disponíveis um forno elétrico por R$ 205 e um puff por R$ 227. Um combo com fritadeira Airfryer, micro-ondas e sanduícheira estava saindo por R$ 765. Já o trio com cafeteira, garrafa térmica e liquidificador estava com lance de R$ 322. Outro combo, desta vez com itens de decoração, incluindo uma raquete elétrica que mata insetos, estava saindo por R$ 6,2 mil e tinha apenas um lance após uma hora de leilão. O catálogo reúne modelos de cadeiras de marcas conhecidas no mercado de mobiliário corporativo, como Herman Miller e Haworth, além de peças de design de fabricantes como Artefacto e Fernando Jaeger. Há ainda estações de trabalho de elevação automática, mesas, sofás e poltronas. Entre os itens disponíveis estão televisores, notebooks, frigobares, geladeiras, adegas, congeladores, cafeteiras, fornos industriais, pratos, copos, faqueiros, lixeiras e extintores. Também há vasos com plantas artificiais e equipamentos para cozinhas corporativas. Uma televisão LG de 98 polegadas e modelos da Samsung também integram o catálogo. O leião inclui desde pequenos utensílios até conjuntos de mobiliário corporativo de alto padrão. A venda é realizada em lotes, que podem reunir várias unidades de um mesmo produto. Um dos exemplos é o conjunto de aproximadamente 20 cadeiras Cosm Média, da Herman Miller, cujo lance inicial era de R$ 98 mil. O leilão é parte do processo de liquidação extrajudicial do Banco Master e do Will Bank. Os recursos obtidos com a venda dos bens serão destinados ao pagamento de credores das instituições. Além do pregão iniciado nesta segunda-feira, há um segundo leilão previsto, com outros 250 lotes de cozinha, que segue até 30 de novembro. Os dois eventos reúnem mais de 700 lotes, com expectativa de arrecadação mínima de R$ 1,7 milhão, de acordo com informações da Kwara. Com informação do Estadão de Conteúdo (Jayanne Rodrigues). Esses são alguns dos itens do leilão dos móveis e objetos de escritório que pertenciam ao Banco Master e ao Will Bank, instituições ligadas ao banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro.
O pregão começou nesta segunda-feira, 9, às 9h30, pela plataforma Kwara, com 445 lotes de móveis, decoração, eletrônicos e equipamentos utilizados nos escritórios dos bancos.

Papa Johns is inviting customers to put every slice to the test with the launch of Snap a Pizza, Get a Free Pizza. Starting Monday, the two-week promotion turns pizza night into an opportunity to be heard, encouraging customers to share photos and honest feedback about their orders. By tapping into the everyday ritual of “the phone eats first,” Papa Johns is turning customer feedback into actionable insights that will help improve the customer experience, while rewarding participants with a FREE large one-topping pizza for sharing their unfiltered take. Real pizza. Real feedback. Real rewards. “We see the pizza pics, the unboxings and the hot takes online every day, and we know our customers aren’t shy about sharing what they think,” said Chris Lyn-Sue, Global Chief Marketing Officer at Papa Johns. “ With Snap Pizza, Get a FREE Pizza, we’re inviting that feedback directly. Every photo and every review helps us better understand what customers love and where we can improve as we continue our journey to deliver a better experience every time they choose Papa Johns.” How Snap a Pizza, Get a Free Pizza Works: Papa Rewards members can participate in seconds: Sign In/Create: Sign in to your Papa Rewards account and opt in to SMS/text messages. Not a member yet? No problem. You can create an account and opt into SMS/text message alerts to be eligible for the offer. Order: Grab your favorite pizza through the Papa Johns app or online at PapaJohns.com ($15 minimum order required) Message Alert: Wait for a text from Papa Johns Snap: Take a real, unedited photo of your pizza before digging in. Drop the Real Review: Upload the photo and leave your honest feedback on the bake, crust, and overall experience. Get Paid in Pizza: Once your photo is confirmed, instantly unlock a free large one-topping pizza in your Papa Rewards offers, valid with a minimum $5 purchase on your next order Snap a Pizza, Get a Free Pizza is the first expression of Papa Johns broader Unbox Better strategy announced in November. HTeaO, the nation’s leading iced tea franchise, announces the grand opening of its new location in Burnet, Texas, on Saturday, November 7, 2026. Located at 1408 S. Water Street, Burnet, TX, the new store is owned and operated by franchise owners Marcus Dawes and Randyn Tenery of Burnet Tea LLC, who also own an HTeaO location in Cedar Park, Texas. HTeaO offers a wide range of ultra-premium tea, water, and coffee products and caters to customers both in-store and through convenient drive-thru services. Each location boasts 20+ meticulously crafted flavors of sweetened and unsweetened tea, made using a proprietary water filtration system and 100% natural ingredients. Building on the success of their HTeaO location in Cedar Park, franchise owners Marcus Dawes and Randyn Tenery saw Burnet as an ideal community for their next store. With its small-town charm, growing population, and location in the heart of the Texas Hill Country, Burnet offered an opportunity to expand their presence in Central Texas while introducing HTeaO to a new customer base. The new store, conveniently located along South Water Street, will serve residents and visitors with the brand’s signature selection of freshly brewed teas, coffee, and more. “We’ve really enjoyed being part of HTeaO’s growth in Central Texas, and Burnet felt like a natural next step for us,” said franchise owner Marcus Dawes. “It’s a community that’s growing while still holding on to that small-town feel, and we see a lot of opportunity here. We’re excited to build on what we’ve started in Cedar Park and introduce HTeaO to even more people throughout the Hill Country.” “One of the things we love most about HTeaO is how easily it becomes part of people’s everyday lives,” added franchise owner Randyn Tenery. “Whether it’s a quick tea run before work, an afternoon pick-me-up, or grabbing gallons for a family gathering, we want to be that familiar stop people can count on. We’re looking forward to getting to know our Burnet neighbors and becoming part of their routines.” To celebrate its grand opening on Saturday, November 7, HTeaO is treating guests to a variety of special offers throughout opening week. The celebration kicks off with all-day happy hour pricing, featuring buy one, get one free cups of tea on Saturday, November 7, and Sunday, November 8. In addition to the grand opening festivities, the Burnet location is giving back to the community through a round-up campaign benefiting the Hill Country Community Foundation’s scholarship fund. Guests will have the opportunity to round up their purchases to support educational opportunities for local students, furthering HTeaO’s commitment to making a positive impact in the communities it serves. But the savings don’t stop there. HTeaO keeps the good times going all year long with its signature happy hour, offering buy one, get one free on any size HTeaO tea every day from 2–4 PM. It’s the perfect opportunity to explore new flavors or stock up on favorites. Guests can also download the HTeaO app to place orders, earn rewards, and stay up to date on exclusive deals. With the new Burnet location opening, there’s never been a better time to sip, save, and enjoy the refreshing taste of HTeaO! For more information, please visit http://www.HTeaO.com. articles.title: Technology Should Make Restaurant Workers Better, Not Busier
articles.titleKo: Technology Should Make Restaurant Workers Better, Not Busier
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . A disconnected workflow can become a guest problem. It’s 7:15 on a Saturday night, and your restaurant’s dinner rush is getting away from the crew. You’re down a cook. A printer has stopped working. A delivery driver is asking for an order nobody remembers seeing, and the manager is at the counter with an unhappy guest. Someone calls across the line to clarify a modifier. The answer gets lost. They ask again. Now a screen needs attention. Whatever that screen is asking had better be worth stopping for. I spent nearly twenty years in professional kitchens, working my way up to executive chef. Later, I moved into technical engineering, field systems, and software and AI development. Those experiences shape how I look at restaurant technology. I want to know how a system is built, how it connects, and how it recovers when something fails. I also want to know what it asks of someone with wet hands, six things working, and a station they cannot walk away from. A buying decision needs to account for both. Your best people are covering the gaps Experienced restaurant workers get good at keeping problems from reaching the guest. They catch the ticket that doesn’t make sense. They remember which tablet needs a separate update when an item runs out. They know the closing report needs an adjustment, even though nobody wrote down why. Service gets through. The numbers get submitted. From a distance, everything looks functional. Closer up, somebody is doing a lot of extra work. That person may also be training a new hire, watching food quality, and helping a teammate catch up. Every interruption competes with those responsibilities. We recognize these employees as dependable. We should also examine what we keep depending on them to fix. When the same person rescues the same process every day, their competence can hide a design problem. It becomes especially obvious on their day off, when everyone else discovers how much of the operation was living in one person’s head. The employee has become the integration layer Consider what happens when a restaurant runs out of an item. Who updates the POS? Who changes availability on the delivery platforms? How does the counter crew find out? What happens to orders already accepted? If those steps depend on someone remembering every place the item appears, that person is holding the system together. Miss one, and another employee gets to explain why the restaurant sold food it cannot make. A disconnected workflow has become a guest problem. The same thing happens after service. A manager exports a report, cleans it up in a spreadsheet, and enters the results elsewhere. When the numbers disagree, the manager stays longer to figure out why. That work belongs in the cost of the technology. The employee has become the integration layer: moving, correcting, and interpreting information that systems should exchange reliably. If your employee has to remember how two systems disagree, the integration is not finished. Start investigating wherever the instructions include “then go into the other app.” Follow the task through to completion. Count the checks, corrections, and interruptions it takes to get there. Ask what comes off the shift Before buying another system, ask what an employee will finally be able to stop doing. Which task disappears? Which decision becomes easier? What information arrives soon enough to prevent a problem? Then ask what gets added. Someone may need to maintain data, review flagged transactions, charge devices, or clear alerts. Those can be reasonable responsibilities, but they need an owner and time to happen. They cannot simply land on whoever is already the most reliable person in the building. articles.title: Mr. Pickle’s Sandwich Shop Signs Deal to Open First Southern Arizona Location
articles.titleKo: Mr. Pickle’s Sandwich Shop Signs Deal to Open First Southern Arizona Location
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Mr. Pickle’s Sandwich Shop, the innovative sandwich brand serving up its signature sandwiches at more than 60 locations across Arizona and California, has signed longtime Tucson resident and military veteran Daniel Hanamoto as its newest franchisee, with plans to open the brand’s first Southern Arizona location in Tucson. The venture marks a new chapter for Hanamoto, whose more than two decades of military service in Tucson and longtime appreciation for Mr. Pickle’s have helped guide his own path to restaurant ownership. Hanamoto grew up in Hilo, Hawaii, and left to join the military shortly after high school. His service brought him to Davis-Monthan Air Force Base in Tucson in 2003, where he began working as an aircraft electrician on A-10s before later working on to F-16s. What began as a military assignment eventually became a place to call home. Hanamoto and his wife, who shares his hometown roots in Hilo, settled in Tucson, bought a home and raised their three sons together in the city. The idea of owning a restaurant had come up several times in conversations between Hanamoto and his wife over the years. They both had considered what it might be like to lead a restaurant, even looking into a franchise years earlier. Nothing came of those plans, but Hanamoto found himself thinking about a different future after retiring from the military in April 2026 following more than 23 years of service. Hanamoto first discovered Mr. Pickle’s more than a decade ago while visiting his best friend in San Jose, California, who suggested they get lunch at one of his favorite spots. Hanamoto quickly became a fan after trying a Mr. Pickle’s sandwich himself, making it a point to stop by whenever he returned to California. “What I like about Mr. Pickle’s is that they’re always finding ways to keep the menu interesting without losing the quality food and personality that have made so many people fans in the first place,” said Hanamoto. “It’s something I’ve always enjoyed as a customer, and now I want to make sure we’re delivering that same experience in my own restaurant.” After retiring from the military, Hanamoto took a job in a familiar field, but it didn’t offer the kind of challenge he was looking for. The restaurant idea he and his wife had talked about years earlier began to feel more realistic. Hanamoto took the leap to see what it would take to bring a Mr. Pickle’s of his own to the community. Now, with his family’s support, Hanamoto is preparing to trade aircraft maintenance for restaurant operations. He plans to oversee the day-to-day business himself, introducing more people across Southern Arizona to the Mr. Pickle’s signature sandwiches and menu items he’s enjoyed for years. “Mr. Pickle’s stands out from the rest, and I’ve always thought people in Tucson would love it, too,” said Hanamoto. “This is a close-knit community that I’ve called home for more than 20 years. I’m excited to be the one bringing the brand here and giving people the chance to try it.” Hanamoto is currently working with the company’s franchise development team to secure a location, with a potential site under consideration. The Tucson veteran joins Mr. Pickle’s as the company continues to focus on growth through locally operated restaurants, working with franchisees who know their communities and want to play an active role in the businesses they build. “Daniel brings years of experience working with teams and understands the responsibility that comes with leading others,” said Mike Nelson, CEO of Mr. Pickle’s. “His willingness to learn and build a business of his own reflects the kind of commitment we value in our franchisees. We’re proud to have him leading our expansion into Southern Arizona.” Mr. Pickle’s opened its first sandwich shop in Northern California in 1995 before expanding into Arizona following the brand’s purchase by Nelson

Anthony & Luca’s Pizza Kitchen is taking its New York slices, Jersey Boardwalk pies, and real ribeye Philly cheesesteaks to more neighborhoods. Following its Tampa and Jersey Village/Houston openings, the brand announces four new Florida locations, including Sarasota, and four Ohio locations, including Strongsville and Canton, coming soon. The next chapter brings the flavors of New York, New Jersey, and Philadelphia to new cities while building on the brand’s Pinellas Park flagship. The Tampa restaurant opened October 20, 2026, at 7032 W Waters Ave, Tampa, FL 33634. Owned by New Jersey transplants Kevin Seelig and family, the franchise brings a personal taste of home to northwest Tampa. In Texas, franchisee Arnold Baxter, a local Houston entrepreneur, opened the Jersey Village-area kitchen in June 2026 at 9618 Jones Rd, Houston, TX 77065, introducing the menu to northwest Houston. Sarasota, Strongsville, and Canton are already featured as coming soon on the brand’s website. Additional city names and opening dates for the eight planned restaurants will be announced as development progresses. The expansion will carry Anthony & Luca’s beyond its current Florida and Texas kitchens and introduce Ohio diners to a menu rooted in three generations of family recipes. At the center of that menu are hand-tossed pizza and cheesesteaks that share the spotlight. Thin-and-crispy New York pizza starts with dough made to a family recipe using real New York City water. Grande whole-milk mozzarella, house plum-tomato marinara, and pecorino romano bring the classic slice together. Jersey Boardwalk style flips the order, with cheese first and sauce on top; Sicilian goes deep dish and fried in the pan. Signature pies such as Spicy Vodka Roni add creamy vodka sauce, cup-and-char pepperoni, and hot honey ricotta. Philly brings its own unmistakable bite with thin-sliced USDA ribeye, sautéed onions, and melting Cooper Sharp American on toasted Philadelphia rolls. The Guido layers fried Italian chicken cutlet, house vodka sauce, burrata, cup-and-char pepperoni, and hot honey on a seeded South Philly roll. Calzones, panzerotti, wings, and Italian street-food favorites turn the kitchen into more than a pizza stop. For prospective franchisees, that combination is the brand’s invitation to bring pizza, cheesesteaks, hot Italian subs, and Italian street food to their own communities. The franchise program describes in-person opening assistance, training resources, ongoing operational communication, and marketing support. Candidates can discuss available markets and the requirements for their proposed location directly with the franchising team. Guests can explore the menu, find open kitchens, and follow coming-soon locations at anthonyandlucaspizza.com . Five-star Google reviews featured in the brand’s Trustindex widget offer a taste of the response.
