articles.title: Dog Haus Signs Four Major Development Deals Across Southeast, Mid-Atlantic
articles.titleKo: Dog Haus Signs Four Major Development Deals Across Southeast, Mid-Atlantic
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Dog Haus, the chef-driven brand rewriting the rules of American comfort food, is ramping up its U.S. growth with four new area directors who have collectively signed development agreements for more than 400 restaurants across the Southeast and Mid-Atlantic. The group includes some of the largest franchisees from the nation’s top brands, including Jersey Mike’s, Tropical Smoothie Cafe and Dave’s Hot Chicken. The four area directors are the first to sign onto a development model executed by Chris Rigassio, who joined the brand earlier this summer as president and chief development officer. Rather than the broker-style development roles common across franchising, each Dog Haus area director is awarded a territory encompassing roughly 100 restaurants and carries a dual mandate: first, to self-develop restaurants as an operator, and second, to serve as a hands-on coach to the franchisees building alongside them in that market. “Chris has exceeded our expectations, quickly assembling world-class operators and development leaders to drive our national expansion,” said Michael Montagano, CEO of Dog Haus. Area directors also join the brand as equity partners, aligning their returns with the long-term performance of the system they build. The model is designed to support 15 territories and 1,500 restaurants nationwide. “Upon joining Dog Haus, the first thing we set out to build was the structure, not the pipeline,” Rigassio said. “Most brands sell master agreements to salespeople. We are awarding markets to proven, large-scale, multi-brand, multi-state operators. They live in their markets and will provide support in site selection, new store openings, maintaining brand standards and driving unit profitability. Their success will derive from the success of their franchisees, and from building restaurants that will perform for years to come.” The Charter Group of Area Directors Leading development in Florida is Nick Crouch , a 16-year franchise veteran whose portfolio includes more than 135 Tropical Smoothie Cafe locations. Crouch has over 25 years of executive leadership experience spanning hospitality, entrepreneurship and real estate development, including serving as co-founder and CEO of a multistate hospitality company that grew to more than 3,000 team members and $150 million in revenue. “Dog Haus has all the ingredients to become an incredible national success story,” Crouch said. “It has outstanding food, a differentiated concept, an efficient footprint and a leadership team that understands what it takes to support franchisees. I believe there is a tremendous runway for this brand, and I’m excited to help bring it to new markets across Florida.” Joining Crouch are additional area directors with extensive experience operating restaurants, developing markets and growing franchise systems. PG1 Restaurants LLC will develop North Carolina, Tennessee, southern Virginia and West Virginia. The group owns and operates more than 60 restaurants, including Dave’s Hot Chicken locations, with a leadership team representing more than 100 years of collective experience in restaurant operations, development and franchise growth. Kyle Yancey takes the territory covering Delaware, Washington, D.C., Baltimore, Philadelphia and northern Virginia. Yancey is the owner of Opportunities Restaurant Group, which operates Jersey Mike’s locations across Maryland and Washington, D.C. He began with the brand in 2009 and went on to serve as an area director of franchise support, leading franchisee selection, training and support before advancing to vice president of operations. Jesse Allen will lead development across Alabama, Georgia, Louisiana and Mississippi. A restaurant industry veteran with more than 13 years of experience, Allen recently exited his Jersey Mike’s portfolio in New Jersey and Pennsylvania and operates Dave’s Hot Chicken

articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Smokey Mo’s BBQ, the neighborhood barbecue brand known for Texas classics smoked in-house daily with fast, friendly service, is celebrating the grand reopening of its newly remodeled Spring Branch restaurant on Friday, November 13, from 5–7 p.m. The festivities will feature food and drink specials, family-friendly activities and a fundraiser benefiting the Smithson Valley High School Band, while showcasing the brand’s first remodeled drive-thru location. Located at 19851 TX-46 in Berry Oaks Plaza, the restaurant will offer $5 Sloppy Mo’s sandwiches, $2 beers and $1 fountain drinks, along with face painting, giveaways and more. Sales from the event will benefit the Smithson Valley High School Band, giving the community a chance to enjoy their favorite Texas barbecue while supporting local student musicians. Attendees are encouraged to RSVP ahead of the celebration by visiting the Smokey Mo’s Spring Branch website. “Investing in our existing locations is just as important as opening new restaurants, and Spring Branch is a great example of that commitment,” said Craig Haley, CEO of Smokey Mo’s BBQ. “We want to ensure our restaurants continue meeting the needs of local communities, whether they’re stopping in for a quick meal or feeding the whole family. With Thanksgiving around the corner, we’re especially pleased to reopen in time for guests to take advantage of our Heat & Serve holiday offerings, including whole smoked turkeys and complete Thanksgiving feasts.” The Spring Branch remodel marks an important step in Smokey Mo’s ongoing efforts to refresh its restaurants and improve convenience for guests. As the brand’s first remodeled drive-thru location, it also highlights a growing focus on enhancing accessibility and creating a more efficient dining experience. The project is part of a series of restaurant updates designed to strengthen operations while maintaining the neighborhood atmosphere that has defined Smokey Mo’s for more than 25 years. Guests can enjoy a variety of Texas barbecue favorites, including brisket, turkey, pulled pork, sausage and chicken, all smoked in-house daily and served by the plate, sandwich or taco. The menu also features homestyle sides, desserts and breakfast options, offering something for every appetite throughout the day. In addition to its everyday offerings, Smokey Mo’s provides catering services for events of all sizes, from office lunches to family celebrations and local gatherings. Beyond its restaurant remodels, Smokey Mo’s continues investing in the infrastructure supporting its next phase of growth. Recent improvements include a redesigned website, PAR Online Ordering and PAR POS across its system, aimed at streamlining operations and enhancing the ordering experience. The brand also recently named Von Dawson Vice President of Franchise Development to lead its development pipeline and expand its presence in new and existing Texas markets. With 22 restaurants across the Austin, San Antonio and Houston areas, Smokey Mo’s remains focused on growing through both franchise development and corporate expansion while strengthening the operations and guest experience at its existing locations. For more information about Smokey Mo’s BBQ, visit smokeymosbbq.com. To learn more about franchise opportunities, visit smokeymosbbq.com/franchising. Chicken Salad Chick, the nation’s only fast casual chicken salad restaurant concept, announced the opening of its second restaurant in The North Star State, located at 11615 Fountains Drive in The Fountains at Arbor Lakes shopping center. The local community is invited to celebrate this grand opening on Tuesday, November 17 when the first 100 guests in line will win free chicken salad for a year*. During the grand opening week, guests can expect to experience the Southern hospitality Chicken Salad Chick is known for while taking advantage of various specials and giveaways. These include: Tuesday, November 17 – Free Chicken Salad for a Year to the First 100 Guests – The first guest in line at 10am will receive one FREE large Quick Chick of chicken salad per week for an entire year. The next 99 guests in line will receive one FREE large Quick Chick of chicken salad per month for a year!* Wednesday, November 18 – The first 50 guests to purchase a meal with two sides will receive a FREE Chick Tote Bag!** Thursday, November 19 – The first 50 guests to purchase a meal with two sides will receive a FREE 40oz Chick Tumbler!** Friday, November 20 – The first 50 guests to purchase a meal with two sides will receive a FREE Chick Hip Bag!** Saturday, November 21 – The first 50 guests to purchase a meal with two sides will receive a FREE Chick Beanie!** Chicken Salad Chick of Maple Grove is owned and operated by the Coffey family, Minnesota natives with strong ties to professional basketball and their local community. Their franchise group, Starting Five LLC, includes Richard, Sheba, Sydney, Nia and Amir Coffey, each bringing a unique set of complementary strengths and experiences to the business. The Coffeys are well known for their accomplishments on and off the court. Richard and Amir both played professionally in the NBA. Richard spent time with the Minnesota Timberwolves, while Amir played six seasons with the Los Angeles Clippers, and most recently for the Milwaukee Bucks and Phoenix Suns. Nia currently plays for the Minnesota Lynx in the WNBA, while Sydney previously played professional basketball overseas. Sheba also has basketball roots, making the sport a defining part of the family’s story. Chicken Salad Chick of Maple Grove marks the family’s first franchise venture. An Army veteran and nonprofit CEO, Richard has extensive experience in leadership and community engagement. Sheba’s background in real estate gives her skills in sales, networking and client relations, while Sydney contributes experience in territory management and business development. Nia and Amir bring discipline, strong work ethics, and high-performance mindsets cultivated throughout their professional basketball careers. Teamwork has been a central theme in the Coffey’s lives, so together, they believe they can build a lasting business rooted in community, service and connection. “Not only are my family and I excited to go into business together, but we’re also grateful for the opportunity to invest in the Minnesota communities that have supported us throughout the years,” said Richard Coffey, co-owner of Chicken Salad Chick of Maple Grove. “We were initially drawn to Chicken Salad Chick because of the brand’s strong community focus, quality product, and growth potential. It aligned perfectly with our family values and desire to start a business that could deliver long-term value for both us and the community we call home. We’re confident our local roots and community ties will help us introduce the brand to new and returning guests across Minnesota.” Chicken Salad Chick is known for its dozen-plus variety of made-from-scratch chicken salad flavors, fresh sides, gourmet soups, signature sandwiches, and desserts. articles.title: Cheba Hut Signs Eight-Unit Development Deal in Oklahoma
articles.titleKo: Cheba Hut Signs Eight-Unit Development Deal in Oklahoma
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Cheba Hut “Toasted” Subs, the counter-culture sandwich shop known for its chill vibes, cottonmouth cures and bold flavors that hit just right, is sparking up new locations in Oklahoma. The brand has signed an eight-unit area development agreement with Oklahoma-based franchise group WGT Concepts LLC, paving the way for additional locations throughout the Oklahoma City and Tulsa markets over the coming years. The expansion is led by entrepreneurs Rose Taylor and Steven VanCauwenbergh, whose first Cheba Hut location in Oklahoma City quickly became one of the brand’s top-performing restaurants. Building on that momentum, the duo plans to grow the brand across the state with new shops in Edmond and Norman, opened August 31st and November 5th respectively, and plans to enter the Tulsa market beginning in 2027. Taylor and VanCauwenbergh bring experience across hospitality, accounting, operations and multi-business ownership, overseeing companies in the restaurant, professional services and investment sectors. Through WGT Concepts, they’ve built their business approach around strong systems, leadership development and long-term scalability. Cheba Hut remains their primary restaurant franchise concept and a brand they intend to continue scaling throughout Oklahoma. The decision to expand was rooted in more than just the business opportunity. Long before becoming franchisees, they were fans of the brand’s personality, culture and ability to create genuine connections with guests. “Oklahoma has always been home for us, and we believe people here are looking for experiences that feel authentic and memorable, not just another place to eat,” said Rose Taylor. “What keeps us investing in Cheba Hut is the way the brand brings people together. Guests walk in for the food, but they stick around because the atmosphere feels welcoming. We’ve seen that firsthand through our first shop, and its what gives us confidence as we continue to grow across the state.” The agreement marks another step in Cheba Hut’s ongoing growth strategy as it continues to move into new and existing markets with experienced operators who understand how to scale while preserving the culture that sets it apart. The Oklahoma development deal also reinforces the demand for distinctive fast-casual brands that offer more than a transactional dining experience. “Rose and Steven understand what makes Cheba Hut click, and they’ve already proven they can bring it to life,” said Seth Larsen, chief development officer of Cheba Hut. “They’ve built a great operation, connected with their community and created the kind of environment that keeps guests coming back. As we continue growing across the country, we’re looking for partners who can do exactly that.” With eight new locations planned, Cheba Hut is positioned to deepen its presence across Oklahoma while continuing its expansion into markets where guests are hungry for something original. articles.title: Mountain Mike’s Opens in Daly City, California
articles.titleKo: Mountain Mike’s Opens in Daly City, California
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Mountain Mike’s Pizza, a leading family-style pizza chain for nearly 50 years, and home of the legendary crispy, curly pepperoni, massive 20-inch Mountain-sized pizzas and dough made fresh daily, is continuing its growth on the San Francisco Peninsula with its Daly City opening. With more than 200 locations across the greater San Francisco Bay Area, the new Daly City restaurant marks the brand’s second location in the city. The restaurant is owned and operated by experienced multi-unit franchisees Jagjit Sethi, Charanpreet Singh and Gurpreet Sandhu, who own two existing Mountain Mike’s locations in the region. The new Mountain Mike’s Pizza is the ideal destination for Bay Area locals to enjoy the brand’s signature experience of “Pizza the Way it Oughta Be!” whether dining in the restaurant, carrying out or having it delivered directly to their door. “We are honored to continue Mountain Mike’s legacy across the San Francisco Bay Area with our newest location in Daly City just miles away from where ‘Pizza the Way it Oughta Be’ started,” said Sethi. “There’s a reason why Mountain Mike’s continues to be a staple in the Bay Area: we consistently deliver high-quality pizza and a family friendly environment the community craves and we’re excited to broaden that experience for Daly City residents.” The spacious 2,000-square-foot Mountain Mike’s Pizza in Daly City features the welcoming, family-friendly atmosphere for which the brand is known. Boasting five big-screen televisions, the new Daly City restaurant is bound to be a go-to destination for sports fans, no matter their preferred team. The Daly City restaurant also includes a weekday all-you-can-eat pizza and salad lunch buffet, a fresh salad bar, domestic and craft beer on tap, a varied wine selection, kids’ arcade games and complimentary Wi-Fi. With extended late-night hours, the restaurant offers even more flexibility for families, sports fans and night-owl diners looking for a quality meal or a place to gather after games and events. There is something for everyone at the new Mountain Mike’s in Daly City, making it an ideal spot for guests of all ages, team parties, family get-togethers, office gatherings and group fundraising events alike. One bite into a cheesy slice of pizza from Mountain Mike’s takes you back to childhood, providing a sense of nostalgia for when pizzas were handmade with the freshest and finest ingredients. From its legendary crispy, curly pepperoni, 100% whole milk mozzarella cheese and a variety of fan-favorite specialty pizzas, Mountain Mike’s has something to satisfy every taste. Whether it’s dine-in, carryout or its own in-house delivery, guests can always count on Mountain Mike’s to ensure quality, freshness, flavor and value. Orders may be placed online, through the Mountain Rewards App or through any of the brand’s third-party delivery partners. The newest Daly City Mountain Mike’s is located at 5999 Mission St., and can be reached by (650) 752-4700. The restaurant is open Sunday through Thursday from 11 a.m. to midnight and Friday through Saturday from 11 a.m. to 1 a.m. For additional information about Mountain Mike’s Pizza, visit www.mountainmikespizza.com. For additional information about the new Daly City location, visit Daly City/Mission St. or find the restaurant on Google and Yelp. articles.title: Vendas da indústria de alimentos a canal de foodservice devem superar R$ 310 bi
articles.titleKo: Vendas da indústria de alimentos a canal de foodservice devem superar R$ 310 bi
articles.originalSummary: As vendas da indústria de alimentos para o canal de foodservice, que engloba bares, restaurantes, lanchonetes, padarias e outros estabelecimentos de alimentação fora do lar, devem superar R$ 310 bilhões em 2026, estimou a Associação Brasileira da Indústria de Alimentos ( Abia ). O montante representa crescimento nominal de 7,5% a 8,5% em relação aos R$ 287,9 bilhões registrados em 2025. Em termos reais, a expansão projetada é de 2%, em meio ao aumento dos custos de produção e a mudanças no comportamento do consumidor, que tem se mostrado mais seletivo na hora de comer fora de casa. Os gastos com alimentação representam cerca de 22% das despesas das famílias brasileiras. Desse total, a parcela destinada à alimentação fora do lar deve alcançar 30,5% em 2026, o maior nível desde a pandemia, mas ainda abaixo dos 34,7% registrados em 2019, antes da crise sanitária. Os dados fazem parte do Balanço Econômico do Food Service, apresentado pela Abia durante o 19º Congresso ABIA de Food Service, realizado em São Paulo. “O consumidor continua frequentando bares, restaurantes e padarias, mas escolhe melhor onde e quando gastar”, afirmou o presidente executivo da Abia, João Dornellas, em nota. Segundo ele, a indústria precisa acompanhar as mudanças de hábito e as necessidades dos operadores, que enfrentam dificuldades relacionadas a custos e mão de obra. Desafios A pressão sobre as despesas é um dos principais desafios do setor. Os custos industriais avançaram cerca de 10% em 2026, enquanto as embalagens acumularam alta próxima de 20%. O diesel, por sua vez, subiu mais de 15%, encarecendo o frete e a distribuição ao longo da cadeia. Na ponta, a inflação da alimentação fora do lar acumulou 5,57% em 12 meses até setembro, o que exige das empresas um equilíbrio entre competitividade e preços acessíveis ao consumidor. Novos empreendedores Apesar dos custos elevados, o mercado segue atraindo novos empreendedores. Levantamento da Abia em parceria com a Wise Sales aponta a abertura de aproximadamente 420 mil negócios de foodservice em 2025. No mesmo período, 289 mil empreendedores migraram do modelo de Microempreendedor Individual (MEI) para estruturas empresariais de maior porte, movimento que, segundo a associação, sinaliza investimentos e profissionalização no setor. articles.title: Texas Roadhouse Doubles Down on Playbook as Online Hoax Hits Sales
articles.titleKo: Texas Roadhouse Doubles Down on Playbook as Online Hoax Hits Sales
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Texas Roadhouse has seen sales pick back up. A now-deleted August Facebook post, authored by “Nancy Smith,” claimed employees at Texas Roadhouse were engaging in racist behavior. It said they were planning to lick their fingers and touch food of Black customers. The screenshot, which alleged 400,000 people were in on the plan, made the rounds on TikTok and X. As soon as Texas Roadhouse noticed, it launched an internal review and engaged a third-party online forensics firm. It found zero evidence supporting a., this was happening, b., the alleged online group (it was posted in a “White and Proud” forum) existed, and lastly, any current or former Texas Roadhouse employees were connected. Simply, it was an online hoax—a fact agreed on by USA Today and others. Still, analysts expected a dent to surface in Q3 sales. As Peter Saleh, U.S. Bancorp, BTIG managing director and restaurants and food distributors analyst, said earlier, “unfortunately, consumers tend to believe what they read online.” He noted credit card data showed trends flowing negative in September and early October. Texas Roadhouse on Thursday confirmed the dip as the brand’s performance was “negatively impacted,” CEO Jerry Morgan shared. Same-store sales climbed 4.3 percent for the quarter (two-year stack of 10.4 percent) with traffic up 0.7 percent (5 percent two-year). September in particular, however, was dragged by the incident. To illustrate, by month, comps hiked 5.9, 6.8, and 1 percent for Texas Roadhouse’s July, August, and September periods, respectively. And they’re 1.5 percent higher over the opening five weeks of Q4, including a 30 basis points hit from Halloween shifting to a Saturday. CFO Mike Lenihan said there’s been sequential improvement in sales and traffic through October and early into November. Michael Bailen, head of investor relations, added Texas Roadhouse saw numbers improve “every week” but admitted recovery perhaps took a bit longer than some expected. “But our operators are out there busting their butts,” he said. “And they’ve doubled down on everything they’re doing. And if there’s any group of managers and operators out there who are up for this challenge, it’s the Texas Roadhouse managing partners and the whole teams out there who are compensated off their restaurants.” “So, they’re out there and working, and not sitting back just waiting to see what might happen,” Bailen added. Morgan and Texas Roadhouse leadership recently completed their annual fall tour, which allows executives to speak across the table with operators. He said overall sentiment was positive despite recent setbacks and there’s been momentum in stores affected by the hoax. And to Bailen’s point, it didn’t require Texas Roadhouse to toss any playbooks aside and reinvent its approach. “There’s no doubt that our operators are doing what business owners do,” he said. “They’re doubling down on Legendary Food, Legendary Service, local store marketing, and being great partners in their communities.” Morgan said conversations centered on strengthening the brand’s market positioning. Food, value, and trust, he explained. “And so, I think that was the real marching orders,” he said. “We’ll continue to focus on our early dine offering, our ‘Wild West Wednesday,’ and the things that we can do. But mostly, it’s about making sure that every guest that walks through those doors, we’re taking great care of and that we’re going out in our communities and shaking hands with folks we might have seen in a little while and trying to engage.” Morgan noted Texas Roadhouse would lean into “other avenues” if it has to. But trends and signs thus far show the hoax to be a fleeting episode. “Absolutely, our sales are coming back,” he said. Lenihan noted mix improved sequentially throughout Q3, and dining room and to-go figures reported positive in August and September. Averag

articles.title: ‘Verdadeiro confisco’, diz decisão de juíza em SP que liberou 3 bets; entenda o que aconteceu
articles.titleKo: ‘Verdadeiro confisco’, diz decisão de juíza em SP que liberou 3 bets; entenda o que aconteceu
articles.originalSummary: A desembargadora Adriana Pileggi de Soveral, da 3ª Turma do Tribunal Regional Federal da 3ª Região ( TRF3 ), autorizou três casas de apostas, as bets, a voltar a funcionar no Brasil. A decisão suspende, exclusivamente para a empresa, os efeitos da extinção antecipada de sua outorga e o bloqueio de seus domínios eletrônicos impostos pela Medida Provisória editada pelo presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT). A magistrada deferiu o pedido de antecipação de tutela recursal interposto pela empresa CDA Gaming Ltda., assegurando a continuidade de suas operações de apostas de quota fixa. A disputa teve início após a edição da MP nº 1.394, editada em 25 de setembro, que proibiu a exploração, a oferta, a intermediação e a publicidade de apostas em todo o território nacional, determinando a extinção de todas as autorizações. A CDA Gaming Ltda., que diz ter investido R$ 30 milhões no negócio, impetrou Mandado de Segurança com pedido de liminar na 26ª Vara Cível Federal de São Paulo. A Justiça da primeira instância negou o pedido liminar, ponderando que a “proteção do interesse público e a salvaguarda da população contra os impactos negativos dos jogos deveriam prevalecer sobre a segurança jurídica pleiteada pela empresa’. A empresa recorreu ao TRF-3 e sustenta que a medida provisória “viola os princípios constitucionais da segurança jurídica, da confiança legítima e da proporcionalidade, uma vez que extinguiu abruptamente uma outorga onerosa por prazo determinado sem qualquer previsão de ressarcimento do valor investido”. “A evocação do termo ‘interesse público’ não confere à Administração o poder mágico de alterar subitamente o acertado com eventual contratado, correndo o risco de descrédito total em relação aos contratos efetuados com a Administração Pública”, destacou a relatora na decisão. Além disso, a desembargadora diz que a MP configura um “verdadeiro confisco”, ferindo o princípio do bona fide (boa-fé) e o princípio da não-surpresa, pilares do Estado Democrático de Direito. A decisão liminar tem efeito até o julgamento de mérito do Mandado de Segurança ou deliberação do colegiado da 3ª Turma do TRF3. AGU prepara recurso A Advocacia-Geral da União (AGU) prepara um recurso contra decisão do Tribunal Regional Federal da 3ª Região (TRF3) que autorizou a retomada de três casas de apostas online da empresa CDA Gaming Ltda. O recurso deve ser apresentado diretamente ao presidente do TRF3, Luís Antonio Johonsom di Salvo. Em outubro, o desembargador já suspendeu uma liminar que permitia à plataforma de apostas Stake continuar operando no Brasil até 25 de outubro. A decisão atendeu a um pedido da AGU. articles.title: Que crise, se está tudo movimentado?
articles.titleKo: Que crise, se está tudo movimentado?
articles.originalSummary: Qualquer fim de semana em São Paulo desmente a palavra crise. Fila no restaurante, ingresso esgotado, estacionamento de shopping disputado vaga a vaga. Quem olha só para o corredor conclui que o consumidor vai bem. Os números contam outra história. Segundo a Confederação Nacional do Comércio de Bens, Serviços e Turismo ( CNC ), 82% das famílias brasileiras chegaram ao segundo semestre endividadas, o maior patamar da série, e quase 30% têm contas em atraso. O Comitê de Política Monetária (Copom) interrompeu o ciclo de cortes e manteve a Selic em 13,75%. E o número de empresas inadimplentes chegou ao recorde de 9,1 milhões. As duas leituras são verdadeiras ao mesmo tempo. O erro estratégico é planejar a Black Friday, o Natal e 2027 com base em apenas uma delas. Cheio não é o mesmo que saudável Em 2025, os shoppings faturaram R$ 200,9 bilhões , recorde nominal, mas com alta de apenas 1,2%, abaixo da inflação. O Dia das Crianças ajuda a ler o momento: as vendas da semana subiram 3,7%, enquanto a cesta ligada à data ficou 6,7% mais cara, segundo a CNC. Em volume, o consumidor levou menos. E o destaque não foi o brinquedo: recreação e lazer cresceram 54%. Para o lojista, essa conta tem um efeito pouco discutido. Quando a venda cresce abaixo da inflação e o aluguel segue corrigido por índice, o custo de ocupação sobe como proporção do faturamento, mesmo com a loja cheia. Fluxo não paga aluguel. Conversão paga. Fluxo virou indicador de humor, não de saúde. O painel que importa cruza conversão, ticket médio, frequência de recompra e custo de ocupação sobre venda real. Quem ainda leva ao conselho apenas o número de visitantes está medindo vitrine, não negócio. A crise não esvazia, troca o carrinho O consumidor endividado não some. Corta primeiro o que exige parcela longa: a geladeira, o sofá, a TV em doze vezes, e preserva o que cabe no bolso de hoje: o café, o cinema, o jantar com os amigos, o passeio com as crianças. O mercado americano batizou esse comportamento de little treat culture, a cultura da pequena recompensa. Quando a grande compra sai do alcance, o consumidor passa a se permitir pequenos prazeres frequentes, de baixo valor e consumo imediato, como forma de preservar a sensação de controle e de bem-estar. É a versão contemporânea do efeito batom, que em crises anteriores sustentou as vendas de itens pequenos de beleza. No Brasil de 2026, o sintoma aparece no mix dos shoppings: alimentação e bebidas responderam por 27% das marcas em expansão no segundo trimestre, e quem liderou as inaugurações foi a Milky Moo, uma rede de milkshakes. O desejo não morreu. Ficou menor, mais frequente e mais imediato. O aperto também aparece no supermercado. Após a proibição das apostas online, em 25 de setembro, as vendas do setor cresceram 6,5% e 6,3% nas duas semanas seguintes, segundo a Abras, puxadas por arroz, óleo e café. A causalidade ainda é debatida, mas o sinal é eloquente: qualquer folga vira comida antes de virar desejo. A crise de 2026, portanto, não é de demanda. É de parcela. Sofre quem depende de vender bem durável em prazo longo, justamente o compromisso que o consumidor deixou de assinar. A loja como ativo de marca Nesse cenário, a loja física virou o lazer mais barato da cidade. Para o varejo, é uma oportunidade maior do que parece. Quando o preço vira a única conversa, e a Black Friday é o auge disso, toda marca fica parecida com a concorrente da aba ao lado. A experiência é o que diferencia, e a loja é onde ela é mais difícil de copiar. Na série The Halo Effect, o ICSC mostrou que abrir uma loja eleva, em média, 37% o tráfego do site da marca naquele mercado. A edição mais recente vai além: a abertura aumenta em 6,9% as vendas online na região, e o fechamento as derruba em 11,5%. A loja não é só ponto de venda. É mídia e motor do digital. Esse papel pesa mais agora, porque conquistar cliente pela tela ficou mais caro. Segundo a Kobe, a Black Friday deste ano pode ter o custo de aquisição mais alto da história, e, desde out

Fila no restaurante, ingresso esgotado, estacionamento de shopping disputado vaga a vaga.

articles.title: O ponto cego do varejo: como o crédito na ponta destrava as vendas de smartphones
articles.titleKo: O ponto cego do varejo: como o crédito na ponta destrava as vendas de smartphones
articles.originalSummary: Todo executivo do varejo acompanha de perto o faturamento do dia anterior, a performance por loja e a variação do tíquete médio. Existe, contudo, um indicador crítico que raramente entra no painel de bordo: o volume de receita perdido na etapa final do pagamento. O cliente escolhe o smartphone, valida as especificações, concorda com o preço e acompanha a demonstração. Na hora de fechar a compra, esbarra no limite do cartão ou na recusa do crediário tradicional. Ele deixa a loja sem o aparelho e, para a loja, vira apenas mais uma estatística invisível: o cliente que “só estava pesquisando”. Essa lacuna está longe de ser um evento isolado. Uma pesquisa do Instituto Locomotiva, encomendada pela PayJoy, aponta que 70% dos consumidores das classes C, D e E já desistiram de comprar um smartphone por falta de crédito ou limite no cartão. Costumo dizer que crédito negado é venda perdida. Por isso, a oferta de crédito não pode ser tratada como um mero processo burocrático de caixa, mas sim como pilar estratégico de conversão, no mesmo nível de precificação, sortimento e atendimento. A relevância dessa questão fica evidente ao olhar para a dinâmica do consumo no Brasil: as classes C, D e E representam cerca de 80% da população, segundo a FGV Social, e dependem do parcelamento para adquirir produtos de maior valor. Esse público movimenta a economia diariamente, mas enfrenta modelos tradicionais de crédito que não acompanham sua realidade – seja pelo uso intenso do limite do cartão ou pela informalidade, que atinge cerca de 37% da população ocupada (IBGE). Para profissionais autônomos, motoristas e prestadores de serviço, a ausência de um holerite tradicional não reflete falta de capacidade financeira, especialmente quando o smartphone é a própria ferramenta de trabalho e geração de renda. Tratar o crédito como estratégia A alternativa de financiamento precisa aparecer quando o cliente ainda está escolhendo o aparelho, e não só depois que o cartão é recusado, e nesse ponto a loja física leva vantagem por ter mais margem de negociação. Em seguida vem o preparo da equipe, já que uma opção de financiamento que o vendedor não sabe apresentar dificilmente vira venda. O treinamento contínuo deve ensinar a reconhecer os perfis que tendem a ser recusados no crédito tradicional e a explicar com clareza entrada, parcelas, valor total e consequências do atraso. Por fim, e na minha avaliação o ponto mais negligenciado, é identificar os clientes que desistem antes mesmo de iniciar uma solicitação de crédito. O varejo normalmente acompanha propostas, recusas, aprovações e vendas concluídas, mas esses indicadores não mostram os atendimentos que deixam de avançar antes de uma proposta ser registrada. Um registro simples no PDV, como “cliente saiu por falta de crédito”, já ajuda a dar visibilidade a essas perdas. Já entre as propostas aprovadas, convém não confundir aprovação com conversão: uma aprovação que não vira venda pode apontar outro problema, como entrada alta ou parcela que não cabe no orçamento. A prova de que essa disciplina gera resultados práticos vem da parceria entre a PayJoy e a Casa & Vídeo , iniciada em março de 2024 e que acompanho de perto. Na telefonia do varejo físico, a aprovação média dos crediários convencionais costuma ficar abaixo de 20%. Com um modelo de avaliação desenhado especificamente para esse perfil de cliente, a taxa de aprovação na Casa & Vídeo atingiu 86% desde o início da operação. O tempo para preencher e analisar uma proposta caiu de cerca de 25 minutos para dois a três e, no pico, o financiamento respondeu por uma em cada quatro vendas de smartphones de toda a rede. Essa eficiência passou pela introdução de parcelas quinzenais, que superaram as resistências iniciais do time de vendas ao se alinharem perfeitamente ao fluxo de caixa de trabalhadores autônomos e informais. articles.title: Panvel fecha 3T com lucro de R$ 46,3mi, alta de 35,4%; digital avança 46,6%
articles.titleKo: Panvel fecha 3T com lucro de R$ 46,3mi, alta de 35,4%; digital avança 46,6%
articles.originalSummary: O Grupo Panvel ( PNVL3 ) teve lucro líquido ajustado de R$ 46,374 milhões no terceiro trimestre de 2026, alta de 35,4% em relação a igual período de 2025. Um dos impulsos foi o digital. A participação dos canais subiu 46,6% no período, disse a companhia em relatório reportado ao mercado . “Nos canais digitais, as vendas somaram R$ 792,4 milhões, equivalentes a 46,6% da receita bruta do varejo, com avanço de 20,2 p.p. em relação ao 3T25. O resultado reflete os esforços da companhia em seu projeto de digitalização do cliente dentro da loja. Por meio dessa iniciativa, a companhia unificou a jornada do cliente entre os canais e ampliou de forma expressiva sua base comunicável”, disse a Panvel. No 3T26, o market share da companhia na região sul saltou 13,5%, avanço de 0,7 p.p. na comparação anual, com ganhos nos três Estados e em todas as 21 regiões intermediárias avaliadas pela IQVIA. No trimestre, a Panvel realizou 14 inaugurações, encerrando o período com 677 lojas. Os produtos de marcas próprias mantiveram trajetória consistente de crescimento no trimestre, reforçando seu papel como importante diferencial competitivo dentro do portfólio da Companhia. No 3T26, excluindo da base as vendas de produtos GLP-1, a participação de Produtos Panvel atingiu 8,2% de participação nas vendas do varejo. No total, essa participação alcançou 7,3%, crescendo 15,0% na comparação anual. O Ebitda ajustado consolidado foi de R$ 96,815, alta de 21,2%. A empresa teve uma receita bruta do varejo de R$ 1,699 bilhão, expansão de 15,3%. A dívida líquida encerrou o terceiro trimestre de 2026 em R$ 320,2 milhões. A empresa informou que a dívida bruta caiu de R$ 614,4 milhões para R$ 549,6 milhões no período. A alavancagem dívida líquida/Ebitda ajustado LTM foi de 0,8 vez no terceiro trimestre de 2026, ante 1,0 vez no terceiro trimestre de 2025 e 0,9 vez no segundo trimestre de 2026. O resultado financeiro ficou negativo em R$ 11,978 milhões, ante R$ 9,829 milhões negativos em igual período do ano passado, “patamar estável na comparação anual”. Da Redação com Estadão Conteúdo. articles.title: Is Competition Catching Up to Dutch Bros?
articles.titleKo: Is Competition Catching Up to Dutch Bros?
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Dutch Bros finished Q3 with 1,273 locations. Dutch Bros is still growing sales and bringing more customers through its drive-thrus. But its Q3 results had some investors questioning if the increasingly crowded beverage market is starting to catch up with it. CEO Christine Barone said the company isn’t seeing that happen. The chain delivered 4.4 percent systemwide same-store sales growth in Q3, extending its streak of positive comps to 14 consecutive quarters. Customer visits increased for the ninth straight quarter, while revenue climbed 30 percent to $550 million. Still, systemwide comps slowed from 5.8 percent in Q2 and fell below Wall Street expectations. Company-operated same-store sales increased 5.4 percent, compared with 8.3 percent in the previous quarter. A more cautious full-year outlook added to analysts’ questions about consumer spending, emerging drive-thru competitors, and established restaurant brands pushing further into beverages. Barone acknowledged some uneven customer behavior during the quarter, potentially influenced by rising gas prices. But she drew a distinction between that volatility and customers choosing other brands. “We’ve had lots of competition since 1992,” Barone said. “Most markets, really every single market we enter, we are near other competitors.” What has changed is the number of brands pursuing similar occasions, including emerging drive-thru chains with comparable menus and quick-service players expanding their beverage offerings. To assess that pressure, Dutch Bros examined its performance near 7 Brew. The two brands now both have at least 20 shops in four states, giving Dutch Bros a larger base from which to evaluate the relationship between competitor proximity and sales volumes. Whether a competing location was a quarter-mile, half-mile, or mile away made no difference to Dutch Bros’ AUV. “So we feel incredibly comfortable going into any different competitive situation,” Barone said. She also said the broader QSR push into beverages hasn’t affected the business. Dutch Bros’ energy category continued to expand, reaching 27 percent of menu mix following the early-May introduction of Myst Energy Refreshers. Before that launch, energy accounted for roughly 25 percent. The company’s confidence in its competitive position comes as it prepares to accelerate development. Dutch Bros opened 48 shops in Q3, bringing its footprint to 1,273 locations. It remains on track for at least 185 openings this year and expects approximately 250 in 2027, primarily company-operated shops in existing states. It also has full visibility into the real estate pipeline needed to reach 2,029 shops in 2029. The strategy is less about planting flags in new states than making Dutch Bros a more convenient option in markets it already serves. More shops put the brand closer to where customers live and work, giving it a better chance to become part of their daily routines. That approach comes with some sales transfer between locations. “Our modeling now, I think, is very good at understanding how much cannibalization we will have as we go into a market,” Barone said. “And we feel very comfortable opening new shops that are more convenient for our customers and if they switch from one shop to another.” CFO Josh Guenser acknowledged that next year’s emphasis on existing markets could produce an elevated level of cannibalization. The company hasn’t quantified that potential impact, but incorporates sales transfer into site underwriting and guidance. New-shop performance continues to support the expansion plans. Q3 openings are annualizing at approximately $2 million in sales, ahead of the company’s $1.8 million second-year underwriting framework. Applebee’s latest appetizer hit began with work customers never saw. Nearly two years before Cheeseburger Wonton Tacos reached the menu, Dine Brands committed to building an eight-quarter pipeline of new food. The goal was to establish a regular cadence of one new entrée and one new appetizer each quarter, giving customers fresh reasons to visit without starting the development process from scratch. That investment is now reaching dining rooms. Bacon Cheeseburger Wonton Tacos became Applebee’s strongest new appetizer launch since the pandemic, surpassing Loaded Potato Waves, which debuted the previous quarter. “And what you’re seeing this year is the result of all that work for the past year and a half,” says Dine CEO John Peyton. The menu work helped Applebee’s return to positive domestic same-store sales in Q3, up 0.9 percent. IHOP posted a 0.8 percent increase and extended its traffic outperformance against Black Box to seven consecutive quarters. Dine is seeking more durable gains through restaurant improvements and development alongside food innovation. Company revenue increased 15.1 percent to $248.9 million, primarily because of additional company-operated restaurant sales. Adjusted EBITDA was flat at $49 million. Applebee’s quarter started with a strong July supported by Dollarita and the Cheeseburger Wonton Tacos. August and September softened. Peyton attributes some of the slowdown to two weeks without television advertising in August and a September promotion that did not match the earlier launch’s response. The uneven performance underscores the challenge of converting successful promotions into consistent visits. Applebee’s reduced its investment in its NFL partnership after returns fell short of expectations. Its NFL activity now focuses primarily on off-premises wings offers, leaving television advertising more directly tied to food and value. Peyton says brand is improving how it develops products and introduces them to customers. Inspiration comes from international trends, consumer focus groups, and quiet restaurant tests before marketing begins. The O-M-Cheeseburger, inspired by a discovery in Japan, offers a cheese pull suited to social media. The Ultimate Trio gives customers customization and sharing opportunities. Peyton says Applebee’s Gen Z guest share has increased quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year. “We’re getting better at finding them on social channels and telling the the stories in ways that resonate, and that’s why we see improvements there as well,” he says. The work serves a customer base still divided by spending capacity. Higher-income guests are visiting more frequently, according to Peyton, and price-sensitive consumers are more likely to substitute a quick-service meal or eat at home. Dine continues to advertise accessible meals, then merchandise premium products inside restaurants. At IHOP, everyday value brings customers through the door, and products such as Stuffed French Toast create opportunities to spend more. There are modest signs that some diners will stretch their budgets. Value platforms accounted for 25 percent of Applebee’s transactions and 22 percent at IHOP during Q3. That’s right in the range of what the brands have seen over the past several quarters, meaning they haven’t experienced an influx of guests going straight to value. articles.title: 30-Unit Denny’s Operator Files for Bankruptcy
articles.titleKo: 30-Unit Denny’s Operator Files for Bankruptcy
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . EYM Diner has locations in Texas and Florida. A 30-unit Denny’s franchisee filed for bankruptcy, extending a series of financial troubles for restaurateur Eduardo Diaz that’s affected his operations across several major chains. EYM Diner of DFW and EYM Diner of Florida, entities based in Texas and Florida, are the latest businesses connected to Diaz to seek bankruptcy protection. Since 2024, affiliated entities have filed for bankruptcy involving Pizza Hut, KFC, and Panera restaurants, resulting in more than 100 closures across those brands. The breakfast chain is now working with existing franchise partners and creditors to transfer as many affected restaurants as possible to new operators. Denny’s says several locations are financially viable, and franchisees within its system have expressed interest in taking them over. “We have spent the past two years working side by side with Mr. Diaz to support the sale of his Denny’s restaurants; that commitment continues. There are viable restaurants in this group, and franchise partners within our system are willing to step in to help secure their future,” Mark Burgess, senior vice president and chief development officer of Denny’s, said in a statement. The company’s involvement predates the filings. According to Burgess, Denny’s has spent two years assisting Diaz with efforts to sell his restaurants, and that work will continue through the bankruptcy proceedings. The goal is to preserve operations at locations that can succeed under different ownership, protecting jobs and maintaining service for customers. Any ownership transfers would need to proceed through the applicable bankruptcy processes and involve coordination with creditors. Denny’s has not announced any completed transactions. “We are working with those partners and other creditors through the necessary processes to transition operations of as many impacted restaurants as possible to experienced operators in our system,” Burgess said. “For the team members whose livelihoods depend on these restaurants and the guests who count on them, continuity matters. That is where our attention and effort remain.” The latest filings add to a difficult stretch for Diaz’s restaurant businesses, which have experienced financial disputes, lawsuits, bankruptcies, and closures across multiple brands. One of the largest cases involved EYM Pizza, which filed for bankruptcy in July 2024 after a legal dispute with Pizza Hut. The franchisee previously operated approximately 140 Pizza Hut restaurants across several states. Pizza Hut sued the operator over alleged contractual violations, unpaid fees, and poor restaurant performance. The bankruptcy ultimately resulted in the sale of 77 Pizza Hut restaurants to six buyers, with approximately 60 other locations closing permanently. Similar difficulties affected EYM Café, Diaz’s former Panera business in the Houston area. The operator, which once controlled 15 bakery-cafés, filed for bankruptcy after Panera terminated its franchise agreements over alleged violations involving royalty payments, food safety standards, and unpaid vendor invoices. EYM Chicken, the group’s KFC business, filed for bankruptcy in 2025 and shuttered dozens of restaurants. In 2023, EYM King of Michigan shuttered all 26 of its Burger King restaurants in the state following a contractual dispute. The latest bankruptcy also arrives as Denny’s works to improve restaurant profitability through its multiyear Project Grand Slam initiative. The strategy targets average unit volumes of $2.5 million, compared with approximately $2 million previously, through restaurant remodels, operational improvements, menu innovation, technology, and additional sales channels. Project Grand Slam also calls for improving lower-performing restaurants through better staffing, repairs, maintenance, and operational standards. Additional

articles.title: HIT Training Launches Hospitality Employer Call To Action As ‘First Job. Future Career.’ Campaign Champions Better Opportunities For The Next Generation.
articles.titleKo: HIT Training Launches Hospitality Employer Call To Action As ‘First Job. Future Career.’ Campaign Champions Better Opportunities For The Next Generation.
articles.originalSummary: With almost one million young people in the UK currently outside education, employment or training, specialist apprenticeship provider HIT Training (part of The Opportunity Provider – TOP), is calling on the hospitality industry to recognise its vital role in helping the next generation into work. The call comes as the company launches its First Job. Future Career. campaign, introducing Commit to Youth – an initiative encouraging employers to make measurable commitments to creating opportunities for young people. And it comes at a time when the Government is preparing to publish the next stage of the Alan Milburn’ Independent Review into Young People and Work, following his interim findings earlier this year. According to the latest Office for National Statistics figures, an estimated 981,000 young people aged 16–24 were not in education, employment or training between April and June 2026. HIT Training emphasises that hospitality is a leading ‘career starter sector’ and plays a vital role in opening doors to employment and developing the next generation of talent. It says the challenge goes beyond offering more entry-level jobs – employers must also ensure young people are given the support, encouragement and career pathways they need to succeed. Importantly, the campaign also highlights the significant financial incentives available to employers taking on young apprentices. Under current Government arrangements in England, eligible apprentices aged 16–24 can have 100% of their training and assessment costs funded, up to the relevant funding limit. Employers who do not pay the apprenticeship levy may also qualify for a £2,000 hiring payment for eligible new apprentices in this age group, while additional incentives are available for Foundation Apprenticeships. Employers can also benefit from relief on National Insurance contributions for apprentices under 25, subject to earnings thresholds. There is also a 16-18 bonus of £1,000 for all employers of apprentices aged 16-18. HIT Training believes greater awareness and take-up of this support could help more businesses overcome some of the financial barriers to investing in the next generation. Mike Worley, Managing Director of HIT Training says: “Hospitality has always been one of Britain’s great career starter sectors. Some of our most successful chefs, hoteliers and hospitality leaders began with relatively modest first jobs, often discovering skills and ambitions they never knew they had. “But with almost a million young people currently outside education, employment or training, we need to ask whether we’re doing enough to give the next generation that same opportunity. “Crucially, a first chance must be a good first chance. It’s not simply about recruiting a young person into a job; it’s about giving them the support, training and confidence to succeed and showing them where that opportunity could lead. “Through our First Job, Future Career – Commit to Youth , we’re asking hospitality employers to move beyond talking about the problem and make practical commitments to creating opportunities. And we’re ready to help them turn those commitments into successful apprenticeships and lasting careers.” The campaign recognises the considerable commercial pressures facing hospitality employers, including rising employment costs and the challenges of recruitment and retention. It also highlights the importance of supporting existing employees to develop and progress. Investing in experienced team members through apprenticeships can strengthen management capability, improve retention and create opportunities for younger people to enter the workforce. Through Commit to Youth , employers are encouraged to create genuine entry opportunities, remove unnecessary barriers to recruitment, consider Foundation and entry apprenticeships, provide appropriate mentoring and support, and establish visible routes for career progression. articles.title: Dino agenda audiência de conciliação sobre escala 6×1 para o próximo dia 10
articles.titleKo: Dino agenda audiência de conciliação sobre escala 6×1 para o próximo dia 10
articles.originalSummary: O ministro Flávio Dino, do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), marcou uma audiência de conciliação para discutir aspectos da implementação da nova jornada de trabalho após o fim da escala 6×1. O encontro será realizado na próxima terça-feira, 10, às 14h. Dino é relator de ações movidas nesta semana pelas confederações do comércio e da indústria . No despacho, publicado nesta quinta-feira, 5, Dino ressaltou que o objetivo da audiência não é o conteúdo da emenda constitucional que acabou com a escala 6×1. “Não se trata de conciliar quanto ao conteúdo da Emenda Constitucional nº 141/2026, que é plenamente constitucional em sua finalidade e cujo mérito não está sujeito a transação. A redução da jornada e a ampliação do repouso semanal não estão em negociação”, destacou. O ministro acrescentou que a audiência vai se concentrar sobre “aspectos de implementação”, matéria que as entidades interessadas reunidas podem equacionar com maior adequação do que decisão judicial proferida sem sua participação. Ele ainda considerou que o prazo de dois meses para o fim da escala 6×1, questionado pelas empresas, “não se revela, a princípio, inviável”. Ele disse que essa avaliação é “preliminar” e poderá ser revista à luz dos dados que forem levados pelos setores econômicos. O ministro ponderou, por outro lado, que as empresas têm razão sobre a “relevância da autonomia privada coletiva” e destacou que a Constituição reconhece as convenções e acordos coletivos e assegura negociações entre empresas e trabalhadores. “Esse reconhecimento conduz ao dever de buscar a solução consensual”, acrescentou. Dino intimou para o encontro as confederações que representam categorias econômicas, as centrais sindicais que representam os trabalhadores, a Advocacia-Geral da União (AGU), as advocacias do Senado e da Câmara e a Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR). Com informações de Estadão Conteúdo (Lavínia Kaucz). Imagem: STF O post Dino agenda audiência de conciliação sobre escala 6×1 para o próximo dia 10 apareceu primeiro em Mercado&Consumo .

articles.title: Ruby Tuesday Introduces Everyday Fresh Meals Starting at $9.99
articles.titleKo: Ruby Tuesday Introduces Everyday Fresh Meals Starting at $9.99
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Ruby Tuesday has introduced Everyday Fresh Meals: a new value menu offering guests a variety of entrees at four price points starting at $9.99. Available seven days a week, the menu gives guests more flexibility to enjoy Ruby Tuesday favorites at a consistent price. Each meal includes an entree, unlimited trips to The Garden Bar, and a bottomless drink. “Guests shouldn’t have to plan their week around a deal,” says Kevin FitzPatrick, chief marketing officer at Ruby Tuesday. “With Everyday Fresh Meals, we’re making it easier for guests to enjoy their Ruby Tuesday favorites at a consistent price, any day of the week while giving them more flexibility and value whenever they choose to visit.” Everyday Fresh Meal Offerings $9.99: Single American Smashed Burger $11.99: Double American Smashed Burger, Ruby’s Cheeseburger, Big Crispy Chicken Sandwich, or Grilled Chicken Sandwich. $14.99: Deconstructed Chicken Kabobs, Cajun Chicken Pasta, Fish & Chips, or Bacon Cheeseburger. $17.99: 6 oz Rib Eye, Double Hickory Bourbon Chicken, Half Rack of Baby-Back Ribs, or Shrimp Scampi. Each Everyday Fresh Meal comes with unlimited trips to Ruby Tuesday’s signature Garden Bar, featuring more than 60 fresh ingredients, including a variety of dressings, fan-favorite pumpernickel croutons, and chef-prepared salads. Guests can also enjoy a bottomless beverage, with options such as soft drinks, flavored tea, and flavored lemonade. Select entrees are also served with a side, such as fries, a baked potato, mashed potatoes, or a breadstick. For details, visit rubytuesday.com/everyday-fresh-meals. “One of the things that makes Ruby Tuesday special is the variety we offer, from our signature burgers and entrees to our all-you-can-eat Garden Bar,” adds FitzPatrick. “We wanted to bring that variety to the forefront with a selection of meals that gives guests plenty of options, no matter what they’re in the mood for.” This Veterans Day, Ruby Tuesday is thanking the brave men and women who have served or are serving in our U.S. military by inviting U.S. veterans and all active-duty, Reserve, and National Guard service members to enjoy a free Everyday Fresh Meal by showing proof of military service. The offer is valid Wednesday, November 11, 2026, for dine-in only at participating locations. Everyday Fresh Meals are now available at Ruby Tuesday locations nationwide and will also be featured in the brand’s upcoming fall menus, arriving in late November. articles.title: Wonder Takes First Step Toward IPO
articles.titleKo: Wonder Takes First Step Toward IPO
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The company's restaurant footprint has grown significantly in recent months, expanding from 46 locations to approximately 140 since its previous funding announcement in May 2025. Wonder is moving closer to becoming a publicly traded company following years of aggressive expansion and billions of dollars in investment. The food technology company announced Thursday that it confidentially submitted a draft registration statement on Form S-1 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for a proposed initial public offering of Class A common stock. The number of shares Wonder plans to offer and the anticipated price range have not been determined. The potential offering is subject to market conditions, regulatory review, and other factors. The filing marks a significant development for the company founded by entrepreneur Marc Lore, who has assembled a food platform spanning restaurants, delivery, meal kits, and automated kitchen technology. It also follows Wonder’s recent $650 million Series D funding round , which valued the company at $9 billion before the investment. Existing investors Accel, GV, and New Enterprise Associates participated alongside new investments from funds managed by AllianceBernstein, ARK Invest, and Kayne Anderson Rudnick Investment Management. Wonder said the funding would support restaurant expansion, marketplace growth, and continued investments in robotics, AI, and technology. The company’s restaurant footprint has grown significantly in recent months, expanding from 46 locations to approximately 140 since its previous funding announcement in May 2025. Wonder operates a digital food platform that allows customers to order meals from multiple restaurant concepts in a single transaction. Its business includes company-owned restaurants, licensed restaurant brands, local restaurant delivery, and meal solutions. The company has also pursued an aggressive acquisition strategy to expand its capabilities and restaurant portfolio. Its recent purchase of New York City barbecue chain Mighty Quinn’s added eight locations across New York, Florida, and Maryland. Earlier this year, Wonder acquired Blue Ribbon Fried Chicken, which has since expanded across additional Wonder locations. Those deals followed several larger transactions, including the $650 million acquisition of Grubhub, the $186 million purchase of Sweetgreen’s Infinite Kitchen business, and the $103 million acquisition of meal-kit company Blue Apron. The acquisitions have given Wonder access to delivery infrastructure, established restaurant concepts, meal-kit distribution, and automated food preparation technology. Wonder also recently announced a partnership with autonomous drone delivery company Zipline, with plans to introduce on-demand drone delivery in Texas in 2027. Wonder has attracted substantial investment throughout its expansion. Bloomberg reported in 2025 that the company raised $600 million at a valuation exceeding $7 billion. In 2024, Wonder secured another $700 million, including $100 million from Lore. The post Wonder Takes First Step Toward IPO appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Wendy’s is Going Back to Basics to Save its Business
articles.titleKo: Wendy’s is Going Back to Basics to Save its Business
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Wendy’s domestic same-restaurant sales declined 5.7 percent in Q3. Wendy’s is giving its U.S. franchisees permission to start the day later. The burger chain will make breakfast optional at every domestic restaurant, a significant shift in its effort to repair restaurant profitability and win back customers. The decision puts the economics of individual locations ahead of a uniform operating schedule as Wendy’s rebuilds a business still losing substantial traffic. The company estimates the change could unlock up to $200 million in restaurant-level EBITDA across franchise and company restaurants. That benefit would come from eliminating breakfast losses and improving margins during the rest of the day. “Mandating that franchisees operate during a daypart where they lose money is going to do nothing but hurt their business,” CEO Bob Wright said during Wendy’s third-quarter earnings call. The breakfast decision is among the most consequential moves under Dave’s Way, Wendy’s multiyear turnaround strategy. The brand chose to move forward with the comeback and rejected a $1.4 billion takeover offer from an investor group led by billionaire Nelson Peltz. Another big move is a proposed acquisition of up to 163 restaurants from bankrupt franchisee Meritage Hospitality Group. READ MORE : New Wendy’s CEO Vows to Restore Quality and Revive Customer Traffic The changes arrive as Wendy’s domestic same-restaurant sales declined 5.7 percent in Q3. Traffic fell 11.9 percent, partially offset by 6.2 percent average check growth. The comparable sales decline improved 130 basis points from Q2, with traffic improving sequentially through each period of the quarter. Global systemwide sales decreased 5.9 percent. Adjusted EBITDA fell $24.6 million to $113.4 million. Wendy’s studied restaurants that had already stopped serving breakfast before extending the option across the country. Those locations improved profitability at lunch, dinner, and late night, and many recovered all their breakfast sales during other dayparts. A shorter operating day allows restaurants to concentrate manager coverage during busier hours. It also reduces waste associated with low-volume periods. The company had discussed the change with franchisees the night before the call and was beginning to provide information to help them evaluate each restaurant. Wendy’s did not disclose how many locations might discontinue breakfast. Restaurants that keep the daypart will continue receiving product, marketing, and operational support. Wright expects a substantial portion of franchisees to identify locations where breakfast fails the profitability test. The same scrutiny of restaurant economics is driving Wendy’s response to Meritage’s bankruptcy. The parties signed a letter of intent earlier in the week under which Wendy’s would acquire up to 163 locations. Those restaurants are concentrated in markets where the company already operates, giving it an existing field organization and local experience to support performance improvements. Other Meritage markets are expected to transition to franchisees through the bankruptcy process. The proposed acquisition also permits higher and better offers from approved franchisees. “This will be, we think, one of the largest, if not the largest acquisition of franchise-to-company restaurants in the company’s history, certainly in a long, long time,” Wright said. Wendy’s could eventually refranchise acquired restaurants, but Wright did not commit to a timetable. The immediate opportunity is to improve operations and participate financially in their recovery. articles.title: OHG Brands Ready to Tap Into Nostalgia with Leadership Team
articles.titleKo: OHG Brands Ready to Tap Into Nostalgia with Leadership Team
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . While the moniker OHG Brands (standing for Original. Honest. Good) might be new, the concepts under its umbrella are not. That’s a point Anthony Ackil keeps coming back to. Ackil, who created fast casual B.GOOD when he was 26, growing it to 80 stores before selling in 2018, today leads Streetlight Ventures as CEO, an operating and investment company he founded a year after exiting. And now, Ackil and the company sit at the helm of OHG Brands, which emerged in late September as a fresh company from previous FAT Brands. Included are 12 legacy names—Round Table Pizza, Fatburger, Marble Slab Creamery, Johnny Rockets, Fazoli’s, Great American Cookies, Buffalo’s Cafe & Express, Hurricane Grill & Wings, Native Grill & Wings, Pretzelmaker, and Ponderosa and Bonanza Steakhouses—collectively covering 1,700 global units. “I love the brands,” Ackil says in an interview with QSR magazine . “I think they’re iconic. I think there’s strength in them. This idea of a brand being viable for 50 years, like some of our brands—almost all of them—it’s really unique.” The “youngest,” Hurricane Grill & Wings, turned 31 in 2026. When they were founded Round Table Pizza: 1959 Fatburger: 1947 Marble Slab Creamery: 1983 Johnny Rockets: 1986 Fazoli’s: 1988 Great American Cookies: 1977 Buffalo’s Cafe & Express: 1985 (express in 2006) Hurricane Grill & Wings: 1995 Native Grill & Wings: 1978 Pretzelmaker: 1991 Ponderosa: 1965 Bonanza: 1963 (merged in 1989 with Ponderosa) Streetlight Ventures began as a restaurant consulting company with a focus on management, operations, finance, and marketing. When COVID hit, it started taking over brands (it works with concepts like Burton’s Grill & Bar, Anna’s Taqueria, and more ) and was an active buyer. But what it found, like many during pandemic valuation swings, was it couldn’t reach an agreement on price with owners, often founders. Where Streetlight couldn’t acquire the company, though, it started running the business. “And what we created [was] an operating company,” Ackil says. “And it came out of the B.GOOD idea of it’s really hard to run a business. You need every functional area. You need expertise at every different functional area. That’s really where Streetlight came from. It’s the idea of running a business or adding support across every aspect of the business, from finance to marketing to innovation to operations, and lifting the business holistically.” That’s what it’s doing with OHG Brands and its roster of 12 concepts. Streetlight’s team of executives, entrepreneurs, and leaders within the restaurant space, want to drive the business forward by surrounding it with expertise and experience across touchpoints. As part of the effort, OHG announced a host of appointments. Among them: Stephen England, Chief Operating Officer: brings 30-plus years in restaurant operations, including roles as Senior Vice President of Operations at Subway and Vice President of Operating Systems at Dunkin’ Brands. Kelly Hansen, Chief Marketing Officer: brings 20-plus years of restaurant marketing experience spanning QSR to fine dining, including five years in marketing leadership at Raising Cane’s during its period of massive growth. She previously oversaw marketing for Tavistock Restaurant Collection, Lemonade Restaurant Group, and others. Jose Ponce, Chief of Staff and Head of HR: holds more than 15 years of HR experience spanning organizational design, talent strategy, and building HR departments from the ground up across high-growth restaurant and franchise businesses, including Burger King, Tim Hortons, and Popeyes. Artie Jones, General Counsel: formerly Associate General Counsel and VP at BJ’s Wholesale Club, where he advised on complex commercial transactions, enterprise risk, corporate governance, regulatory compliance, employment and litigation strategy, and helped modernize the legal department. articles.title: Coca-Cola Femsa investe R$ 75 milhões em centro de distribuição em Limeira
articles.titleKo: Coca-Cola Femsa investe R$ 75 milhões em centro de distribuição em Limeira
articles.originalSummary: A Coca-Cola Femsa Brasil vai inaugurar um novo centro de distribuição em Limeira, no interior de São Paulo, com investimento estimado em R$ 75 milhões. Desenvolvida no modelo build-to-suit (BTS), a estrutura tem início das atividades previsto para outubro de 2027 e ampliará a capacidade logística da companhia na região. “A nova operação em Limeira representa um importante investimento da Coca-Cola Femsa Brasil, que contribuirá para a geração inicial de 400 oportunidades de emprego e para o desenvolvimento econômico da região. Ao mesmo tempo, fortalecerá nossa estrutura logística, permitindo atender mais de 7,5 mil clientes com mais agilidade e eficiência e nos aproximar ainda mais dos consumidores”, afirma Eduardo Pereyra, CEO da Coca-Cola Femsa Brasil. O centro contará com 4.848 posições de armazenamento e terá capacidade para distribuir todo o portfólio da Coca-Cola Femsa Brasil. A operação atenderá 22 municípios do interior paulista. O empreendimento será instalado às margens da Rodovia Deputado Laércio Corte, conhecida como Limeira-Piracicaba, com acesso às rodovias dos Bandeirantes e Washington Luís. “Limeira tem localização estratégica, infraestrutura e condições favoráveis para receber grandes empreendimentos. A Prefeitura trabalha para apresentar essas vantagens ao mercado e criar oportunidades para a chegada de novos investimentos. A instalação de um dos maiores centros de distribuição da Coca-Cola Femsa no estado reforça esse potencial e representa mais empregos e desenvolvimento para a cidade”, diz o prefeito Murilo Félix. Crescimento de 3,9% em volume no Brasil A Coca-Cola Femsa reportou ao mercado crescimento de 3,9% no volume de bebidas comercializadas no Brasil no terceiro trimestre de 2026 , na comparação com o mesmo período do ano passado. O resultado contribuiu para o avanço das operações da companhia na América do Sul, mas não afastou as preocupações do BTG Pactual com o desempenho do mercado brasileiro em 2027. Em relatório divulgado nesta quarta-feira, 28, o banco projeta estabilidade dos volumes vendidos no País no próximo ano, em um cenário de custo elevado de capital e menor previsibilidade para o consumo. A avaliação acompanha a divulgação dos resultados trimestrais da Coca-Cola Femsa, maior engarrafadora de produtos Coca-Cola do mundo em volume de vendas. Globalmente, a companhia registrou receita de 79,72 bilhões de pesos mexicanos, crescimento de 10,9% em relação ao terceiro trimestre de 2025. Desconsiderando os efeitos cambiais, o avanço foi de 11,3%. articles.title: Privalia passa a oferecer entrega no próximo dia útil em São Paulo
articles.titleKo: Privalia passa a oferecer entrega no próximo dia útil em São Paulo
articles.originalSummary: A Privalia passa a oferecer entrega no próximo dia útil para compras realizadas até o meio-dia, de segunda a sexta-feira. A modalidade, sem cobrança adicional, já está disponível na capital paulista e em sete municípios da Grande São Paulo. A iniciativa amplia os serviços logísticos da plataforma digital de moda e lifestyle, que reúne 20 milhões de clientes no Brasil. O serviço já alcança mais de 98% dos pedidos de produtos participantes na cidade de São Paulo, além de Barueri, Osasco, Guarulhos, Santo André, São Bernardo do Campo, São Caetano do Sul e Mauá. A empresa prevê levar a modalidade a pelo menos outras 20 cidades da Grande São Paulo até o fim de novembro. “A Privalia é conhecida pelas oportunidades de comprar grandes marcas a preços atrativos, e isso não muda. O que faltava era estarmos presentes também quando o cliente precisa do produto para amanhã. Com a entrega no próximo dia útil, passamos a atender essas duas necessidades na mesma plataforma”, afirma Cesar Borges, COO da Privalia. Ainda em 2026, a Privalia pretende expandir a entrega no próximo dia útil para outras regiões, incluindo Belo Horizonte, Campinas e Curitiba. A política de frete da plataforma, incluindo as condições de gratuidade quando aplicáveis, permanece inalterada. As campanhas participantes estão identificadas no site e no aplicativo com o selo “entrega rápida”, permitindo que o consumidor identifique os produtos elegíveis antes de finalizar a compra. Entre as marcas participantes estão Live!, Insider, Lança Perfume e Hering. Operação logística Para viabilizar o novo prazo, a Privalia ajustou os processos de preparação e despacho dos pedidos, alinhando estoque, centro de distribuição e transportadoras. Antes do lançamento, a modalidade passou por uma fase piloto que envolveu cerca de 30 mil entregas. Durante as campanhas de 11.11 e Black Friday, a proposta é manter a entrega no próximo dia útil para todos os produtos identificados como entrega rápida nas regiões atendidas. A modalidade está disponível desde a primeira semana de novembro, no site e no aplicativo da Privalia. articles.title: Presidente do Paraguai renuncia em meio à crise bancária; vice assume
articles.titleKo: Presidente do Paraguai renuncia em meio à crise bancária; vice assume
articles.originalSummary: Enquanto a Câmara dos Deputados do Paraguai discutia a abertura de um processo de impeachment contra o presidente, nesta quinta-feira, 5, o mandatário do país Santiago Peña anunciou a renúncia ao cargo, em meio a uma crise financeira causada pela intervenção do Banco Central Paraguaio (BCP) no banco digital Ueno Bank. Abandonado pelo próprio partido, que passou a cobrar sua renúncia, Peña justificou a decisão em nome da estabilidade do país e da necessidade de “preservar nossas instituições”. O vice-presidente Pedro Allana assumirá o cargo. “Me dirijo a vocês em um dos momentos mais difíceis da minha vida, com o coração voltado para o Paraguai e com a convicção de que a nossa República deve estar sempre acima de qualquer pessoa ou circunstância”, disse o presidente, em pronunciamento nas redes sociais. “A história se encarregará de julgar e colocar na sua devida dimensão os acontecimentos que hoje nos cabe vivenciar. Tomei a decisão de apresentar a minha renúncia à Presidência da República”, acrescentou. Crise A crise financeira que sacudiu o Paraguai começou na terça-feira, 3, e se transformou em crise política. Na manhã de hoje, a Câmara iniciou o debate para abertura de um processo de impeachment que contava com o apoio até mesmo da legenda do mandatário, o Partido Colorado. O terremoto político no país vizinho é consequência da liquidação do Ueno Bank, que tinha 2,9 milhões de correntistas, cerca de 60% da população adulta do país. Essas pessoas tiveram seus depósitos congelados. Após a liquidação do banco, o presidente do BC paraguaio, Carlos Carvallo, renunciou ao cargo. Ele foi dirigente do banco digital até 2023, antes de assumir a chefia do Banco Central do país. https Protestos de rua cobram que os responsáveis pela crise sejam punidos. O Ministério Público do Paraguai pediu a prisão de oito pessoas, incluindo o presidente do Ueno, Juan Manuel Gustale. Presidência A crise atingiu o presidente Santiago Peña por ele ter sido acionista, até março de 2025, do grupo que controla o banco, o Grupo Vázquez. Eleito em 2023, o Santiago Peña é um político da direita conservadora do Partido Colorado que há sete décadas controla o poder no Paraguai, exceto por cinco anos (1947-1952). A oposição acusa o governo pelos investimentos realizados pelo Instituto de Seguridade Social (PIS), que é estatal, no Ueno Bank. O banco digital ainda administra o pagamento de pensões de milhares de aposentados e tem cerca de 30% dos depósitos de fundos públicos, estimados em US$ 850 milhões. A oposição responsabiliza Peña pela crise por ele ter nomeado para presidente do BC um ex-dirigente do Ueno. Ao anunciar a renúncia, o presidente pediu desculpas ao povo paraguaio. “Também quero pedir desculpas ao povo, caso em algum momento eu tenha falhado. Nunca foi minha intenção trair a confiança que depositaram em mim. A cada dia, assumi esta responsabilidade com a vontade de trabalhar pelo Paraguai”, afirmou Peña. Partido Colorado O presidente do Partido Colorado e ex-presidente do país, Horácio Cartes, afirmou que a legenda não estará ao lado “do latrocínio de fundos públicos, privados e dos aposentados”. O presidente do Congresso paraguaio, Bachi Nunéz, dois dias antes de pedir a renúncia de Peña, avaliava à imprensa que o presidente não poderia ser responsabilizado porque o Banco Central tinha autonomia institucional. A oposição acusa o Partido Colorado de querer se afastar do escândalo que teria ajudado a construir. A deputada do Partido País Solidário (PPS), Johanna Ortega, destacou, durante a sessão da Câmara, que os recursos dos aposentados estavam sendo depositados em um banco próximo ao presidente Peña. “Temos alertado sobre conflitos de interesses, sobre a utilização de instituições públicas para favorecer negócios privados de uns poucos, e sobre o crime de gestão em proveito próprio — prática na qual este Presidente da República tem incorrido sistematicamente”, afirmou. O Paraguai conta com um fundo garantidor que pode reembolsar até US$ 38 m
