articles.title: CEO da Cimed é alvo de queixa-crime por suposto uso de fórmulas da Suavetex
articles.titleKo: CEO da Cimed é alvo de queixa-crime por suposto uso de fórmulas da Suavetex
articles.originalSummary: A fabricante de produtos de higiene pessoal Suavetex apresentou queixa-crime contra João Adibe, CEO da Cimed, por suposto uso indevido de informações técnicas obtidas durante negociações societárias. Segundo o site Metrópoles , a empresa acusa o executivo de utilizar formulações desenvolvidas por ela no lançamento de seis produtos de higiene bucal. De acordo com a publicação, a Suavetex afirma que as formulações foram compartilhadas com a Cimed para viabilizar o registro dos produtos na Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa). A proposta de sociedade previa que a Suavetex seria responsável pela fabricação, enquanto a Cimed cuidaria da distribuição dos produtos por meio da marca Carmed 12 horas. Em resposta à reportagem da Mercado&Consumo , a Cimed afirma que a queixa-crime representa mais uma tentativa da Suavetex de reverter as sucessivas derrotas que vem sofrendo na esfera cível. “A Cimed confia que o Poder Judiciário, como já fez, reconhecerá a improcedência das alegações.” “Esse posicionamento tem sido reconhecido de forma consistente pelo Poder Judiciário, tanto em decisões de primeira quanto de segunda instância, que vêm reiteradamente negando os pedidos apresentados pela Suavetex”, diz a empresa. A Cimed também considera “especialmente grave a tentativa da Suavetex de transformar uma controvérsia comercial, marcada pelo insucesso das medidas adotadas na esfera cível, em uma verdadeira aventura jurídica de natureza criminal”. “A companhia não admitirá imputações falsas ou infundadas que atinjam a honra e a reputação de seus representantes. Acusações dessa natureza terão consequências jurídicas, e a Cimed adotará todas as medidas cabíveis, nas esferas cível e criminal, para responsabilizar seus autores”, completa. Com informações de Metrópoles. Imagem: Divulgação O post CEO da Cimed é alvo de queixa-crime por suposto uso de fórmulas da Suavetex apareceu primeiro em Mercado&Consumo .

Segundo o site Metrópoles , a empresa acusa o executivo de utilizar formulações desenvolvidas por ela no lançamento de seis produtos de higiene bucal.
De acordo com a publicação, a Suavetex afirma que as formulações foram compartilhadas com a Cimed para viabilizar o registro dos produtos na Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa).

articles.title: Highland Brewing Celebrates 30 Years of Cold Mountain with a Weekend of Festivities
articles.titleKo: Highland Brewing Celebrates 30 Years of Cold Mountain with a Weekend of Festivities
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Milestone celebration features beer dinner with James Beard-winning chef Taylor Montgomery, rare anniversary beers, live music and five days of Cold Mountain. Highland Brewing’s Cold Mountain is not just a seasonal winter ale—it’s an Asheville holiday tradition that attracts thousands of beer lovers each year. November 12-16, Asheville’s original craft brewery celebrates 30 years of Cold Mountain Winter Ale with new and limited anniversary beers, a culinary collaboration with one of the South’s most celebrated chefs, the opening of Oscar’s Pizza, and five days of music and festivities. Cold Mountain Winter Ale is a 5.9% ABV spiced winter ale, with notes of vanilla, hazelnut, dark fruit and cinnamon. More than just a beer, its release has become a yearly tradition that marks the unofficial start of the holiday season in Western North Carolina. “Cold Mountain’s 30-year history is incredible to consider,” said Leah Wong Ashburn, President and CEO of Highland Brewing. “The release weekend brings people back to Highland year after year to mark the start of the holiday season and the beer brings them home to be with family and friends. Dad started this brewery with a commitment to great beer and community, so the way Highland fans celebrate and share Cold Mountain is special. Credit for the magic belongs to our inspiring Highland team. Cold Mountain the beer and Cold Mountain the weekend deliver on tradition and new experiences every year.” This year, Cold Mountain Winter Ale returns in bottles and on draft, with the original and three spin-offs featured in a special 30th Anniversary Variety Pack of 16-ounce cans: Cold Mountain Winter Ale, returning Coconut Cold Mountain, and two new releases: Chocolate Orange Cold Mountain, which pairs rich chocolate with bright citrus notes; and Pumpkin Spice Latte Cold Mountain, featuring notes of cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, cloves and coffee. The three spin-offs are also available in four-packs of 16-ounce cans. The commemorative packaging features an original illustrated design inspired by Nova, a gray wolf at Asheville’s WNC Nature Center, one of Highland’s Thirst for Good community partners, along with special 30th anniversary bottle crowns. Taproom-only versions of Cold Mountain Winter Ale on draft include Chai, Sour Cherry, Apple Cider Donut and Imperial Cold Mountain. Two limited barrel-aged releases will also be available on draft and in 500 mL bottles: Barrel-Aged Cold Mountain (11% ABV) and the first-ever bottled Double Barrel-Aged Bourbon Pecan Cold Mountain (13% ABV). Guests attending Friday and Saturday also have the chance to sample a super-limited Triple Barrel-Aged Cold Mountain, non-carbonated and tapped directly from the barrel. Don’t miss your chance to enjoy Cold Mountain Winter Ale among friends during Highland Brewing’s annual Cold Mountain event! Here’s what to expect: Thursday, Nov. 12: 7th Annual Cold Mountain Beer Dinner (SOLD OUT): The festivities begin with Highland’s 7th Annual Cold Mountain Beer Dinner from 5-9 p.m. on Nov. 12! Chef Taylor Montgomery of Montgomery Sky Farm , the 2026 James Beard Award winner for Best Chef: Southeast, will curate a multi-course dinner paired with Cold Mountain releases and specialty offerings. Friday, Nov. 13: Live Music: Grab your favorite 2026 version of Cold Mountain Winter Ale and join Highland Brewing for a full day of live music from noon to 11 p.m. Groove to the funky-but-chic sounds of Pleasure Chest , dance along with high-energy Ska City , stomp your boots to the twangy, genre-bending country music of Heavenly Vipers and experience the psychedelic adventure-rock and jam-fusion sounds of New Dawn Starkestra . Beyond the live music, Friday’s festivities include a Cold Mountain Heritage Panel featuring Leah Ashburn, Nikki Mitchell, Jamie Rowe and Joshua Jiles celebrating three decades of the iconic winter ale,

articles.title: Fenabrave prevê aumento de 12,8% na venda de veículos novos em 2026
articles.titleKo: Fenabrave prevê aumento de 12,8% na venda de veículos novos em 2026
articles.originalSummary: A Federação Nacional da Distribuição de Veículos Automotores (Fenabrave) aumentou a projeção de crescimento para as vendas de veículos novos em 2026 de 8,6% para 12,8%. A expectativa foi divulgada nesta quarta-feira, 4, com os dados de emplacamentos de veículos novos no País em outubro. A previsão é de que o setor, como um todo, deve vender quase 5,6 milhões de unidades no ano. Entre janeiro e outubro, foram emplacadas 4.722.650 unidades, o que já representa um crescimento de 12,62% sobre igual período de 2025. De acordo com a Fenabrave, este foi o segundo maior resultado acumulado da série histórica, atrás apenas do registrado em 2011. “Os resultados acumulados permitem uma avaliação mais favorável para o fechamento do ano, principalmente entre automóveis e comerciais leves. Ao mesmo tempo, continuamos projetando retração para caminhões e ônibus, ainda que menores que as estimadas em julho, mas abaixo do que prevíamos em janeiro”, disse Arcelio Junior, presidente da Fenabrave. Para a federação, o resultado mostra que o mercado brasileiro mantém ritmo consistente de crescimento, ainda que com ajustes pontuais. “Observamos uma recuperação gradual em segmentos como caminhões, ônibus e implementos rodoviários, cuja queda acentuada vem retrocedendo ao longo dos meses, notadamente, após a implantação do Programa Move Brasil”, acrescentou Arcelio Junior. Queda em outubro As vendas desses veículos tiveram queda de 4,06% em outubro, na comparação com setembro, segundo o balanço. Em relação a outubro de 2025, também houve retração, de 0,85%. A Fenabrave avalia que a retração de outubro foi influenciada pelo calendário, já que outubro do ano passado teve 23 dias úteis, enquanto neste ano foram 21. O total de 489.119 emplacamentos no mês passado inclui automóveis, veículos comerciais leves (picapes e furgões), ônibus, caminhões, motos e implementos rodoviários, como reboques e carrocerias. Veículos elétricos Um fator que tem contribuído para o bom desempenho no ano é a venda dos veículos eletrificados, que apresentaram crescimento superior a 130% no acumulado do ano, com 524.766 unidades emplacadas. Isso considera tanto os modelos híbridos quanto os totalmente elétricos. Considerando-se apenas automóveis e veículos comerciais leves, a participação dos eletrificados praticamente dobrou no país: atualmente, eles já representam 20,54% dos emplacamentos no Brasil, diz a Fenabrave. No ano passado, isso correspondia a 10,67%. Desempenho por segmentos O segmento de automóveis e comerciais leves continua tendo um bom crescimento no ano, informou a Fenabrave. No acumulado do ano, o crescimento foi de 17,29%, com 2.410.505 unidades emplacadas. Considerando-se apenas o mês de outubro, houve queda de 5,48% em relação a setembro e crescimento de 2,5% ante outubro do ano passado. Quanto aos segmentos de caminhões e ônibus, a queda persiste, apesar de alguma recuperação no ano. No acumulado do ano, o recuo foi de 4,18%, enquanto, em setembro, a queda foi de 8,36%. Em relação a outubro de 2025, as vendas caíram 10,26%. Já as motocicletas cresceram 8,90% no ano, com 1.985.816 unidades emplacadas, maior volume acumulado de sua série histórica. “A motocicleta atende tanto às necessidades de mobilidade individual quanto às atividades profissionais, especialmente nas cidades. Essa diversidade de utilização contribui para manter a demanda elevada, ainda que com pequenos ajustes pontuais de um mês para o outro, como os que ocorreram em outubro, em função do menor número de dias úteis em relação a outubro do ano passado”, afirma Arcelio Junior. Com informações de Agência Brasil. Imagem: Shutterstock O post Fenabrave prevê aumento de 12,8% na venda de veículos novos em 2026 apareceu primeiro em Mercado&Consumo .

Bikky, the customer data platform built exclusively for multi-unit restaurants, announced its partnership with Sonny’s BBQ. Known for expertly crafted, authentic barbecue, Sonny’s is working with Bikky to better understand guest behavior, evaluate menu performance, and drive more personalized marketing. Sonny’s opened its first barbecue restaurant in 1968, serving slow-smoked meats rooted in southern tradition. Today, the brand operates 90 restaurants across eight Southeastern states, combining casual dining with the convenience of a drive-through. Before Bikky, Sonny’s had limited visibility into the people behind their sales transactions. “We knew what was selling, but not who was buying it,” said Katelyn Moré, Director of Marketing. “We were able to see sales traffic and the number of items sold, but we couldn’t get to the guest behavior underneath.” That gap became more apparent as Sonny’s focused on growing their share of younger guests. “We had three defined personas to go after,” said Katie Love, Chief Marketing Officer. “We spent a lot of time and money on demographic research but had no idea if we were gaining any traction.” With Bikky, Sonny’s can see the impact of their marketing initiatives on different demographics. When Sonny’s rolled out a seasonal menu expecting it to appeal to a younger audience, the data showed the opposite. Seasonal innovation performed better with the brand’s core audience, while an $11.99 bowl promo was bringing in younger guests. “We had just always assumed that younger guests wanted new flavors and seasonal trends,” said Moré. “Now we know price point is the lever that’s actually driving younger customers versus the LTOs we were running.” Bikky AI turns Sonny’s data into action, working directly from the brand’s own sales, menu, and guest data to dig into complex questions without manual reporting. “I am in the chat all day long. I use Bikky as my source of truth and it’s a good pulse check against our internal reporting.” said Moré. Katelyn uses Bikky AI for location-level analysis and year-over-year holiday comparisons that previously took hours. “Being able to look at Labor Day over Labor Day last year through Bikky is so seamless,” said Moré. “Prior to Bikky, I’d have to pull four sets of data to compare that.” Sonny’s is also catching menu wins earlier. When its smoked wings began gaining traction during a recent promotion, Bikky AI Recommendations flagged the trend within days. “That’s something I wouldn’t have realized until month-end,” said Love. “When you have that information 3 days into a promotion, you can adjust the rest of the campaign while it’s still running.” Looking ahead, Sonny’s plans to expand its use of guest data throughout the organization. The brand and its agency partner are using Bikky to rethink loyalty tiers ahead of a new website launch. “We can see that our highest-tier guests aren’t coming to us for discounts,” said Moré. “Instead, we can offer them rewards and experiences that feel more valuable.” Data from Bikky will also inform the November Feast menu, custom dashboards for franchisees, and more tailored communications across media, SMS, and email. “Bikky has been a huge unlock for us. We’re equipped with much better data, and it’s finally telling the story versus us having to fill in the gaps,” said Love. “The Sonny’s team is one of the best we have worked with. articles.title: Construção defende período de transição de 5 anos para acabar com jornada 6×1
articles.titleKo: Construção defende período de transição de 5 anos para acabar com jornada 6×1
articles.originalSummary: A Câmara Brasileira da Indústria da Construção (CBIC) entregou ao Ministério do Trabalho um documento composto por 11 pleitos para amenizar os efeitos da mudança na jornada de trabalho com o fim da escala 6×1. Segundo a CBIC, a principal reivindicação é a ampliação do período de transição para cinco anos, permitindo que as empresas reorganizem suas operações, renegociem contratos e invistam em qualificação profissional e inovação tecnológica. Outro ponto é a definição de um divisor nacional para o cálculo do valor da hora trabalhada. A CBIC propõe a adoção de divisores de 255 horas para jornadas de 42 horas semanais e de 243 horas para jornadas de 40 horas, ambas na escala 5×2. Segundo a entidade empresarial, a medida busca estabelecer critérios uniformes e evitar interpretações divergentes que possam gerar insegurança jurídica e aumento dos encargos trabalhistas. A entidade também propõe que a regulamentação reconheça expressamente a possibilidade de distribuir a jornada de 42 horas semanais em cinco dias, com carga diária de 8 horas e 24 minutos, sem que os 24 minutos excedentes à oitava hora sejam considerados horas extras. O pleito prevê ainda que a adequação da jornada possa ser estabelecida por meio de acordos ou convenções coletivas, garantindo maior segurança jurídica a ambas as partes. Entre as reivindicações está ainda a criação de regras específicas de compensação de jornada para a construção civil, considerando as particularidades dos canteiros, sujeitos a condições climáticas, paralisações técnicas e diferentes etapas de execução. A CBIC defende mecanismos negociáveis de compensação semanal e mensal, além de sistemas de banco de horas compatíveis com a dinâmica do setor. O documento também propõe critérios claros para o descanso semanal remunerado, a fim de garantir previsibilidade na organização das equipes. Em relação aos feriados, a entidade pede que a coincidência com dias de descanso não gere automaticamente folgas adicionais, créditos em banco de horas ou pagamentos em dobro. A entidade também defende a criação de parâmetros nacionais uniformes para a regulamentação, evitando que questões como divisores salariais, compensações e descanso semanal sejam submetidas a interpretações distintas em cada região do País. Por fim, a CBIC propõe ajustes nas regras de transição do Bolsa Família , permitindo que beneficiários ingressem ou retornem ao mercado formal sem perda imediata do auxílio. A medida busca ampliar a oferta de trabalhadores e estimular a formalização, preservando a proteção social durante esse processo. Na quarta-feira, 4, uma comitiva da CBIC liderada pelo presidente Eduardo Aroeira Almeida se reuniu em Brasília com o ministro do Trabalho e Emprego, Luiz Marinho. A principal preocupação da CBIC está relacionada à dificuldade de adaptação de um setor intensivo em mão de obra, que já enfrenta escassez de trabalhadores. Pelas contagens da entidade, a redução da jornada poderá representar a perda de quase 600 milhões de horas de trabalho por ano, exigindo a contratação de aproximadamente 300 mil novos profissionais para manter a atual capacidade produtiva. Segundo a associação empresarial, a elevação prevista dos custos de mão de obra gira entre 10% e 15%. A construção civil tem, hoje, um recorde de pessoas empregadas no setor, com 3,150 milhões de trabalhadores com carteira assinada no País, aumento de 3% em relação a igual mês de 2025. O número é o mais alto desde o início da pesquisa do novo Cadastro Geral de Empregados e Desempregados (Caged), iniciada em janeiro de 2020, conforme dados compilados pela CBIC. Nos primeiros oito meses de 2026, a construção criou 200,4 mil novos empregos. Com o mercado de trabalho aquecido na construção, o salário médio para quem está ingressando no setor é de R$ 2.642,46, mantendo-se acima da média nacional dos salários de entrada, que é de R$ 2.410,74. articles.title: Havan inaugura megaloja de número 200 com fachada comemorativa em Roraima
articles.titleKo: Havan inaugura megaloja de número 200 com fachada comemorativa em Roraima
articles.originalSummary: A Havan prepara uma fachada especial para celebrar a inauguração de sua megaloja de número 200, marcada para sábado, 14 de novembro, em Boa Vista (RR). A unidade terá uma logomarca comemorativa e marcará um novo capítulo na expansão da varejista, que completa 40 anos em 2026. A escolha de Boa Vista representa também a chegada da empresa a mais um Estado brasileiro. Roraima ainda não contava com uma megaloja da Havan, que se aproxima do objetivo de estar presente em todo o País. O Ceará será o próximo destino, com uma unidade prevista para Fortaleza a partir de 12 de dezembro. “Chegar à megaloja de número 200 justamente no ano em que completamos 40 anos é a realização de um sonho construído com muito trabalho, coragem e dedicação. Queremos que essa conquista fique marcada na memória dos brasileiros e que todos se lembrem de que, juntos, alcançamos uma meta histórica. Inaugurar essa loja em Boa Vista, levando a Havan a mais um Estado, torna tudo ainda mais especial”, afirma o dono da Havan, Luciano Hang . A nova loja será a mais distante da matriz da Havan, em Brusque (SC), e do Centro de Distribuição Havan (CDH), em Barra Velha (SC). A operação logística para transportar a Estátua da Liberdade, símbolo da varejista, percorreu cerca de seis mil quilômetros entre Camboriú (SC) e Boa Vista. O transporte levou 15 dias pelas rodovias e outros oito dias de balsa, tornando-se a maior operação logística já realizada pela Havan para transportar uma Estátua da Liberdade. articles.title: Oxxo aposta em mídia exterior com tecnologia 3D e integração à paisagem urbana
articles.titleKo: Oxxo aposta em mídia exterior com tecnologia 3D e integração à paisagem urbana
articles.originalSummary: A rede de lojas de proximidade Oxxo apostou em uma ação de mídia exterior que combina tecnologia e criatividade para ampliar a visibilidade de suas ofertas em Santos, no litoral de São Paulo. Desenvolvido pela Chicooh+, OOH Tech especializada em mídia exterior, em parceria com a Agência Mestiça, o projeto reúne diferentes formatos de OOH e DOOH, com destaque para uma banca digital que exibe conteúdo 3D anamórfico. Com exibição realizada pela I Mídia Painéis Publicitários Ltda. ME, a iniciativa explora novas possibilidades de comunicação na paisagem urbana e incorpora o conceito de mídia regenerativa, que propõe uma atuação da publicidade exterior para além da veiculação de mensagens comerciais. “A mídia exterior faz parte da paisagem das cidades e tem potencial para construir relações mais interessantes com os espaços e as pessoas que circulam por eles. A banca é um exemplo de como podemos pensar a comunicação para além da mensagem publicitária, considerando também a presença visual do ativo e sua relação com o entorno”, afirma Chico Preto, CEO da Chicooh+. Instalada em meio à vegetação, a banca digital chama a atenção para a presença da publicidade no cotidiano da cidade. A proposta também busca explorar como o mobiliário urbano pode contribuir para uma experiência visual que vá além da exposição de ofertas. A estratégia inclui bancas, painéis digitais e totens em formatos estáticos e digitais, distribuindo a comunicação por diferentes pontos de circulação de Santos. Parte do conteúdo exibido na banca foi produzida pela Bridge Content e utiliza o recurso 3D anamórfico para criar uma sensação de profundidade e ampliar o impacto visual da peça. A tecnologia permite explorar as características da tela e transformar o próprio suporte em parte da ideia criativa. Dessa forma, a comunicação do Oxxo combina recursos digitais e presença física no ambiente urbano para chamar a atenção de quem circula pelo entorno. articles.title: Receita apreende 15 toneladas de produtos irregulares no Porto do Rio
articles.titleKo: Receita apreende 15 toneladas de produtos irregulares no Porto do Rio
articles.originalSummary: A Receita Federal apreendeu, nesta quarta-feira, 4, contêiner com aproximadamente 15 toneladas de mercadorias irregulares no Porto do Rio de Janeiro. A carga, proveniente da China, continha cerca de 243 mil itens e foi avaliada em R$ 3,6 milhões. Durante a fiscalização, a mercadoria foi inicialmente declarada como guarda-chuvas, produtos de baixo valor comercial. No entanto, a verificação física realizada pelos servidores da Receita Federal revelou a presença de cosméticos importados sem a devida anuência da Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa), além de produtos com indícios de fraude de marcas regularmente registradas no Brasil. A apreensão integra as ações da Operação Fronteira Receita Federal 2026, iniciativa de vigilância e repressão em rotas utilizadas para a prática de ilícitos como contrabando, descaminho e tráfico de drogas, armas, fauna e flora. A ação reúne órgãos de segurança pública, fiscalização e defesa, promovendo o compartilhamento de inteligência e a atuação integrada no combate ao crime organizado. Ao impedir a entrada de produtos irregulares no mercado nacional, a Receita Federal contribui para a proteção da saúde e da segurança dos consumidores, para a defesa da propriedade intelectual e para a promoção de um ambiente de concorrência leal entre as empresas que atuam regularmente no País. Anvisa interdita terminal no Porto de Santos Nesta terça-feira, 3, a Anvisa determinou a interdição parcial do Brasil Terminal Portuário (BTP), no Porto de Santos, em São Paulo. A decisão foi tomada após uma fiscalização de rotina identificar irregularidades sanitárias durante uma análise de risco. A resolução da Gerência-Geral de Portos, Aeroportos, Fronteiras e Recintos Alfandegados da agência está publicada no Diário Oficial da União. A fiscalização constatou a ausência de área reservada ao armazenamento de produtos com suspeita de comprometimento da qualidade ou interditados pelas autoridades sanitárias. O espaço, de acordo com a regulamentação, deve atender a requisitos específicos de conservação e controle de temperatura. A inspeção também identificou a falta de áreas separadas, trancadas e de acesso restrito para a guarda de substâncias e medicamentos sujeitos a controle especial, em diferentes condições de temperatura, como exige a legislação sanitária. Com informações de Agência Brasil. Imagem: Tânia Rêgo/Agência Brasil O post Receita apreende 15 toneladas de produtos irregulares no Porto do Rio apareceu primeiro em Mercado&Consumo .

A carga, proveniente da China, continha cerca de 243 mil itens e foi avaliada em R$ 3,6 milhões.
Durante a fiscalização, a mercadoria foi inicialmente declarada como guarda-chuvas, produtos de baixo valor comercial.

articles.title: Someburros Celebrates 40 Years with Anniversary Fiesta in Scottsdale
articles.titleKo: Someburros Celebrates 40 Years with Anniversary Fiesta in Scottsdale
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Someburros, the locally owned and family-operated Mexican restaurant group that has been serving Arizona since 1986, is celebrating 40 years of family, flavor and tradition with its 40th Anniversary Fiesta on Saturday, November 14, 2026, from 3 to 9 p.m. at Salt River Fields at Talking Stick in Scottsdale. The Fiesta celebrates four decades of bringing people together over homemade Sonoran-style Mexican food and honors the guests, employees, partners and communities who made Someburros a local favorite. With tickets starting at $10, guests can enjoy live music, food and family-friendly activities, and Someburros hopes to welcome thousands of Arizonans. “Reaching 40 years is an incredible milestone for our family, and we wouldn’t be here without the support of the Arizona community,” said Tim Vasquez, Owner and President of Someburros. “What started with our family’s recipes and a passion for bringing people together has grown into something much bigger than a restaurant. This Fiesta is our way of saying thank you to the guests who have supported us, the team members who bring our traditions to life every day, and the communities that have welcomed us into their neighborhoods. We look forward to celebrating this special milestone with everyone.” A Fiesta Four Decades in the Making The Someburros 40th Anniversary Fiesta will feature a variety of entertainment and activities for guests of all ages, including: Live Entertainment: Enjoy performances by Rock Lobster and Selena The Show, along with DJs and performances from local communities. Food and Festive Flavors: Guests can purchase Someburros favorites and enjoy a variety of food options throughout the event. Someburros Cantina: Celebrate with refreshing beverages and festive drinks in a lively gathering space. Games and Raffles: Participate in games, raffles and opportunities to win prizes like a trip to Disneyland, Arizona Cardinals memorabilia, and much more. Kid Zone: A dedicated area featuring activities and entertainment for younger guests. Story Village: Explore 40 years of Someburros history, family recipes and the memories that have helped shape the Arizona-born brand. Spectacular Drone Show: End the evening with a dazzling drone show lighting up the Arizona sky, creating a memorable finale to Someburros’ 40th Anniversary Fiesta and celebrating four decades of family, flavor and community. The evening will also include a special Someburros presentation and thank-you celebration, recognizing the people and communities behind the company’s four decades of success. Tickets General admission tickets are $10, VIP tickets are $30, and children ages 5 and under receive free admission. VIP tickets include a bean and cheese mini burro, an exclusive tequila tasting, double raffle tickets and access to a private section with seating near the stage. Parking is free for ticketed guests. Supporting Rancho Feliz Proceeds from the Fiesta benefit Rancho Feliz, a nonprofit serving families in Agua Prieta, Mexico, through education, housing, social services and community programs. The partnership reflects Someburros’ commitment to giving back and making this milestone celebration meaningful beyond the event itself. Forty Years of Family, Flavor and Tradition Founded in Tempe in 1986, Someburros grew from the cherished recipes of family matriarch Nana Isabel Vasquez. Today, the company operates 19 locations across the Phoenix area and Flagstaff, and the Fiesta is a chance to both celebrate that legacy and welcome new guests into the Someburros familia. Tickets and event information are available at www.someburros.com/40thanniversary. The post Someburros Celebrates 40 Years with Anniversary Fiesta in Scottsdale appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Prince St. Pizza Teams Up with ‘NCIS: New York’ for Veterans Day Fundraiser
articles.titleKo: Prince St. Pizza Teams Up with ‘NCIS: New York’ for Veterans Day Fundraiser
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Prince St. Pizza, the New York City-born pizzeria known for its Sicilian-style square pies and signature pepperoni-loaded slices, is serving up a little extra appreciation this Veterans Day. On Nov. 11, the brand will donate 10% of in-store sales at participating locations to the American Red Cross Service to the Armed Forces program. Through a partnership with CBS’ “NCIS: NEW YORK”, the donation will be matched up to $10,000. Service to the Armed Forces provides critical support services to military members and their families, connecting loved ones during deployments and emergencies and providing care and comfort at military and veteran hospitals. Prince St. Pizza is also thanking those who served with a FREE slice of pizza at all of its locations on Veterans Day. Veterans and active-duty military can claim a slice at the counter by showing a valid military ID or proof of service.* “Prince St. Pizza has always been about bringing people together, and we’re glad to put that spirit behind a cause that matters so much,” said Lawrence Longo, CEO of Prince St. Pizza. “With the support of our guests and ‘NCIS: NEW YORK’, we can help the Red Cross continue supporting service members and their families every day, not just on Veterans Day.” Prince St. has made a habit of celebrity team-ups, and this one arrives as the recently launched drama continues to draw viewers. Cast members Devin Druid, Shane Harper and Jacqueline Byers will be at the Brooklyn location on Nov. 11, handing out slices to fans and veterans. “NCIS: NEW YORK has the privilege of telling stories about people who serve, and now on Veterans Day our focus is to honor the real men and women who have served our country and the families who have supported them,” said Byron Balasco, executive producer and showrunner of NCIS: NEW YORK. “We’re proud to join Prince St. Pizza and the American Red Cross in saying thank you and showing our appreciation.” “I’m so grateful that NCIS: NEW YORK and Prince St. Pizza are joining forces to honor and celebrate military service members and veterans this Veterans Day”, said Joshua Cain, Division Director of the American Red Cross Service to the Armed Forces. “As a veteran myself, I am inspired by their support and collaboration.” Founded in Manhattan’s Nolita neighborhood over a decade ago, Prince St. Pizza has become a national destination for its crave-worthy square pies, now served at over 20 locations across the U.S. and Canada. For more information, visit princestreetpizza.com . *Offer available for any slice. One slice per person. Must show valid proof of service. articles.title: Crisp & Green Opens in Chaska, Minnesota
articles.titleKo: Crisp & Green Opens in Chaska, Minnesota
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . CRISP & GREEN, a fast-casual dining destination known for its convenient, chef-crafted and health-focused menu, today announced it is continuing its strong momentum in Minnesota with the opening of a new restaurant in Chaska. The location marks the brand’s 23rd in Minnesota, where the brand got its start almost 10 years ago. The Chaska opening reinforces CRISP & GREEN’s response to increasing demand for convenient, better-for-you dining and the brand’s continued momentum as it grows nationwide. “Minnesota is where CRISP & GREEN started, and nearly a decade later, it continues to be one of our greatest opportunities for growth,” said Steele Smiley, Founder and Executive Chairman of CRISP & GREEN. “As we quickly approach the milestone of 100 restaurants nationwide, opening our 23rd location in our home state is especially meaningful. It’s a reflection of how far we’ve come, the strength of the communities that have supported us, and the tremendous opportunity we see ahead as we continue building CRISP & GREEN into a nationally recognized brand.” CRISP & GREEN’s Chaska location is operated by franchise partner M3 Holdings, a seasoned multi-brand operator with expertise in the restaurant and wellness sectors, including ownership of multiple Planet Fitness locations. Since joining CRISP & GREEN in 2023, M3 Holdings has expanded the brand throughout Minnesota, Iowa and Ohio. By the end of 2026, M3 will own 9 locations with several in the pipeline opening as soon as Q1 in 2027. This growth helps to accelerate CRISP & GREEN’s broader system momentum, reinforcing how corporate and franchise development works hand-in-hand to bring the brand’s vision to life nationwide. “Continuing to invest in Twin Cities communities is a priority for our group, and Chaska felt like a natural next step in our growth,” said Alex Mortensen, President of M3 Holdings. “We believe making healthy food more accessible makes healthy choices easier. Our vision is for CRISP & GREEN to become a convenient part of people’s everyday lives, whether they’re commuting to work, taking their kids to practice, or simply looking for a fresh, nutritious meal on the go.” CRISP & GREEN expansion activities are underpinned by a unique model that balances corporate-owned restaurants with a growing roster of franchise partners, ensuring consistency in execution while scaling quickly to meet demand. Since its founding in 2016, CRISP & GREEN has carved out a distinctive niche in the healthy fast-casual space, blending chef-crafted convenience with a commitment to wellbeing. From grain bowls, salads, wraps, sandwiches, smoothies and more, every menu item is designed to energize every lifestyle. More than just a restaurant, CRISP & GREEN has become a wellness hub where guests gather to fuel body and mind. To celebrate the Chaska opening, CRISP & GREEN is offering a Grand Opening Free Food event from 10:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. on Friday, November 6, where guests can enjoy a complimentary salad, grain bowl or wrap. Recipients must download the CRISP & GREEN app and scan their CRISP Rewards account at checkout to receive their free entree [one per guest]. As part of its mission to empower healthier communities, CRISP & GREEN will also host a free Wellness Series event on Saturday, November 7, at 9:00 a.m. Attendees will meet at the restaurant for a group workout led by local CRISP Fit Coach Bailey Braccini. The first 50 attendees will receive exclusive CRISP & GREEN merch and wellness gifts from best-in-class brands like Lululemon, Isopure, Olipop, and more and the opportunity to enter to win a Peloton bike! Reserve your spot now by visiting crispandgreen.com/events. The event will be followed by CRISP & GREEN food sampling and premium wellness brand activations at the restaurant. Located at 122 Pioneer Trail, the Chaska CRISP & GREEN will be open daily from 10:30 a.m.

Döner Haus, the German-style Döner concept bringing one of Europe’s favorite street foods to the U.S., is opening its first Long Island location in Wantagh on Friday, Nov. 13. Located at 3336 Jerusalem Ave., the new restaurant will serve the brand’s signature Döner Sandwiches, Döner Wraps and Döner Boxes, loaded with freshly sliced, filler-free, 100% Zabiha Halal meats, fresh vegetables and creamy garlic sauce. The formula is simple: do one thing and do it right. In this case, make a Döner you’ll have dreams about. The Wantagh restaurant is owned and operated by franchise partner Hamza Jalili, marking his second Döner Haus following the opening of his Bayside location in Queens. A third restaurant in Garden City Park is expected in the coming months. Long Island, consider this the start of a very tasty habit. “We’re proud to bring some German flair to Long Island and show the community what makes Döner Haus special: We do one thing and we do it right.,” said Hamza Jalili, owner of Döner Haus Wantagh. “We’ve seen guests in Bayside come in curious and return as regulars, so we’re excited to see that same energy in Wantagh.” THIS IS HOW WE DÖNER Döner Haus started with a craving that wouldn’t quit. After moving to New York, German-born founder Nikolaus von Solodkoff missed the Döner Kebabs he grew up eating, so he stopped looking and started building, founding Döner Haus in New York City in 2023. Beginning in the East Village and opening to franchising opportunities the following year, Nikolaus set out to bring this crave-worthy concept across the U.S. With roots in Germany’s Turkish immigrant communities, German-style Döner brings together meat cooked on a vertical rotisserie, Turkish bread, fresh vegetables and plenty of sauce. In Germany, it’s an everyday favorite for lunch breaks, dinner on the go and the inevitable late-night craving. Döner Haus is here to make it just as much of a habit in the U.S. No passport required. YOUR DÖNER. YOUR BUSINESS Guests can choose chicken, beef or a mix of both, tucked into a crispy Turkish pide pocket. The Döner Sandwich and Döner Wrap come with red cabbage, lettuce, tomatoes, onions and signature garlic sauce. Prefer a fork? Döner Boxes offer a choice of fries, rice or salad, from a loaded comfort-food fix to a lighter, protein-packed lunch, with every meal delivering 53 grams of protein. While others continue to add to their menus, Döner Haus keeps things simple with an easy-to-navigate menu that makes ordering a breeze, even at midnight. Your call. Nein regrets. GOOD DÖNER GETS AROUND With more than 50 franchise commitments nationwide, Döner Haus is giving the usual lunch order some competition. Its expansion is backed by efficient kitchens and a proprietary operating platform connecting ordering, inventory, reporting and franchisee support. AI-powered tools help answer customer calls and turn daily operating data into practical guidance, giving franchise partners more time to focus on food and service. The next big thing in fast-casual is just getting started. For more information, visit doner.haus. For the latest openings, updates and a little giggle, follow the brand on Instagram at @realdonerhaus and TikTok at @realdonerhaus. Like the brand and want in? For franchising information, visit www.doner.haus/franchising. The post Döner Haus to Open First Long Island Location appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: The Salty Partners with Táche to Bring Pistachio Milk to Menus Nationwide
articles.titleKo: The Salty Partners with Táche to Bring Pistachio Milk to Menus Nationwide
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The Salty x Táche limited time menu will be available Available Nov. 13–22 at all Salty locations. The Salty, a national modern donut and coffee brand founded by Amanda Pizarro with more than 20 locations across the U.S., has announced a partnership with Táche, the original pistachio milk founded by Roxana Saidi. Launching at all Salty locations on Friday, Nov. 13, the partnership’s limited-edition fall drink offerings coincide with The Salty’s addition of Táche as a plant-based milk offering on its permanent, year-round menu. “I reached out to Táche because I loved the product and felt an immediate connection to what they were building,” said Amanda Pizarro, founder and chief brand officer of The Salty. “As a fellow founder, I really respect the care they put into their ingredients and the way they’ve built the brand. We’re obsessive about what goes into our coffee at The Salty, so bringing Táche behind our bar felt like a natural fit. And instead of simply adding a new milk, we wanted to make a little more of it, with a full menu and experience to celebrate.” Available Nov. 13–22 at all Salty locations, The Salty x Táche limited time menu will feature two specialty items, including: Pistachio Orgeat Latte ($8): Available as an espresso or matcha latte, the drink features house-made pistachio and orgeat syrup and Táche Original Barista Pistachio Milk topped with pistachio and vanilla swirled whip and pistachio crunch. Pistachio Tres Leches Donut ($5.25): The Salty’s signature 24-hour brioche donut soaked in Táche Original Barista Pistachio Milk, bottom dipped in pistachio white chocolate and topped with torched vanilla bean meringue and caramelized pistachios. To celebrate the launch, The Salty’s Georgetown location in Washington D.C. will host a one-day pop-up on Saturday, Nov. 7 giving guests early access to the limited time Táche menu and exclusive co-branded merch. On Friday, Nov. 13 through Sunday, Nov. 15, the first 10 guests to order the Táche drink and donut pairing at every Salty location will receive an exclusive key chain or bandana gift with their purchase. Táche will be available to order year-round at all Salty locations. “The Salty has built something really special by bringing creativity and an extraordinary level of care to both its coffee and culinary offerings,” said Roxana Saidi, founder and CEO of Táche. “We’ve long believed pistachio milk deserves a place behind the bar alongside the very best ingredients, and this partnership is such a natural expression of that. We’re thrilled to bring Táche to The Salty’s cafés nationwide, kicking things off with a deliciously creative menu that celebrates everything pistachio has to offer.” Known today for its signature 24-hour brioche donuts, meticulously sourced coffee program and warm hospitality, The Salty was founded by Amanda Pizarro in 2015 with a Miami pop-up in a vintage camper. The brand has since grown to more than 20 locations across eight states and recently developed a line of bottled, clean-label coffee syrups. A trendsetter, The Salty has partnered with likeminded brands including Poppi, Snif, Summer Fridays and Salt & Straw for thoughtful guest activations anchored in community connection and attention to craft. For more information about The Salty and its limited time Táche menu offerings, visit saltydonut.com. articles.title: Slice House by Tony Gemignani to Open in Tracy, California
articles.titleKo: Slice House by Tony Gemignani to Open in Tracy, California
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Slice House by Tony Gemignani, the highly successful fast-casual pizza franchise by world renowned pizzaiolo Tony Gemignani, is proud to announce the November 2026 opening of its newest Northern California location in Tracy. Located at 2050 Ellis Town Drive in Ellis Village Town Center, the pizzeria will continue the brand’s expansion throughout the region, bringing Gemignani’s award-winning pizza to San Joaquin County and offering a welcoming, community-focused dining destination for local residents and visitors. The new restaurant is currently hiring across all positions and is expected to bring around 25 full- and part-time jobs to the community. “Every new Slice House is an opportunity to introduce more people to the pizza styles and techniques that have shaped my career,” said Founder Tony Gemignani. “Ratika and Ranjan know our brand and share our commitment to quality, and it’s exciting to continue growing alongside partners who believe in what we’re building. We’re looking forward to bringing that same experience to Tracy.” Franchised and operated by Ratika Tyagi and Ranjan Bhasin, longtime Slice House partners with multiple locations across California, Slice House Tracy marks the latest expansion for the experienced franchise partners, whose existing portfolio includes Slice House locations in Livermore, Castro Valley, Walnut Creek, San Leandro, and Milpitas. The new pizzeria will feature an expansive menu of Gemignani’s acclaimed New York, Sicilian, Grandma, and Detroit-style pizzas, available by the slice or whole pizza. The menu will also include fresh wings, salads, and options for gluten-free, vegan, and vegetarian diners. The beverage menu will consist of craft beers and premium wines, in addition to non-alcoholic sodas and juices. Slice House Tracy will have indoor seating for 16 people, outdoor patio seating for 38 people and will offer takeout, online ordering, and delivery. It will be open seven days a week – from 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. Sunday through Thursday and 11 a.m. to 10 p.m. on Friday and Saturday. “It’s been incredibly rewarding to grow alongside Slice House and see the enthusiasm for Tony’s award-winning pizza firsthand,” said Tyagi. “We’re excited to bring that same experience to Tracy and become part of the vibrant Ellis Village community. Whether it’s a quick lunch, family pizza night, or a casual dinner with friends, we look forward to offering locals a new go-to spot for great food and a welcoming atmosphere.” Slice House Tracy will open in Ellis Village Town Center, a neighborhood shopping destination in Tracy’s Ellis community. The center features a growing mix of retailers, restaurants, and everyday conveniences, including Sprouts Farmers Market, Chipotle, BMO Bank, Great Clips, Pokemoto, and Wingstop. Situated near established and developing residential neighborhoods, including Waterstone Apartments and the surrounding Ellis community, the restaurant is conveniently located for local families, residents, and professionals seeking a casual dining option close to home. The location is also within easy reach of nearby schools, parks, and community amenities, including Anthony Traina Elementary School, Tracy Hills Park, and Dr. Powers Park. With Tracy’s growing residential population and its position as a connection point between the Bay Area and Central Valley, Slice House is poised to become a go-to destination for everything from family dinners and casual lunches to takeout and group gatherings. Opening in November 2026, Slice House Tracy will host an exciting grand opening event, the details of which will be shared over the coming weeks. For more information, visit www.slicehouse.com and follow along on Instagram @SliceHouse and @SliceHouse.PizzaCraft. Members can enjoy a range of options, including national favorites like Wingstop, Chipotle, and Sweetgreen, regional options like Aga’s Restaurant in Houston and Papalote Mexican Grill in San Francisco, and a variety of small business restaurants in their own backyard. Whether it’s ordering takeout from Uber Eats or tackling a weekly grocery list for the week ahead, Prime members can do it all on Amazon. Currito, the fast-casual concept fueling communities through its globally inspired bowls, salads, and smoothies, is thrilled to announce the grand opening of its second restaurant in Louisville. The restaurant, located in the Paddock Shops shopping complex at 4037 Summit Plaza Dr., opens its doors on Monday, November 9th, marking the newest restaurant for franchisee Rudrik Patel. To celebrate, the first 50 guests through the door on opening day will receive free Currito for a year, redeemable for one meal per week through the Currito app. Soft Opening/VIP Parties: Thursday, November 5: 11am – 1pm and 5:30pm – 7:30pm Friday, November 6: 11am – 1pm and 5:30pm – 7:30pm Saturday, November 7: 11am – 2pm To keep the celebration safe and fair for everyone, overnight camping is not permitted, and guests may begin lining up no earlier than 6 a.m. ET on opening day. A Family Affair Brings Currito to Paddock Shops Rudrik’s connection to Currito is a family affair. His uncle, Peter Patel, owns and operates the brand’s successful St. Matthews location in Louisville, where Rudrik was first introduced to the concept. After seeing the restaurant’s success firsthand and developing an appreciation for the brand, he recognized an opportunity to build on Currito’s momentum in Louisville by opening the brand’s second location in the market. Entrepreneurship runs in Rudrik’s family, and the new restaurant marks his fifth business venture. Based in nearby Bardstown, he has leaned on his uncle Peter as an invaluable resource throughout the process of opening his first Currito location. His cousin will also join the team, further extending the family’s involvement with the brand. Community excitement is already building ahead of the grand opening, with the new location receiving an overwhelmingly positive response. “I first tried Currito while visiting my uncle’s restaurant, and I was hooked from the first bite. My go-to is always the build-your-own bowl,” said Rudrik. “Seeing how much he’s built and how much our family and community have embraced the brand made this an easy decision. I’m excited to bring that same experience to Paddock Shops and to have my cousin join me on this journey.” A Growing Presence in Louisville This opening in the Paddock Shops reflects Currito’s growing momentum in the Louisville market. The St. Matthews location has become one of the brand’s standout performers since opening, giving Rudrik a firsthand look at what a successful Currito restaurant can achieve before he decided to become a franchisee himself. “Our St. Matthews location has exceeded what we hoped for, and it’s been amazing to watch this community embrace the brand,” said Kyle Gardner, Brand Managing Partner for Currito. “Louisville has shown us there’s real demand for what Currito offers, and I think Rudrik is going to see that same success.” Currito is part of the Cincinnati-based Thunderdome Restaurant Group, which owns The Eagle, a concept with two Louisville locations of its own. That local experience means the team behind Currito already knows what it takes to successfully open and operate a restaurant in the market. Currito Continues to Grow Its Kentucky Footprint “Rudrik represents exactly what we look for in a Currito franchisee: someone who genuinely loves the food and understands what it takes to run a great restaurant,” said John Lanni, co-founder of Currito. “It’s especially meaningful to see the brand grow through family, with Rudrik following in his uncle’s footsteps to bring Currito to Paddock Shops.” Founded in 2005 by brothers Joe and John Lanni, Currito was created to bring fresh, globally inspired meals to the fast-casual space. articles.title: Biggby Coffee Announces Holiday Menu
articles.titleKo: Biggby Coffee Announces Holiday Menu
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . BIGGBY COFFEE, the 470-plus-unit high-energy coffee franchise, is getting into the holiday spirit with a seasonal menu filled with peppermint, frosted sugar cookie and cranberry-raspberry flavors. Available Nov. 2 through Jan. 4, the lineup also includes returning food favorites, a new holiday treat and promotions designed to give guests more reasons to stop by throughout the season. Leading the holiday menu are the Peppermint Stick Mocha and Snow Mint Mocha, two seasonal favorites built around one of the most recognizable flavors of the season. Frosted Sugar Cookie also returns, along with a Kid’s Sprinkle Cookie drink for younger guests. For those looking for something beyond coffee, BIGGBY COFFEE is offering CranRazz Energy in both a BIGGBY Blast and Red Bull Mocktail. The holiday lineup extends to food, with the Maple Waffle Sandwich returning for the season. The sandwich features a Belgian-style waffle made with real maple syrup and pearls of sugar, with several combinations of egg, cheddar, sausage and bacon available. Guests looking for something sweet can also pick up the Chocolate Holiday Cake Pop. BIGGBY COFFEE is making Mondays a little merrier throughout the season with More the Merri-Mint Mondays. Every Monday from Nov. 2 through Jan. 4, guests who purchase any size Peppermint Stick Mocha Latte or Snow Mint Mocha Latte can get $1 off any Bragel or Maple Waffle Sandwich. The weekly offer gives peppermint fans another reason to make BIGGBY COFFEE part of their holiday routine. The holiday calendar will also include several limited-time promotions: Veterans Day: Veterans and active-duty military members can receive a free 16-ounce hot or iced brewed coffee. Through the offer, BIGGBY COFFEE is thanking those who have served while continuing to build relationships in the communities its stores serve. Thanksgiving: At participating stores that are open on Thanksgiving, customers can receive a buy-one-get-one-free 20- or 24-ounce specialty beverage, making it easy to pick up a favorite drink for themselves and share one with someone else. Check your local BIGGBY for hours of operation! Black Friday: During the first 60 minutes after stores open, customers can receive a free 16-ounce hot or iced black coffee with the purchase of a Bragel or Maple Waffle Sandwich. Christmas Eve: Last-minute shoppers can fuel up before finishing their holiday errands with a choice between a buy-one-get-one offer and $1 off any 20- or 24-ounce specialty beverage. For anyone still checking names off their shopping list, BIGGBY gift cards offer an easy holiday gift for teachers, coworkers, employees, friends and family. Available in physical and digital formats, gift cards give recipients the chance to pick their own BIGGBY favorite. From peppermint mochas and Frosted Sugar Cookie drinks to quick stops during holiday shopping and coffee shared with family and friends, BIGGBY COFFEE is giving guests plenty of ways to celebrate the season. This holiday season, MilkShake Factory, the neighborhood dessert destination known for its handspun milkshakes and premium, small-batch chocolates, is welcoming back the Peppermint Brownie Fudge Shake, available beginning November 9, 2026. As holiday traditions make their return, this seasonal favorite gives guests another sweet way to celebrate. Part refreshing, part decadent, the Peppermint Brownie Fudge Shake pairs cool, crunchy peppermint with oven-baked brownies and warm fudge. Priced at $10.95, the seasonal favorite is back to satisfy holiday cravings for something rich, chocolatey, and sweet. “Some flavors just taste like the holidays, and the combination of peppermint and chocolate is one of them,” said Dana Edwards Manatos, Founder and CEO of MilkShake Factory. “Over the years, we’ve loved seeing our seasonal treats become something guests look forward to. What began with handcrafted chocolates and classic soda fountain treats has evolved into a menu of signature handspun milkshakes, housemade sundaes, dairy-free options, and premium chocolates, with seasonal creations offering guests something new to enjoy throughout the year. articles.titleKo: CAVA’s Growth Story Keeps Building
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . CAVA's same-store sales rose 3.1 percent in Q3. The typical CAVA restaurant is now doing more than $3 million in annual sales, a figure that would have seemed ambitious just a few years ago. And as the Mediterranean fast casual pushes deeper into the country, it is finding that customers in smaller markets and lower-income communities are just as receptive to the brand as those in its established territories. That consistency is helping CAVA maintain its expansion trajectory despite an unpredictable consumer environment that disrupted traffic during the third quarter. The chain reached 500 restaurants during the period, achieving the milestone ahead of schedule on its journey toward at least 1,000 locations by 2032. It opened 24 net new restaurants, bringing its footprint to 30 states and Washington, D.C., and increasing its restaurant count 20.5 percent year over year. Revenue climbed 22.1 percent to $353.7 million, and same-restaurant sales increased 3.1 percent, driven primarily by menu pricing and product mix. Guest traffic was slightly positive. READ MORE : The People Plan Fueling CAVA’s Expansion CAVA Sees More Room to Run as Restaurant Volumes Climb CAVA Sees Massive Runway as Mediterranean Cuisine Goes Mainstream CFO Tricia Tolivar says the results demonstrated CAVA’s ability to maintain momentum despite pressures affecting the industry. The quarter began with consumer concerns surrounding Cyclospora and fresh produce consumption, which reduced CAVA’s same-restaurant sales by an estimated 150 basis points. The food safety issues were not directly connected to the chain, but they temporarily affected customer behavior across the category. Higher gasoline prices created another obstacle following Labor Day, contributing to uneven traffic patterns before conditions improved toward the end of September. CAVA did not introduce additional promotions or make significant changes to its operations in response to the produce concerns. Tolivar says customers gradually returned as the initial uncertainty faded. “Food safety is always a very high priority for us, and we continue to to focus on that as we always have,” Tolivar says. “There wasn’t anything specifically that we did or shifted to address the concerns.” The recovery continued into October, giving CAVA confidence to increase its full-year same-restaurant sales guidance to 6–7 percent. The company also expects 76–78 net new restaurants in 2026. One of the more notable developments is where CAVA is finding its strongest sales growth. Restaurants in markets with lower median household incomes continue to outperform the rest of the system on comparable sales, driven by transaction growth and customer demand for premium proteins. The results challenge assumptions that consumers facing greater financial pressure would gravitate exclusively toward the least expensive menu items. CAVA offers an entry-level meal priced around $10.65 at many locations, allowing customers to choose chicken, falafel, or roasted vegetables, along with unlimited toppings, three dips and spreads, and two dressings. Customers can also upgrade to higher-priced proteins. Tolivar says that flexibility has helped CAVA reach a diverse customer base without resorting to aggressive discounts. “Since 2020, we had significantly underpriced CPI inflation, as well as food away from home and food at home, to create an increasingly strong value proposition for our guests, so that they can access our food and enjoy it, and really have that experience of great flavors and great tastes that make you feel good while you’re eating it, and after,” she says. The company is also seeing little evidence of customers systematically trading down across its menu. articles.titleKo: Wendy’s Rejects $1.4 Billion Takeover Bid, Adopts Poison Pill
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Wendy's five-part comeback strategy focuses on menu quality and value, marketing, restaurant operations, digital engagement, and restaurant-level growth and profitability. Wendy’s announced Thursday that it rejected a proposal from an investor group led by billionaire Nelson Peltz’s Trian Fund Management and adopted a shareholder rights plan, otherwise known as a poison pill, to protect itself from a hostile takeover. An independent committee of its board unanimously rejected the $7.35-per-share cash offer from Trian, Flynn Group, BlueFive Capital, and Sixth Street Partners. The proposal, which valued Wendy’s equity at approximately $1.4 billion, sought to acquire all outstanding shares not already owned by the investor group. After reviewing the proposal with its financial and legal advisors, the committee concluded that the offer substantially undervalued Wendy’s and failed to reflect the company’s long-term earnings potential. “The Independent Committee thoroughly evaluated this Proposal and unanimously concluded that it substantially undervalues Wendy’s standalone prospects and long-term earnings potential,” Art Winkleblack, chairman of Wendy’s board and a member of the independent committee, said in a statement. “Our confidence rests firmly in [CEO] Bob Wright’s proven track record of seasoned industry leadership, including restaurant business turnarounds. We believe in Bob and his executive team’s ability to execute on the plan they recently presented to our franchisees at the 2026 Wendy’s convention.” The rejection comes shortly after the investor group submitted its nonbinding proposal, which represented an approximately 20 percent premium to Wendy’s stock price before the offer. Trian and related parties own approximately 16.3 percent of Wendy’s, while Flynn Group operates more than 340 Wendy’s restaurants. Meanwhile, the shareholder rights plan is designed to make it harder for an investor to take control of Wendy’s without paying shareholders a fair price. The brand said it adopted the measure partly because the investor group refused to agree to restrictions that would have limited its ability to pursue a takeover. The company is instead backing its newly announced Dave’s Way turnaround strategy, introduced alongside its Q3 earnings results. Led by Wright, the five-part strategy focuses on menu quality and value, marketing, restaurant operations, digital engagement, and restaurant-level growth and profitability. Wendy’s has also established a Strategic Activation Office to coordinate implementation across the franchise system. Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs are serving as financial advisors to the independent committee, while Simpson Thacher & Bartlett is providing legal counsel. Kirkland & Ellis is advising Wendy’s. The decision follows a similar move by Dine Brands , parent of Applebee’s, IHOP, and Fuzzy’s Taco Shop, which recently rejected a $39-per-share takeover proposal from Arkhouse Management and Cobblers Cove Capital. Dine also adopted a shareholder rights plan after determining that the offer substantially undervalued the company. Angry Crab Shack operates 28 restaurants across the U.S. and U.K. Alaska’s snow crab supply is tightening again, and that’s creating another challenge for seafood restaurants already navigating unpredictable costs and availability. The state’s snow crab quota for the 2026–27 season dropped roughly 45 percent, from 9.3 million pounds to 5.1 million pounds. Meanwhile, increased quotas for Tanner and red king crab are giving operators alternatives as they evaluate purchasing decisions and menu pricing. Angry Crab Shack, which operates 28 restaurants across the U.S. and U.K., has been preparing for these fluctuations by expanding its sourcing relationships, securing longer-term purchasing agreements, and offering alternative crab varieties. The company has also kept its seafood boil prices unchanged for the past 18 months despite volatility in the market. FSR magazine spoke with Angry Crab Shack president and CFO Andy Diamond about navigating seafood shortages, protecting franchisee profitability, maintaining value for customers, and preparing for continued uncertainty in 2027. 1. Alaska’s snow crab quota has dropped roughly 45 percent this season. What does that reduction mean for Angry Crab Shack, and how are you preparing for potential supply shortages and price increases? Though numbers for snow crab look different in Alaska this upcoming season, it’s not entirely unexpected as numerous closures have affected the fisheries since 2021. In 2022, for instance, Bering Sea snow crabs were designated as “overfished,” prompting a two-year closure for the fishery. Though now reopened, the shifts in Alaska’s snow crab fisheries led Angry Crab Shack to turn to fisheries in Newfoundland, Canada, which operate under an entirely different fishing season from Alaska, beginning in April instead of October. In 2026, the Canadian fisheries caught 61,000 tons, or 134 million pounds of snow crab, which helped Angry Crab Shack secure a consistent supply and lock in prices until February 2027. The quota was reduced 3 percent from 2025 and if in April, the Newfoundland snow crab fisheries’ quotas go down, I think there will be enough snow crab, plus the increased availability of Tanner [crab], to meet our demand, provided you’re giving yourself options and you’re planning ahead. 2. How has Angry Crab Shack’s seafood sourcing strategy evolved in recent years as crab availability and pricing have become more unpredictable? What role are direct supplier relationships and longer-term purchasing agreements playing in protecting the business? In the past, we approved all purchases of volatile seafood items, but over the past few years Angry Crab Shack has taken control over procurement of shrimp, snow crab, and king crab. We now handle all supplier contact, process all bids from suppliers, and have more control over pricing for all markets. We are still able to control overall pricing by utilizing master sales agreements (MSAs) with the firm’s main supplier and distributor, Houston, Texas based wholesale distributor Sysco. It’s a benefit we pass on to our potential franchise partners. When buying a franchise, you’re simply not purchasing the name, the recipes and operational system, you’re buying down your risk by benefiting from the purchasing power of a national brand verses a single unit restaurant. 3. Sam Fox’s name is synonymous with excellence in the restaurant world. The acclaimed entrepreneur went from a college dropout to opening nearly 200 restaurants across the country over the past three decades. Having been nominated for more than a dozen James Beard Awards, Fox built and sold one of the country’s most admired culinary portfolios through Fox Restaurant Concepts (FRC), creating more than 20 brands like True Food Kitchen, The Henry, Flower Child, and North Italia. He sold FRC to The Cheesecake Factory in October 2019 for $353 million , when the group had almost 50 restaurants across eight states. Since then, FRC has grown to 13 concepts with more than 100 locations nationwide, plus 52 North Italia locations. Now, seven years after selling his company, Fox officially announced he was stepping away from FRC on Thursday. His last day was October 30. “It’s hard to sell your business and be partners with the people you sell your business to for this long,” he admits, adding that his departure was the result of a gradual, year-by-year transition rather than a fixed timetable set at the sale. As the business grew, the company built a transition team to manage its next stage, and he and the ownership discussed his timing over the past year. Though the transition was planned and agreed upon years in advance, it marks an important milestone for the restaurateur and his career path as he turns his full attention to the luxury lifestyle hotel and independent restaurant realm. “The timing coincides with the success of the hotel and some of the growth I want to do outside of Fox Restaurants,” he notes. “We’re really excited for the future, for what’s ahead for FRC, and equally, if not even more excited for what our new organization is going to do.” In 2021, Sam Fox opened The Twelve Thirty Club—a multi-level dining and entertainment destination inspired by the supper clubs of the Prohibition era—in partnership with celebrity Justin Timberlake in Nashville, Tennessee. Fox created Author & Edit Hospitality in 2021 with the debut opening of The Twelve Thirty Club—a multi-level dining and entertainment destination inspired by the supper clubs of the Prohibition era—in partnership with celebrity Justin Timberlake in Nashville, Tennessee. He then created his first hotel, The Global Ambassador in Phoenix , in December 2023. “Opening The Global Ambassador put me in a world I had never been in before. After spending my entire career in restaurants, suddenly I was a first-time hotelier, earning a MICHELIN Key in our first year and every year since. And I loved it,” Fox notes. “It reminded me how much I still have to learn and how much more there is to create. In a lot of ways, I feel like I’m starting all over again, only this time with nearly 30 years of experience behind me. And that’s what makes it so exciting.” His shift into the hotel side of hospitality stemmed from his past frustrating experience opening a restaurant inside a hotel, where third-party operators worked to operate the various parts from the restaurants to the valet and spa. “I looked around and everyone was working in different silos, and it was really draining and taxing on the guests and really not great for employees either. articles.title: Pague Menos amplia lucro em 19,5% no 3T26; vendas digitais crescem 32,8%
articles.titleKo: Pague Menos amplia lucro em 19,5% no 3T26; vendas digitais crescem 32,8%
articles.originalSummary: A Pague Menos ( PGMN3 ) registrou lucro líquido ajustado de R$ 96,3 milhões no terceiro trimestre de 2026, crescimento de 19,5% em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado. O resultado , divulgado ao mercado nesta quarta-feira, 4, foi favorecido pelo controle de despesas, pela melhora da margem bruta e pela redução dos custos financeiros. A companhia também registrou avanço de 32,8% nas vendas digitais, que contribuíram para sustentar o crescimento da operação em um cenário de desaceleração do mercado farmacêutico. A receita bruta somou R$ 4,429 bilhões, alta de 6,9% na comparação anual. Embora positiva, a expansão ficou abaixo dos 9,3% registrados no segundo trimestre e dos 14,4% do primeiro trimestre de 2026. A companhia atribui a perda de ritmo principalmente às bases de comparação mais elevadas, especialmente dos medicamentos GLP-1, que impulsionaram as vendas ao longo de 2025. O Ebitda ajustado atingiu R$ 278,8 milhões, crescimento de 7,2% em relação ao terceiro trimestre do ano passado. A margem Ebitda permaneceu em 6,3%, enquanto a margem líquida ajustada avançou de 1,9% para 2,2%. No acumulado dos nove primeiros meses de 2026, a receita bruta chegou a R$ 12,916 bilhões, alta de 10%, enquanto o lucro líquido ajustado somou R$ 225,5 milhões, avanço de 46,5%. Controle de despesas e menor custo financeiro sustentam lucro A melhora do resultado da Pague Menos ocorreu mesmo diante de um crescimento mais moderado das vendas. Um dos fatores foi a expansão da margem bruta, que passou de 29,9% para 30% na comparação anual, o maior patamar para um terceiro trimestre desde 2018. O lucro bruto somou R$ 1,327 bilhão, crescimento de 7,2%. Segundo a companhia, o desempenho reflete melhorias nas condições comerciais, especialmente nas categorias de medicamentos genéricos e GLP-1, além de ganhos tributários relacionados ao novo centro de distribuição na Paraíba. A empresa também destacou a manutenção das perdas de estoque em níveis reduzidos, resultado associado à maior eficiência na gestão de mercadorias, com utilização crescente de ferramentas de inteligência artificial. As despesas gerais e administrativas totalizaram R$ 102,8 milhões, redução de 3,3% em relação ao mesmo trimestre de 2025. A queda foi explicada principalmente por menores provisões para remuneração variável e planos de ações restritas. Já as despesas com vendas cresceram 8,5%, chegando a R$ 946 milhões, pressionadas por custos relacionados à operação do novo centro de distribuição, à expansão da rede e a ajustes no quadro de funcionários. O resultado financeiro também contribuiu para a melhora do lucro. As despesas financeiras líquidas diminuíram 13%, passando de R$ 129,6 milhões para R$ 112,7 milhões. A redução foi favorecida por menores custos com antecipações de recebíveis e pela queda do CDI médio no período. Digital cresce 32,8% e amplia participação nas vendas A estratégia digital permaneceu como uma das principais frentes de crescimento da Pague Menos no terceiro trimestre. As vendas realizadas pelos canais digitais somaram aproximadamente R$ 1,1 bilhão, alta de 32,8% em relação ao mesmo período de 2025. Com isso, a participação desses canais na receita bruta passou de 19,8% para 24,6% em um ano, avanço de 4,8 pontos porcentuais. O crescimento foi impulsionado principalmente pelo aplicativo da companhia, cujas vendas aumentaram 73,2% na comparação anual. O canal concentra cerca de dois terços das vendas de e-commerce da rede. Nos últimos 12 meses, a Pague Menos registrou crescimento de 23% no número de usuários ativos mensais do aplicativo, além de 3,4 milhões de downloads. A companhia também ampliou a base de consumidores que utilizam mais de um canal de compra. Os clientes omnicanal passaram a representar 14,5% da base, crescimento de 2,9 pontos porcentuais em relação ao terceiro trimestre de 2025. Embora representem uma parcela menor do total de consumidores, esses clientes respondem por aproximadamente 40% das vendas da Pague Menos e apresentam gasto médio 3
koreanSummary: A Pague Menos ( PGMN3 ) registrou lucro líquido ajustado de R$ 96,3 milhões no terceiro trimestre de 2026, crescimento de 19,5% em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado.
O resultado , divulgado ao mercado nesta quarta-feira, 4, foi favorecido pelo controle de despesas, pela melhora da margem bruta e pela redução dos custos financeiros.
A companhia também registrou avanço de 32,8% nas vendas digitais, que contribuíram para sustentar o crescimento da operação em um cenário de desaceleração do mercado farmacêutico.

articles.title: “O plano cabe no bolso da companhia”, diz Caito Maia sobre reestruturação da Chilli Beans
articles.titleKo: “O plano cabe no bolso da companhia”, diz Caito Maia sobre reestruturação da Chilli Beans
articles.originalSummary: Caito Maia, CEO e fundador da Chilli Beans, publicou um vídeo nas redes sociais para comentar o plano de recuperação extrajudicial da companhia e esclarecer as diferenças em relação à recuperação judicial. Segundo o executivo, o procedimento representa um acordo negociado com os credores e aprovado por eles, com condições de pagamento adequadas à capacidade financeira da empresa. A empresa vai renegociar uma dívida financeira de R$ 340 milhões e prevê receber um aporte de até R$ 50 milhões para financiar a reestruturação e sustentar os próximos passos de crescimento. O plano prevê novos prazos e condições para o pagamento das dívidas com instituições financeiras. Segundo a empresa, fornecedores, funcionários e outros parceiros não estão incluídos na negociação. Maia afirmou que as negociações ocorreram de forma sigilosa durante meses e que a conclusão dessa etapa permite à companhia organizar um fluxo de caixa compatível com seu faturamento e suas possibilidades de pagamento. “A gente fez um plano que vai acontecer, que cabe no bolso da companhia”, disse. O executivo também destacou que o protocolo do plano foi motivo de comemoração interna, por representar um avanço na construção de uma estrutura financeira viável. Na recuperação extrajudicial, a empresa negocia diretamente com seus credores um plano de reestruturação, que pode ser submetido à homologação judicial, conforme os requisitos legais. No vídeo, Caito Maia reafirmou que permanece à frente da Chilli Beans como CEO e mencionou a atuação de André Dela Togna como co-CEO, responsável por comandar as frentes financeira e de reestruturação da empresa. Segundo ele, as mudanças internas começaram há cerca de dois meses e já apresentam resultados positivos. O empresário também aproveitou o vídeo para alertar outros empreendedores sobre a importância de agir rapidamente diante de dificuldades financeiras, especialmente na revisão de despesas e na redução de custos. “Não demorem para tomar decisões, não demorem para diminuir custos, porque isso pode ser fatal. Cada dia que você demora pode ser fatal”, afirmou. Apesar do momento de reorganização financeira, Maia demonstrou otimismo em relação ao futuro da marca e mencionou os preparativos para a comemoração dos 30 anos da Chilli Beans, em 2027.
